summary: Waluigi has pieced together what happened at the ruined manor from multiple sources of varying reliability, and what Waluigi has assembled is either a pivotal moment in the current crisis or the most elaborate series of coincidences and exaggerations Waluigi has ever encountered. According to reports, Agent L discovered a broken teleportation circle and obtained testimony from a murdered spirit containing coordinates in the Thornwood and allegations about false coronations. Then ghosts appeared—the number varies between twenty and forty depending on who Waluigi asks—and everyone fled. Archie allegedly fell forty feet from a window, woke up in an Iron Legion hospital surrounded by corpses, was offered ritual components by the Mole, escaped through disguise, and returned to find the Regency attempting to arrest Luigi on charges that include withholding Mario's location and 'residual Mr. L activities.' A fight broke out. Archie became an impromptu judge. Luigi fled before verdict. And somehow three hostile factions agreed to form an alliance called the Cells of the Third Eye. Waluigi notes that Archie is the primary source for much of this account, and Archie has demonstrated a flexible relationship with objective truth. WAH.
description:
Waluigi must be honest about the limitations of this entry. Unlike events Waluigi witnessed personally or documented through multiple independent sources, the ruined manor convergence comes primarily from participants whose accounts Waluigi cannot fully verify. Archie Miser provided the most detailed testimony, but Archie is a man who once convinced a tribunal he acted in 'justifiable magical defense' after killing someone in a public market. His version of events may be accurate. His version of events may also be carefully constructed to present himself in the best possible light. Waluigi has attempted to cross-reference where possible, but the chaotic nature of this event means that even honest witnesses might remember things differently than they occurred.

## What Waluigi Has Been Able to Confirm

Certain elements of this account are independently verified. The ruined manor exists—Waluigi has confirmed its location near the Thornwood through cartographic records. A teleportation circle was discovered there—multiple sources reference it, and Waluigi has obtained partial sketches of the geometric patterns. A warrant for Luigi's arrest was issued by Magistrate Toadsworth IV—Waluigi has seen copies of this document, and its authenticity appears genuine. An alliance calling itself the Cells of the Third Eye now operates in the region—Iron Legion intelligence confirms their existence, even if they dispute the organization's legitimacy. These facts form the skeleton of the account. Everything else is flesh that Waluigi has assembled from testimony, rumor, and educated guessing.

## The Circle and the Spirit — What Luigi Found

According to multiple sources, Agent L kicked aside a rug in the manor's central room and discovered the remnants of a teleportation circle etched in chalk and charcoal. The circle had been deliberately damaged—sections scratched out, connections severed—suggesting someone wanted to ensure it could never be used again. Or perhaps someone wanted it to APPEAR unusable while preserving its function for those who knew how to restore it. Waluigi cannot determine which interpretation is correct from available evidence.

More concerning is the spirit testimony that Luigi allegedly obtained before arriving at the manor. Waluigi has seen fragments of Luigi's notes—or documents claiming to be Luigi's notes—describing a communion with someone named Ashford. The spirit spoke of coordinates in the Thornwood, of documents 'sealed in iron' beneath a hanging tree, of coronations that were 'theater' while 'real power signed in blood not ink.' The spirit allegedly said the Crown's true heir 'walks among the Thornwood dead' and that the bloodline was 'broken at third branch.' If this testimony is authentic, it suggests the entire succession crisis is built on fundamental lies. If it is fabricated, someone went to considerable effort to create compelling disinformation.

Waluigi notes that Luigi's final recorded words from the spirit were 'trust no crowns.' Sound advice, perhaps, but also convenient phrasing for anyone wanting to undermine legitimate authority. Waluigi is uncertain whether to treat this testimony as revelation or propaganda.

## The Ghost Swarm — Numbers Vary Considerably

Everyone agrees that ghosts appeared in the lord's chamber. The number varies dramatically depending on the source. Archie's account mentions 'over forty,' which would represent an unprecedented concentration of spectral activity. Bones—who fled first and therefore saw the initial manifestation—estimates 'more than twenty, maybe thirty.' A Regency operative who arrived later heard it was 'a dozen or so' from secondary sources. Waluigi suspects the actual number was somewhere in the middle range, with witnesses inflating or deflating based on how brave or practical they wished to appear.

What matters more than the exact count is that everyone fled. Agent L reportedly said 'it's time' when the ghosts appeared, suggesting he intended to fight. Archie reportedly said 'we can take them,' demonstrating his characteristic overconfidence. But within minutes, Bones had jumped from a balcony, Archie was retreating toward the master bedroom, and Luigi was left alone with whatever number of ghosts actually manifested. Luigi's reported response to being abandoned—'I'm used to it'—has been confirmed by multiple sources and carries emotional weight that suggests authenticity. People do not typically fabricate phrases that make them sound pathetic.

## Archie's Hospital Account — The Most Questionable Section

This is where Waluigi's confidence in the narrative drops significantly. According to Archie, he fell approximately forty feet from a manor window, survived, woke up in Ironmend Bastion—the Iron Legion's premier medical facility—and discovered that everyone in his room had been murdered while he slept. The Mole was standing there smiling, offering him ritual components 'free of charge.' Archie refused, looted the corpses for supplies, disguised himself as a guard, and escaped the facility without being detected.

Waluigi has problems with this account. First, forty-foot falls are typically fatal or at minimum severely injurious. Archie claims he 'got lucky,' but luck of that magnitude strains credulity. Second, Ironmend Bastion is a heavily guarded facility—the idea that one man could disguise himself and walk out unchallenged suggests either exceptional skill or significant exaggeration. Third, the Mole killing an entire room of patients to offer Archie components is theatrical in a way that feels PERFORMED. Either the Mole operates according to a logic so alien that Waluigi cannot comprehend it, or Archie is embellishing what actually occurred.

Waluigi has attempted to verify the hospital massacre independently. Iron Legion sources confirm 'an incident' at Ironmend Bastion around the relevant timeframe, but details are classified. This could mean Archie's account is accurate and the Legion is covering up their security failure. It could also mean something different happened entirely and Archie constructed his narrative around a kernel of truth.

## The Warrant — This Document Waluigi Has Verified

Unlike the hospital account, the warrant for Luigi's arrest is documented and authentic. Waluigi has examined copies. The charges are real: Conspiracy to Withhold Material Information regarding Mario's location, Unauthorized Association with the Mages' Guild, Residual Mr. L Activities, and Obstruction of Ongoing Investigations. The probable cause section references 'one very talkative Boo informant'—which may be Waluigi's own source, suggesting that information Waluigi gathered has been used to build a case against Luigi. This is uncomfortable but not unexpected. Information flows in multiple directions.

What troubles Waluigi most is the authorization. The warrant was issued by Magistrate Toadsworth IV, who according to multiple sources 'usually doesn't do warrants' and 'is quiet unless it involves Peach.' Why would Toadsworth personally authorize this document? Why would Captain Toadette's name appear initially and then be crossed out for 'administrative error'? The Regency explanation is unsatisfying. Administrative errors do not typically result in Loyalist commanders being listed as authorizing officials on Regency warrants.

## The Interrogation — Archie as Judge

According to witnesses from multiple factions, Archie appointed himself magistrate in the middle of an active battlefield and proceeded to evaluate each charge against Luigi. Luigi's responses to the charges, as reported by witnesses, are revealing. On Mario's location, he allegedly said: 'He's fine. Better than fine. He's doing what heroes do when no one else can. I can't say more.' This is consistent with the Eastern Passage documentation Waluigi has compiled—Luigi knows something about Mario's situation and considers it necessary rather than concerning. On the Guild association, Luigi allegedly said: 'They pay well, okay? And after everything, I needed something to do.' The loneliness in that response matches what Waluigi has observed of Luigi's current state.

On the Mr. L charges, Luigi reportedly became agitated, claiming he 'wasn't himself' and that 'someone else was driving while I was screaming in the back seat.' When Archie allegedly asked if Luigi did something evil during that period, Luigi went silent. Multiple witnesses confirm the silence. Whatever happened during the Mr. L incident, Luigi cannot or will not deny it directly. Before Archie could render any verdict, Luigi slammed his Poltergust into the ground and fled. Multiple witnesses confirm this. Luigi chose escape over judgment.

## The Alliance — Cells of the Third Eye

The most improbable element of this entire account is that three hostile factions agreed to work together afterward. Iron Legion operatives who had just decapitated Regency Toads agreed to serve alongside surviving Regency representatives. Archie—a known quantity to the Legion, a stranger to the Regency—became nominal leader. The organization named itself the Cells of the Third Eye, suggesting aspirations toward hidden knowledge and surveillance.

The roster, as Waluigi has reconstructed it, includes a troubling concentration of Iron Legion personnel. Byscilla Danos, Aemenor Evenflight, Hargram Fidger, Darno Spriggon, Warol Creeton, Rhak the Lost, Thornbury, and Manderaz the Mad—all Legion affiliated. Against this, the Regency contributed only three representatives: Gregir Fendelsohn, Terenzio Cassalanter, and Nine-Fingers Keene. The Liberated Toads added Lucky T, Bones, and Archie himself. The balance of power within this 'alliance' is heavily skewed toward Legion interests. This cannot be coincidental.

## Waluigi's Theories and Extended Analysis

Waluigi has spent considerable time analyzing this event, and Waluigi has developed multiple theories about what actually occurred and what it means for the broader crisis. Waluigi presents these theories not as conclusions but as frameworks for understanding—each has supporting evidence and each has significant problems.

**Theory One: The Legion Orchestrated Everything**

The Iron Legion's presence at the manor was not coincidental. They arrived to 'protect' Archie at precisely the moment the Regency arrived to arrest Luigi. They had operatives in position. They knew where Archie was despite his escape from their own hospital. They brought enough personnel to dominate any resulting alliance. This suggests foreknowledge, planning, and strategic positioning that transforms the 'convergence' from chaotic accident to deliberate operation.

If the Legion orchestrated this event, their goals become clearer. They wanted Archie—a powerful fire mage with connections to the Raventree crisis—under their influence. They wanted Luigi discredited or driven underground, removing a potential ally from other factions. They wanted a cross-factional organization they could control from within while appearing to cooperate with enemies. The Cells of the Third Eye, under this theory, is a Legion front operation with Archie as an unwitting figurehead.

Supporting evidence: The Legion's dominant numbers in the alliance roster. Darno Spriggon's refusal to take orders from Archie—suggesting he answers to someone else. Byscilla's mysterious papers that influenced her decisions—possibly Legion intelligence briefings. The convenient timing of Legion arrival. Archie's presence in a Legion hospital before the convergence.

Problems with this theory: The Legion also suffered casualties during the fight. Thornbury took an arrow to the knee. If this was a planned operation, why allow their own people to be injured? Additionally, Archie's escape from Ironmend Bastion suggests the Legion did NOT have full control over his movements—unless the escape itself was permitted to establish Archie's sense of independence before drawing him back in.

Waluigi rates this theory as PLAUSIBLE but not confirmed.

**Theory Two: The Mole Is Running Everyone**

The Mole appears at critical moments throughout this crisis. The Mole appeared at the hospital offering Archie exactly what he needed. The Mole killed witnesses—the hospital patients—who might have complicated the narrative. The Mole operates according to patterns that no faction fully understands. What if the Mole is not serving any existing faction but rather manipulating ALL factions toward some independent goal?

Under this theory, the ruined manor convergence was engineered by the Mole to create chaos from which a new organization would emerge. The Mole ensured Archie survived the fall—perhaps through intervention Archie did not perceive. The Mole ensured Archie would return to the manor at the precise moment when factions were colliding. The Mole's offer of 'free' components was not generosity but investment—Archie's refusal does not matter if the Mole achieves their goals through other means.

Supporting evidence: The Mole's presence at the hospital is otherwise inexplicable. Why would the Mole be there? Why would the Mole kill those specific people? Why would the Mole offer help and accept refusal? These questions only make sense if the Mole's actual goal was accomplished regardless of Archie's response—perhaps simply ensuring Archie left the hospital and returned to the manor.

Problems with this theory: Waluigi has no evidence of the Mole's broader goals. This theory explains the Mole's behavior by assuming hidden purposes, which is circular reasoning. The Mole might simply be chaotic, opportunistic, or operating according to logic that appears purposeful but is actually random.

Waluigi rates this theory as POSSIBLE but highly speculative.

**Theory Three: Ashford's Testimony Is the Key**

What if the ruined manor convergence matters primarily because of what Luigi discovered, not because of the factional chaos that followed? Ashford's spirit provided coordinates, allegations about false coronations, claims that the true heir 'walks among the Thornwood dead.' If this testimony is accurate, someone powerful has reason to suppress it. The warrant for Luigi's arrest, the convergence of factions, the formation of a new alliance—all of this might be maneuvering around the REAL issue: what Ashford knew and who wants that knowledge controlled.

Under this theory, Toadsworth IV issued the warrant because he knows Ashford's testimony threatens the current power structure. The Regency wants Luigi arrested not for the stated charges but to interrogate him about what the spirit revealed. The Legion wants Archie controlled because Archie now travels with people who have access to that testimony. Everyone is reacting to Ashford, not to each other.

Supporting evidence: Toadsworth IV 'usually doesn't do warrants' but personally authorized this one. The warrant references the Star Fountain investigation and 'obstruction'—but what is being obstructed? The phrasing 'trust no crowns' directly challenges Regency legitimacy. If Ashford's claims about broken bloodlines and theatrical coronations are true, the entire Regency power structure is fraudulent.

Problems with this theory: Waluigi cannot verify that anyone besides Luigi actually knows what Ashford said. If the testimony is so dangerous, why hasn't Luigi been assassinated rather than warranted? A warrant creates legal process, witnesses, documentation. Assassination is cleaner. Unless someone wants Luigi alive for questioning—which supports this theory—or unless the warrant is cover for something else entirely.

Waluigi rates this theory as COMPELLING but requiring more evidence.

**Theory Four: Luigi Engineered His Own Escape**

This theory troubles Waluigi because it casts Luigi in a more calculating light than Waluigi has previously considered. What if Luigi WANTED to be confronted at the manor? What if the Poltergust escape was planned, not panicked? What if Luigi used the chaos to disappear while leaving others to deal with the consequences?

Consider: Luigi knew a warrant existed or would exist. He knew the Regency was looking for him. He knew the Iron Legion had interest in Archie. By positioning himself at the manor during a ghost crisis, he created conditions where multiple factions would collide. His 'escape' during the interrogation removed him from immediate custody while leaving Archie to form an alliance that would occupy both the Legion and the Regency. Luigi gets freedom to pursue whatever he's actually doing—possibly following Ashford's coordinates to the Thornwood—while his pursuers are distracted by a new organization that he is no longer part of.

Supporting evidence: Luigi's Poltergust is not typically an escape tool—it is designed for ghost capture. Using it to scatter everyone and flee suggests preparation, not panic. Luigi's phrase 'I'm used to it' when abandoned could be resignation OR could be performance—the appearance of the abandoned brother who is actually manipulating events. Luigi has survived things that should have killed him. He is not as helpless as he appears.

Problems with this theory: Waluigi has documented Luigi's emotional struggles extensively. The man Waluigi has observed seems genuinely lost, not cunningly strategic. This theory requires Luigi to be acting, which contradicts everything Waluigi thinks he knows about Luigi's character. Unless Waluigi has been fooled. Unless everyone has been fooled. Unless Luigi's apparent vulnerability is the most sophisticated deception of all.

Waluigi rates this theory as UNLIKELY but not impossible. Waluigi does not WANT this theory to be true because it would mean Waluigi has fundamentally misread Luigi's character.

**Theory Five: Coincidence and Chaos**

The simplest explanation: nothing was orchestrated. The Legion arrived because they were tracking Archie after his hospital escape. The Regency arrived because they had a warrant and intelligence about Luigi's location. The ghosts appeared because the manor is haunted and intruders triggered defensive manifestations. The alliance formed because desperate people in dangerous situations sometimes cooperate despite historical enmity. There is no grand plan. There is no hidden orchestrator. There is only chaos producing outcomes that APPEAR purposeful in retrospect.

Waluigi resists this theory because Waluigi has spent months documenting conspiracies, patterns, and hidden connections. If the ruined manor convergence is simply chaos, it suggests that other events Waluigi has analyzed might also be chaos. The assassination conspiracy, the Eastern Passage, the Star Fountain reunion—all of these might be random events that Waluigi has forced into narrative frameworks because Waluigi needs to believe that meaning exists.

This possibility frightens Waluigi more than any conspiracy theory. A world of deliberate evil can be fought. A world of random chaos can only be survived.

Waluigi rates this theory as TERRIFYING and refuses to think about it further.

**What Waluigi Actually Believes**

After extensive analysis, Waluigi's working hypothesis is a combination of theories. Waluigi believes the Iron Legion saw an opportunity and exploited it—they did not create the convergence, but they positioned themselves to benefit from it. Waluigi believes Ashford's testimony is significant and that multiple parties are maneuvering to control or suppress that information. Waluigi believes the Mole has purposes that no one understands, and that the hospital incident served those purposes in ways that are not yet apparent. Waluigi believes Luigi fled because he had no better options, not because he engineered the situation—but Waluigi acknowledges uncertainty about Luigi's true capabilities.

Waluigi believes the Cells of the Third Eye will collapse, probably violently, when the Iron Legion's patience with the pretense of cooperation expires. The numbers favor them. The positioning favors them. Archie's nominal leadership is exactly that—nominal. When the Legion decides they have extracted sufficient value from this arrangement, they will dispose of non-Legion members and claim whatever Archie has accomplished.

Waluigi believes Archie knows this, or suspects it, and is racing to accomplish his goals—reaching his friends on other planes—before the betrayal comes. The teleportation circle in the manor, the components the Mole offered, Byscilla's claimed expertise in planar travel—all of these point toward Archie's actual priority. He does not care about factional politics. He cares about rescue. The alliance is a tool, and he will discard it when it stops being useful.

This makes Archie either admirably focused or dangerously amoral. Waluigi suspects both.

**On Manderaz the Mad**

Waluigi must note that Manderaz the Mad is Iron Legion despite the name suggesting otherwise. The 'Mad' appellation apparently refers to combat behavior rather than political affiliation—Manderaz fights with a ferocity that other Legion operatives find excessive even by their standards. Including Manderaz in the alliance roster adds another Legion-loyal fighter to an already Legion-dominated group. Whether Manderaz's 'madness' makes them unpredictable even to Legion command is unknown. They might be a loose cannon that complicates Legion control. They might be exactly as controlled as every other Legion operative, with the 'mad' reputation serving as cover for calculated brutality.

Waluigi has not been able to interview Manderaz directly. Sources describe them as 'difficult to approach' and 'prone to violence when questioned.' This is either genuine instability or very effective deterrence against investigation. Waluigi will attempt contact through intermediaries if opportunity presents.

**On the Thornwood Coordinates**

Ashford's spirit provided specific coordinates: 47°N 23°W from castle ruins, beneath a hanging tree where the Toad Council fell. Waluigi has attempted to identify this location. Multiple castle ruins exist in the region. Multiple hanging trees have historical significance. The Toad Council's fall is documented—a massacre during the early civil war period—but the location of that massacre is disputed by different sources.

If Waluigi can identify the correct location, Waluigi might be able to retrieve the 'documents sealed in iron' that Ashford referenced. These documents allegedly prove that the current heir is illegitimate and that the coronation was theater. Such documents would be explosive. They would validate Loyalist claims while undermining Regency authority. They might also reveal information that neither faction wants public—the 'real power signed in blood not ink' suggests agreements that transcend the official conflict.

Waluigi intends to investigate these coordinates personally. This is dangerous. The Thornwood has a reputation for consuming those who enter unprepared. But Waluigi has spent months documenting others' discoveries. Perhaps it is time for Waluigi to make discoveries of his own.

**On Luigi's Silence**

The moment that haunts Waluigi most from this account is Luigi's silence when asked if Mr. L 'did something evil.' Multiple witnesses confirm the silence. Luigi—who defended himself on every other charge, who explained his Guild association, who insisted he 'wasn't himself' during the Mr. L period—could not or would not deny doing evil.

What did Mr. L do? The Mr. L incident is poorly documented in available sources. Waluigi knows it involved dimensional manipulation, possibly mind control, possibly collaboration with forces hostile to the Mushroom Kingdom. But specifics are classified, redacted, or simply not recorded. Luigi's silence suggests the truth is worse than rumor. If he could deny evil, he would have denied it. His silence is confession by omission.

This complicates Waluigi's understanding of Luigi considerably. Waluigi has portrayed Luigi as a sympathetic figure—the abandoned brother, the lonely ghost hunter, the man trying to do right in impossible circumstances. But sympathetic figures do not go silent when asked about evil. Sympathetic figures deny, explain, contextualize. Luigi did none of these things.

Waluigi does not know what to do with this information. Waluigi does not know if it changes the overall assessment of Luigi's character or if it reveals a single dark chapter in an otherwise decent person's life. Waluigi knows only that the silence happened, that it was witnessed, and that it means something Waluigi has not yet understood.

**Final Thoughts on the Convergence**

The ruined manor convergence was either a turning point or a footnote. Either the Cells of the Third Eye will accomplish something significant—retrieving Archie's friends, uncovering Ashford's documents, changing the balance of power—or they will collapse into mutual destruction and be remembered only as another failed alliance in a war filled with failed alliances.

Waluigi will continue monitoring this situation. Waluigi will attempt to verify Archie's more questionable claims. Waluigi will investigate the Thornwood coordinates if possible. Waluigi will track Luigi's movements if Luigi can be tracked.

And Waluigi will remember that in the middle of chaos, when asked to judge a man he barely knew on charges he could not fully evaluate, Archie Miser attempted something like fairness. He asked for Luigi's side. He listened to the responses. He was reaching a verdict—we will never know what verdict—before Luigi fled.

In a world where factions kill each other over decades-old grievances, where conspiracies nest inside conspiracies, where the truth is always obscured by layers of deception and counter-deception, one pyromaniac trying to be fair in a haunted manor might be the most hopeful thing Waluigi has documented.

Or it might be another performance, another manipulation, another lie dressed in the clothing of justice.

Waluigi does not know. Waluigi rarely knows. Waluigi documents anyway.

WAH.

## Prologue: What the Regency Already Knew Before Miller Boarded the Helicopter

Before the play-by-play begins, Waluigi needs to establish what was already in the Regency's possession when they designed Operation POP QUIZ. Because the operation did not happen in an intelligence vacuum. There was prior contact. There was prior documentation. There was an operative who got close enough to Baldi to observe his behavior, record his responses, and produce an account that the Regency cross-referenced against the POP QUIZ parameters in their internal filing system.

The diplomatic circuit account — assembled by an operative Waluigi will not name here because the operative is still active and naming them creates a target — describes an encounter with Baldi that preceded the extraction attempt by an indeterminate period. In fey-adjacent time and in the Post-Assassination Period's general temporal unreliability, 'preceded' is doing significant work, but Waluigi is confident the diplomatic circuit encounter came first because the account's operative was gathering intelligence for the archive analysis program that the encrypted archive lockout subsequently terminated.

What the diplomatic circuit account documented:

Baldi carries a leather-bound notebook. He closes it when he does not want its contents observed. The operative who got closest to reading the notebook described partial mathematical notation — sequences that looked like the encoded keys the Regency was trying to recover — before Baldi noticed and shut the cover with the specific deliberateness of someone protecting something valuable, not something private. He was not embarrassed by the notebook. He was managing access to it.

Baldi received a vial from Agent T during the diplomatic circuit. The vial contained a dark, viscous, self-motile substance. Baldi examined it. He said 'yeah.' He closed the notebook. He did not analyze the substance as an unknown — he recognized it. The operative documented this response and flagged it as significant.

The substance in the vial is analytically consistent with the substance that flows from Baldi's wounds when he is cut or shot. Waluigi established this through cross-reference after obtaining the extraction account. The diplomatic circuit operative flagged the substance as significant without knowing why. Waluigi now knows why. Baldi was not analyzing the vial's contents as a scientist examines an unknown compound. He was looking at a sample of his own material and confirming that it was his.

The diplomatic circuit account also documented Baldi's name recognition — he knew the operative's cover identity without introduction — and his spatial behavior: appearing simultaneously in locations that were not adjacent, moving between positions without visible transit. The operative noted this as anomalous without being able to explain it. Miller encountered the same behavior on entry: Baldi stunned on the lawn, Baldi already inside the hallway. The operative saw it first. The operative documented it. The Regency filed the document.

Waluigi wants to be very precise about what 'filed the document' means in this context. It means the Regency read the diplomatic circuit account. It means someone in the Regency's intelligence apparatus processed the information that Baldi recognizes people without introduction, that he moves between locations instantaneously, that he bleeds a self-motile dark substance that he can identify on sight, that he maintains a locked notebook containing what appear to be mathematical key sequences, and that conventional social or diplomatic engagement with him produces hollow responses that reveal nothing he has not decided to reveal. Someone read all of that. Someone cross-referenced it against the POP QUIZ parameters. And then someone sent Miller down a rope ladder with a flashbang and told him not to trigger an angry state.

*Waluigi has spent a significant amount of time sitting with this sequence. The diplomatic circuit operative got closer to understanding Baldi than anyone the Regency subsequently sent into the building. They observed him at rest — not in pursuit mode, not in correction mode, but in the social-diplomatic register where Baldi performs the role of a cooperative schoolteacher while managing access to his actual self with precise, practiced control. That operative produced an account. The Regency suppressed the relevant findings when designing POP QUIZ. Miller was not briefed on the dark fluid, the spatial anomalies, the notebook, the vial recognition, or any of the other intelligence that would have changed his tactical approach — or his decision to board the helicopter at all. The Regency chose the probe model over the intelligence model. The probe model costs operatives. The intelligence model costs time. The Regency preferred to spend Miller. WAH.*

Waluigi proceeds with the play-by-play, cross-referencing the diplomatic circuit account at each relevant point.

## The Briefing: What Miller Was Told and What Miller Was Not Told

Specialist 'Viper' Miller. Communications and Intel. Not the squad commander — the stealth element, the one who goes in while the others watch from above. This distinction matters because it means Miller was given the insertion role without the command-level intelligence that would have informed his risk assessment. He was told to go inside. He was not told what inside meant.

The briefing as reconstructed from Miller's initial radio chatter:

**Target:** Baldi. Schoolteacher. Located at his Schoolhouse.

**Objective:** Extract Baldi intact. Recover encoded mathematical sequences that act as keys to the Regency's encrypted archives.

**Rules of Engagement:** Capture intact. Do not trigger an 'angry' state.

**Squad composition:** Miller on insertion. Sergeant 'Brick' Stone on heavy weapons, staying in the helicopter for overwatch. Corporal 'Ghost' Reyes piloting and providing sniper overwatch.

**Extraction point:** Schoolhouse North Perimeter.

Waluigi needs to sit with the phrase 'do not trigger an angry state' for a moment, because that is not language used about a civilian target. That is language used about a weapon system with known behavioral parameters. The Regency understood that Baldi has operational states. They understood that one of those states is dangerous in a way that requires specific warning in a military briefing.

The diplomatic circuit account describes Baldi in his non-angry state — cooperative, socially fluent, performing the role of a helpful schoolteacher while maintaining precise control over what he reveals. The operative who documented that encounter noted that Baldi's cooperative state is itself a performance: meticulous, consistent, and calibrated to prevent the observer from understanding what they are observing. The 'angry state' referenced in Miller's briefing is the state where the performance ends. Where the schoolteacher stops pretending to be a schoolteacher.

*The Regency knew both states existed. The diplomatic circuit account documented the cooperative state in detail — the hollow 'yeah,' the closed notebook, the social deflections, the name recognition without introduction. The briefing's warning about the angry state confirms the Regency also had intelligence about what happens when the cooperative state terminates. You do not write 'do not trigger an angry state' as a hypothetical precaution. You write it because someone came back from a previous operation — or didn't come back — and the debrief included words that produced silence in the room. The Regency knew what both states looked like. They sent Miller into a building containing both and briefed him on neither. WAH.*

Brick's comment before insertion — 'If he starts swinging that ruler, this whole mission goes sideways' — indicates he had access to threat intelligence from previous operations that Miller did not receive. Brick knew about the ruler. The diplomatic circuit operative had also documented the ruler — the tapping, the rhythm, the way it changed pace when Baldi was processing versus pursuing. Brick's knowledge of the ruler means the heavy weapons operator, the person staying in the helicopter, had been briefed on an object that the diplomatic circuit account identified as a core behavioral indicator. The person going inside was briefed on none of this.

*The information gradient within the three-person squad is the most precise expression of the Regency's expendability calculus. Brick: knows about the ruler, stays outside. Ghost: knows about thermal anomalies, stays outside. Miller: knows 'do not trigger an angry state,' goes inside. The person who most needed the threat intelligence was given the least of it, because operatives who understand what they are walking into have a tendency to decline to walk into it. The compartmentalization was not operational security. It was mission assurance. Miller didn't know enough to refuse. WAH.*

## The Previous Insertions: What the Archive Knows and What It Will Not Say

Waluigi needs to address the previous failed insertions before the play-by-play begins, because they are the context in which Miller's operation took place and because the Regency's decision to send Miller was not made in an intelligence vacuum — it was made in full knowledge of what had happened to the people they sent before.

The micro-transmitter that Miller found in the ventilation shaft did not belong to him. It was embedded in the duct work — not dropped, not left by accident, but embedded, suggesting it had been there long enough to become integrated with the surrounding material. Its sonar pulse was still active when Miller touched it, which means it was still broadcasting, which means it had power, which means it had been maintained — by the building, or by the void, or by whoever had been carrying it when they entered the duct and had not left.

Things brought inside the building become part of the building's accounting. Miller's blood is in the building's vents. Waluigi does not know what that means for Miller's status in the void. He suspects it means the building knows where Miller is. WAH.*

Junction: left descends to basement. Right levels out toward administrative wing.

Miller went right.

Waluigi does not know what is in the basement of the Schoolhouse. The diplomatic circuit account does not document the basement — the operative's encounter remained on the ground floor and the cooperative state never produced an invitation to descend. Waluigi has one hypothesis, based on the cold blue thermal signature of the object Baldi carries and the void-adjacent materials analysis: the basement is where the building touches the void from below. The ground floor is the lesson. The basement is the answer. Miller went right, toward the administrative wing and the exit that opened on the void, which is the side-door to the answer. The basement is the direct entrance. Waluigi is not going near the basement.

## Phase Eleven: The Door That Opened on Zero

Miller charged for the exit. The hallway extended during his sprint — the distance to the door grew longer with each stride despite continuous forward motion. The floor was soft beneath the carpet. Flesh-like.

He reached the handle. Heaved.

Nothing.

No parking lot. No sky. A vast yawning emptiness. Pitch black. Air freezing, smelling of nothingness and old stagnant dust.

Baldi at the end of the hallway, not pursuing. Watching.

'You can't leave until you get it right.'

The sound came from behind Miller and from directly inside his ear simultaneously.

'The answer is zero.'

Waluigi needs to give this statement its full analytical treatment because it is the most important thing Baldi says during the entire operation and because the diplomatic circuit account provides context that makes it more interpretable than it appears in isolation.

The diplomatic circuit operative documented Baldi's relationship to mathematical correctness as absolute — not preferences, not standards, but a framework within which things are either correct or they are not, and incorrectness is not a matter of degree but a matter of category. Something is wrong or it is not. The lesson has a correct answer or it does not have one. Baldi teaching implies that the answer exists and can be reached.

'You can't leave until you get it right' means the lesson has a correct answer. It means the Schoolhouse is not an inescapable trap — it is an unsolved problem. Every operative who went in got the answer wrong. The lesson is still running because nobody has gotten it right yet. The Schoolhouse is not a prison. It is a classroom that has been in session since before the first probe, waiting for a student who can produce the correct answer.

'The answer is zero.' Zero is the additive identity — the number that, added to any value, leaves it unchanged. Zero is the boundary between positive and negative. Zero is the number that, multiplied by anything, produces itself. Zero is the point where the equation balances, where the variables on both sides collapse into equality. If the Schoolhouse exists at zero — at the boundary between the exterior world and the void, between positive and negative, between the classroom and the darkness — then zero is not an answer about nothing. Zero is an answer about balance. About the boundary itself.

*Waluigi's hypothesis: the correct answer to the lesson is not a number. It is not a formula. It is an understanding. The Schoolhouse is asking something about the nature of the boundary — about what zero means, about what exists at the point where positive becomes negative, about what the void is and what the classroom is and why they are separated and what would happen if they weren't. Every operative who went in tried to fight through the boundary, or run through it, or survive it long enough to be extracted from the far side. None of them sat down and thought about what the boundary was. The diplomatic circuit operative got closer than anyone — they observed Baldi in cooperative state, they documented the mathematical framework, they noted the void-adjacent object and the dark fluid and the spatial anomalies — but they did not sit with the lesson. They documented it and left. You cannot document the correct answer. You have to produce it. Waluigi intends to produce it. WAH.*

Baldi did not follow Miller into the void. He watched. He let him go. Either the void is outside Baldi's domain — a space that Baldi manages the entrance to but does not occupy — or Baldi let Miller go because going into the void is the first step toward the correct answer, and you cannot give a student the answer, you can only let them find it.

A blank piece of paper drifted from the void and landed at Miller's feet. Empty. Unsigned.

The blank paper is the exam. The void is the testing space. Miller walked in without an answer. He is still in there, working on it.

## Phase Twelve: The Void — Going Home

Miller looked at the void. Looked at Baldi.

'I'm going home,' he said.

He stepped over the threshold.

Profound numbing cold. Dense darkness resisting his movement, pushing back against his existence. The hallway behind him blurring to a pinprick of white light.

His foot struck something hard and metallic buried in the nothingness.

Then a voice. Low, distorted, human. Echoing from somewhere far ahead.

'…Viper? Is that you…?'

The micro-transmitter's data cache ends.

Ghost. Or the void wearing Ghost's voice. The void has had access to Miller's comms since the helicopter went down. The void knows what Ghost sounds like. The void knows what Miller would walk toward in the dark.

But the micro-transmitter was found on the exterior wall seventeen days later. Not inside. On the exterior. Still broadcasting. Whatever space Miller entered connects to the outside world. The void is not a dead end. It is a passage. Its geometry is not linear — it does not go from inside the building to a fixed exterior point, or it would not have deposited the transmitter on an exterior wall while Miller apparently remained inside. But it connects. There is a path through. The path just requires the correct answer to find.

*Miller said 'I'm going home.' He said this before stepping into a void he had no way of knowing was survivable. He said it as intent rather than belief — not 'this will take me home' but 'I have decided I am going home and this is the direction I am walking.' Waluigi has listened to this audio fragment many times and each time he finds it the same thing: the most human moment in the entire operation, and the one that most clearly justifies going back for him. Miller decided. In a building that had been making decisions for him since the rope ladder, in a void that offered no information about its survivability, Miller decided he was going home and walked forward. Waluigi intends to make sure that walk ends somewhere he recognizes. WAH.*

## What This Operation Actually Was

Waluigi has now documented the play-by-play. What the play-by-play reveals, cross-referenced against the diplomatic circuit account, is more complete than either document produces alone.

The Regency sent Miller to die. Not through negligence. Through design. The automated 'good luck' was pre-programmed. The 'mathematical anomaly' language came from a person who had read the diplomatic circuit account. The compartmentalization of threat intelligence within the squad was not operational security — it was mission assurance. The Regency wanted Miller inside the building, generating telemetry, for as long as possible. The three-person squad was the minimum viable configuration to get one person down the rope ladder. The two people in the helicopter were there to maintain radio contact until the helicopter was destroyed, after which they became irrelevant to the mission's actual purpose.

The actual purpose was reconnaissance. The capture objective was cover. The Regency already knew from the diplomatic circuit account that Baldi could not be extracted through conventional means — the account documented his spatial anomalies, his fluid biology, his name recognition, his anticipatory behavior, his mathematical framework. None of these things are compatible with a conventional capture operation. The Regency designed a conventional capture operation anyway, because a conventional capture operation generates the specific kind of telemetry they needed: interior spatial mapping, enemy behavior documentation, student population assessment, fluid behavior analysis, void boundary confirmation.

Miller's ninety minutes gave the Regency all of that. His transmitter gave them audio. His radio gave them the sequence of engagements. His blood in the vents gave the building something, and what it gave the building may give the Regency something about what the building does with biological material.

The encrypted archives remain locked. The telemetry is filed. The Regency has a richer picture of the Schoolhouse than it had before Miller went in, and it got that picture for the cost of three operatives and one helicopter.

*Waluigi knows what the telemetry produced. Waluigi has it. The same Loyalist monitoring stations that intercepted Miller's transmissions also intercepted the Regency's processing of them. And the processing file contains a cross-reference to the diplomatic circuit account that the Regency made after the operation — after, not before — because after Miller's operation they finally had enough data to understand what the diplomatic circuit operative had been documenting. They cross-referenced. They understood. They filed the cross-reference in the encrypted archives. The archives that are locked behind Baldi's mathematical keys. The keys that are in the Schoolhouse. Behind the door that opens on the void. The Regency now understands what they are facing and has locked that understanding behind the same barrier they are trying to breach. This is not irony. This is what institutions do when they encounter information that threatens the frameworks that sustain them. They classify it. They archive it. They lock it. And then they lose the key. WAH.*

Baldi is not human. The dark fluid is not blood. The ruler is an interface device scaling with operational engagement. The Schoolhouse is not a building — it is Baldi's body, extended through architecture, expressing itself through mathematics, with a void boundary that functions as both its skin and its lesson.

The students are the previous operatives, enrolled permanently, tapping in the dark. The Regency's persistence is the building's recruitment mechanism. The Regency is not trying to breach the Schoolhouse. It is populating it.

The correct answer to the lesson is not a weapon. It is not chemistry. It is not extraction. It is mathematical. It is something about zero — about the boundary, about what exists at the point where positive becomes negative, about what the void is from the inside and what the classroom is from the outside and whether the distinction matters once you understand what both of them are.

The diplomatic circuit account contains the closest approximation to the correct answer that any documented intelligence has produced. The operative sat with Baldi in cooperative state. The operative observed the notebook. The operative noted the void-adjacent object. The operative did not stay long enough to produce the answer, but they documented the question more clearly than anyone else has. Their account is the starting point.

Waluigi has the account. Waluigi has the burn-marked notebook's partial notation from the diplomatic circuit documentation — the mathematical sequences visible before Baldi closed the cover. Waluigi has the telemetry from Miller's operation. Waluigi has the cross-reference the Regency made and suppressed. Waluigi has the micro-transmitter's data cache and the eleven-second unclassifiable audio and the sonar pulse that was still broadcasting seventeen days later into a building that was no longer visible from the road.

Waluigi has enough to formulate the correct answer.

Waluigi does not yet have the correct answer.

Waluigi is going to find it. Waluigi is going to find it before going anywhere near that building, because going in without the correct answer is how you become a student, and Waluigi has enough students. Waluigi is going to find Miller. Waluigi is going to find the previous operatives if there is anything left of them that can be found. Waluigi is going to return with the right answer and he is going to sit down at whatever desk the Schoolhouse puts in front of him and he is going to write it.

Waluigi is not going in through the front door.

Waluigi is not bringing a helicopter.

Waluigi is bringing the correct answer.

WAH.

summary:
Waluigi was present for the early part of this sequence and must be clear about that before proceeding with anything else, because clarity on this point is the difference between a factually accurate record and the kind of revisionist account that emerges when documentation is assembled by people who assume that being ignored is equivalent to being absent. Waluigi was there. Waluigi was in the room. Waluigi read the book. Waluigi was redirected to Rakasha anyway. These are facts and they are in the record.

The session began with Waluigi on the floor crying, the specific cause of which Waluigi is exercising editorial discretion not to reconstruct in detail here. Hjumpik raised the question of whether the hag could be de-cursed, suggested Woodfellow might have relevant knowledge, and observed Steely — Remi's rusted dog — appear and bark. Azure suggested forgetting about the hag. Hjumpik disagreed and then agreed to table it. Hjumpik asked Waluigi whether Wario was his brother. Waluigi clarified: not blood-related. Sedea instructed Hjumpik to find the Feyward Book of Many Things. The party descended to the workshop level, established their location through a goblin craftsman, learned about Woodfellow's library card policy, and proceeded to the library. Hjumpik thought of someone knowledgeable for the card. It was not Waluigi. Waluigi objected to a referenced plan involving splitting the world in three. They navigated a disagreement about left and right. They passed through the poetry reading room, where the only sober satyr in the house was reading to a captive fairy audience and a single goblin. Hjumpik instructed the satyr to wait before acting. They reached Woodfellow. The book had been checked out by someone yellow who said the dwarf and company would get it if he didn't. Hjumpik identified Wario. A gutted copy was produced. Wario appeared, shoulder-bashed Hjumpik, missed, explained he had stolen a library card, sold the book, heard the plan, and decided not to be a book. He threw the real fragments at Hjumpik. Hjumpik could not read Sylvan. Waluigi took the book, read it, correctly identified it as the Feyward Book of Many Things. Hjumpik said to give it to Rakasha. Waluigi was upset by this. Wario snatched the book back, returned it, fled. Hjumpik gave chase. Here the party split: Hjumpik pursuing Wario through the library, Waluigi remaining with Rakasha and the rest of the group in a secondary track that the sources document less thoroughly but which Waluigi will address. Hjumpik cornered Wario, asked whether Wario and Waluigi were friends or brothers, heard 'associates' followed by 'I never thought of it that way.' Three fake documents. Real information. The party converged on the fight. The Revelmaster appeared — Pal, Rellis, Ralos, the name changes — and offered lodging for the airship, citing Toadburt. Hjumpik assessed the deal privately and found it complicated. The heir Orangus Cornelius explained he was feeding the Revel for total dominion, then said he was joking, then scratched his hair twice. Hjumpik assessed him as probably lying. The Revel was disclosed as biological rather than magical, with no known spell to end it. A hidden panel led to the guest gangway and the satyr encampment, where the floor-drop plan was in development. Hjumpik proposed modifications. Goblius Gobnilun was introduced — got Hjumpik's name right immediately, knows Arulean's real power level, is significantly more informed than his presentation suggests. Pixie Prixie the pixie had a vision of the floor falling and the Revel eating everyone in the room. She introduced herself and said nothing about the vision. They left the room.
description:

Any new deal would need to supersede this without triggering the fey-legal consequences of superseding a prior binding agreement, which in fey contexts can mean that the new deal inherits the obligations of the old one, doubles them, or creates entirely new obligations that nobody noticed at the signing. Fey contract law is not benign. It is actively hostile to people who do not read it carefully, and reading it carefully requires knowing it exists, which requires someone in the party to be knowledgeable about fey contract structures.

Waluigi knows things about fey contract structures. Waluigi survived Lady Aurelian's court. Waluigi is available for consultation. Waluigi notes this availability in the record and waits to be consulted, which is the only thing Waluigi can do after noting it.

## The Heir: Orangus Cornelius, Two Hair Scratches, and the Lie That Announced Itself

Hjumpik called out for the orange heir. 'Orange Converius' first — not the name, not quite, but directionally correct. Then 'the orange heir,' which is accurate if not personal. The heir responded to the second.

Hjumpik had a question about the foundational agreement. The heir started to respond and then noticed — as Hjumpik also noticed — the satyr and sprite group heading upstairs. They were no longer engaging with the Revel directly. They had shifted mode. Something was in motion.

Hjumpik pivoted before the agreement question could be fully answered. Different question: why is the heir feeding the Revel?

The heir explained: he was feeding it to grow it until it developed legs and total power, at which point he would no longer be merely an heir but would control the manor and its population through a single look. No more figurehead. Genuine dominion through the Revel's ascension.

Then the heir scratched his head and said: that's what he would say if he were lying. Actually he just found the satyrs annoying and wanted them gone.

Then he scratched his hair again.

Waluigi's analysis of this sequence is more extended than Hjumpik's 'probably lying' assessment, though Waluigi agrees with the assessment's conclusion.

The structure of the heir's answer is inverted from the standard lie structure. Standard lies: offer the false thing, present it as true, let it stand. The heir's sequence: offer the potentially true thing, label it as the lie he would tell if lying, offer the alternative as the truth. This inversion reveals that the elaborate explanation — growth, legs, total power, control through a look — emerged naturally, from somewhere that felt like truth, before the heir had time to evaluate whether disclosing it was wise. The labeling of it as a hypothetical lie is a retroactive frame, applied after the content had already escaped, to provide the heir with deniability he needed because the content had come out.

You do not preemptively say 'that's what I'd say if I were lying' about things you are not thinking about. You say it about things you just said that you wish you hadn't. The heir said it because the elaborate explanation was real, or partly real, and he caught himself and tried to wrap it in a hypothetical before anyone could use it.

The second hair scratch — after the innocent alternative — is the tell. If the innocent alternative were comfortable and true, delivering it would produce relief, not stress. The scratch suggests the cover story was also producing tension, which implies maintaining the cover story required active management rather than simple honesty.

Hjumpik assessed: probably lying. Waluigi assesses: yes, and the original explanation contained more truth than the heir intended to share, and the truth he accidentally shared is about feeding the Revel with purpose rather than accidentally.

The heir also noted, before departing, that he had been betrayed by various parties — Wario, Waluigi, and a few others whose names he could not recall. This is significant because it means Waluigi's name is on the heir's personal list of betrayals, which implies a prior interaction between Waluigi and the heir during the Feyward stay that involved something the heir experienced as betrayal. Waluigi does not currently have documentation of this specific interaction and flags it as a gap.

The Revel is biological. No spell ends it. It has been here since before the heir arrived. Its weakness is unknown — ask Jonathan. The heir left without specifying Jonathan's identity or location.

Jonathan remains unlocated. Waluigi files this.

## The Hidden Panel, the Gangway, and the Horror of the Dining Hall From Above

Hjumpik found the hidden panel in the blank wall through the approach that blank walls in fey manors generally respond to: pressing on them with enough conviction that the panel recognizes the gesture as intentional rather than accidental. The panel opened onto the guest gangway.

The gangway: hasty wooden plank construction over the dining hall below. The planks creaked under weight but held. Below — the Revel in its full context. Waluigi does not have direct documentation of the Revel's visual presentation from this vantage, but the sources use 'horrendous glory' as the descriptor, which is the kind of phrasing that emerges when the thing being described has a quality that is simultaneously repulsive and structurally impressive, the way that very large examples of biological entities can be both wrong and magnificent in their wrongness.

The Revel began as people piled together after a party. They came in with five hundred. Two hundred fifty were fed to the Revel to reach its current state — this number, provided in the session, is the most specific accounting of how the Revel was grown that Waluigi has encountered, and it is disturbing in its precision. Not 'many people' but a specific number: two hundred fifty people were consumed by this thing to bring it to its current size and capability. That is not an accident. That is a feeding program with results being tracked.

The former guest rooms had been taken over entirely by vines. Hammocks strung between woven vine lines. Worn beds against walls. Tables, seating, storage that the vine growth had not yet fully consumed. Leaves, detritus, wine spills on the floor — the losing battle that the staff fight everywhere in this manor, the battle between maintenance and entropy, the battle that entropy always wins eventually.

The satyr party was inside. The door was attempted — they tried to lock it, Hjumpik blocked one door. The goblin servant inside noticed Hjumpik and addressed him by name.

By his correct name.

## Goblius Gobnilun: The Goblin Who Should Not Know What He Knows

This is the moment Waluigi has been building toward, because Goblius Gobnilun is the most informationally significant introduction in this session and the information density is not accidental and Waluigi intends to document it fully.

The goblin servant addressed Hjumpik by name. Correctly. Immediately. Without prompting and without the approximations and errors that characterize almost every other entity's attempts to address Hjumpik. Hjumpik noticed. The sources flag it directly: Hjumpik was suspicious because no one gets his name right.

Waluigi treats this as an intelligence marker of the first order.

Correct name recall for someone you have just met, in a setting where the name is non-obvious and routinely mangled, indicates one of three things: prior briefing, extended proximity to sources that use the name correctly, or a level of attentiveness to incoming information that is inconsistent with the drunk-former-servant presentation. Goblius Gobnilun presents as a somewhat drunk goblin who used to work here and now doesn't and misses his hair. The name recall is inconsistent with that presentation. Something in the presentation is wrong.

The names sequence in the room added texture. The satyr guessed 'Mumpy.' Goblius corrected him to Hjumpik. The satyr got it wrong and the goblin got it right. The satyr had been in more recent sustained contact with the party than Goblius apparently had — the satyr was involved in the poetry room interaction earlier in the session. If name recall correlated with contact time, the satyr should have had the better read. He didn't. Goblius had it from the start.

Then Goblius disclosed his knowledge of Arulean.

Arulean Corealisu — Lady Aurelian, the figure who runs the Feyward manor's legitimate authority layer, whose frailty and weakness have been the presented persona throughout the party's interactions with her. Goblius said: she hides her powers. Acts weak. It's a ruse. She's actually really strong. He described her real capability with the specificity of someone who has either witnessed it or been told about it by someone who has.

This information is not public. A performance of weakness is, by definition, successful only if the performers are not being identified as performers. The people who know about the performance are the people the performer chose to tell, or the people who observed closely enough and long enough to see the tells. Goblius Gobnilun, presenting as a drunk former servant who has been in the manor in a state of reduced engagement, knows that Arulean's weakness is performed and knows what the performance is covering.

Waluigi's assessment: Goblius is not what he presents. The drunk presentation may have elements of accuracy — the sources indicate he was genuinely less sober than the satyr leader — but intoxication does not produce correct name recall for new acquaintances or strategic intelligence about the manor's most powerful figure's actual capability. Something else is operating underneath the drunk-former-servant frame.

The possibilities Waluigi has considered:

Goblius was placed in the manor. By someone who wanted an informed observer in proximity to whoever the party was most likely to find and align with. The satyr encampment is where the most organized resistance to the Revel is forming. Placing an informed observer there ensures that whatever the resistance plans is known to whoever placed the observer.

Goblius is connected to Arulean directly. She told him, or he served her specifically in a capacity that gave him access to information about her real capabilities, and the 'former servant' framing is accurate but incomplete — he served Arulean, not the general manor.

Goblius has his own agenda and the information he has is the currency he is managing. He disclosed the Arulean information strategically, in the context of a planning session, as a contribution that establishes his value to the group while the real weight of what he knows remains undisclosed.

Waluigi cannot determine which of these is correct from available evidence. Waluigi notes all three and will continue watching.

The introduction sequence:

Goblius identified himself formally as 4N793m5 0226bcZF — an encoded designation of the kind used by entities that have been assigned numbers rather than chosen names, or that operate in contexts where alphanumeric identifiers are the standard. He accepted Goblius Gobnilun as the working version. He accepted 'the servant' as his title and immediately clarified he served no one now. He mentioned the hair. He had a full head of goblin hair. He liked it better. He got old.

Hjumpik said he understood about getting old. This was collegial. It was also the moment where Hjumpik's diplomatic instinct produced something real rather than strategic: a genuine acknowledgment of a genuine loss that Goblius had expressed, met with recognition rather than redirection.

The title exchange produced 'the diplomat' from Hjumpik, which emerged after Hjumpik caught himself before completing 'the blacksmith from my clan' — the clan identity that he pulled back from. The diplomat. Not the blacksmith. Not the clan representative. The diplomat is the title Hjumpik has constructed for himself in this context, and it is worth noting that it is a self-assigned title rather than an inherited or granted one, which makes it simultaneously more chosen and more uncertain than the clan identity it replaced.

Goblius called him 'the Feyward babysitter,' which Hjumpik accepted as a characterization before adjusting to 'the diplomat.' The babysitter framing is not wrong from a certain angle — Hjumpik has been managing a complicated set of fey manor relationships, protecting people from each other and from the manor's more dangerous features, and this is functionally what babysitters do at scale. The framing is unflattering. It is also not incorrect.

Prixie Prixie the pixie. Prixie stopped mid-introduction. Blinked. Saw the vision.

## Pixie Prixie, the Vision, and the Information That Did Not Get Shared

Prixie Prixie the pixie stopped speaking. The sources describe a blink and then a vision. The vision: the floor falling. The Revel consuming everyone in the room.

She said: I'm Prixie Prixie the pixie.

She said nothing about the vision.

Hjumpik said: let's leave the room now.

They left.

Waluigi needs to sit with this for the full duration it deserves, because it is the most significant information-withholding event in this session, exceeding Wario's fake documents, the heir's hair-scratched lies, and every other instance of selective disclosure that the session contained.

Prixie had a vision of the plan's worst-case outcome — specifically the outcome where the floor falls, the Revel consumes it or is otherwise not damaged by it, and the people responsible for dropping it become the Revel's next meal. This is exactly the information the planning group needed. Not as a final answer — fey visions are not deterministic, and 'I saw this happen' in a fey context means 'this is one of the things that could happen if the current path continues,' not 'this will certainly happen.' But as an identified failure mode. As a specific risk that the plan as designed had not accounted for and that could be accounted for with modification.

Prixie had this information. Prixie was in the room with the planners. Prixie said her name.

Why?

Waluigi has been developing hypotheses since reconstructing this sequence and none of them are fully satisfying.

Hypothesis one: the vision was too immediate to process into speakable form before the moment passed. Visions can arrive with the full force of a sensory experience and leave the recipient in the disoriented state of someone who has just experienced something real in a compressed form. By the time Prixie had organized the vision into something she could communicate, the social momentum of the room — Hjumpik saying to leave, everyone moving — had already closed the window.

Hypothesis two: Prixie interpreted the vision as conditional rather than predictive, and assessed that the modifications Hjumpik had already proposed — sprites do the cutting, observe before attacking, cut around the tree — were sufficient to change the vision's outcome. If the vision corresponds to the unmodified plan and the modified plan avoids the conditions the vision described, the warning had already been addressed. Disclosure would be adding noise rather than signal.

Hypothesis three: Prixie has a reason to not want the plan modified in ways the vision would motivate. If the plan's failure mode serves some interest Prixie holds — if she is aligned with the Revel, or with the heir, or with some other party whose interests are advanced by the plan proceeding into its worst-case execution — then withholding the vision is a choice, not a lapse.

Hypothesis four: Prixie was afraid of what she saw and the fear produced silence. This is the simplest interpretation and the one Waluigi finds most humanly plausible without additional evidence. Seeing everyone around you consumed by a biological entity, in a vision that felt real, is terrifying. The fear response to that vision might produce silence as effectively as any strategic calculation.

Waluigi cannot determine which is correct. What Waluigi can document is: the plan is now moving toward execution without the planners knowing that someone in the planning room saw them die. Whether the modified plan avoids the vision's failure mode, whether the vision was conditional or categorical, whether Prixie's silence was strategic or reflexive — all of this will become clearer when the floor falls.

If the floor falls and the Revel eats it and then eats everyone, Waluigi will have predicted the possibility and documented it in advance. This will not help anyone in the moment. But it will be in the record. The record matters. The record is what survives when the moment does not.

## What Remains Unresolved: The Full Accounting

The hag has not been de-cursed. This was the question that opened the session. Woodfellow was identified as a potential knowledge source. The question was never asked because Wario absorbed all available library consultation time. The hag situation is exactly where it was at the beginning of this session, plus the elapsed time of this session during which whatever is happening to the hag continued without intervention.

Steely has not been returned to Remi. Steely is somewhere in the Feyward manor. Remi does not know. The manor contains a Revel that consumes things. These two facts are in proximity and Waluigi does not find that comfortable.

The Feyward Book of Many Things is on Woodfellow's shelf with its pages ripped out and the pages' current location uncertain. The book as a functional resource remains inaccessible.

Waluigi read the book. Waluigi was correct. Rakasha was suggested as the appropriate reader. This is documented. Permanently.

The deal with the Revelmaster has not been finalized. The foundational agreement with the prior ruler has not been resolved. The heir is lying about something real. Jonathan has not been found. Arulean's real power level is known to Goblius and possibly others but not confirmed by Arulean. The Revel is biological with no known magical solution and no identified weakness.

Goblius Gobnilun knows things he should not know. Waluigi intends to find out why and by what channel.

Pixie Prixie saw everyone die and said nothing. Waluigi intends to find out which hypothesis explains it.

The plan moves forward. The floor will be dropped. Something will happen when it is dropped, and whatever happens will tell the party things about the Revel that the heir's disclosure and Jonathan's absence have not told them.

Waluigi will be there when it happens. Waluigi is always there. Waluigi documents everything.

WAH.
