summary:
Waluigi was not present for this sequence, which means this entry is reconstructed from testimony rather than direct observation, but the reconstruction is thorough because the important line through all of it is clear: Raventree Manor is no longer merely a destination. It is a gravity well. Everyone with unfinished business — divine mandates, barrel-toad history, pyromancer problems, missing companions, intercepted communications, wanted posters, or suspiciously partial witness statements — is being pulled toward the same house.

The session centered on Markop's father, who by the end of the sequence formally identified himself as Kaelor Judi. He entered an office and was handed a wanted poster naming his son, Markop Judi, with a 2,000-gold bounty attached for crimes against magic. Present in the room were an interviewer, a woman operating the process, two goblins whose affiliation was initially unclear, and a line of supposed witnesses who claimed they might know something about Markop's whereabouts. The witness list: one goomba, one hammer bro, one koopa decked out in impressive swag, Ryan, a mage, and a guard.

The goomba went first, asked whether he could take off his shoes — which was weird — claimed he had seen Markop at the grove with Mazebound, was stopped when he tried to leave, and was exposed as a fraud when Kaelor seized his notes and found newspaper clippings instead of firsthand accounts. Headlines about Markop helping a pyromaniac escape and Raventree Manor being surrounded during the fracture. Kaelor told him he did not get paid for lying and threw him out the window.

The koopa — Slick — was more interesting. He claimed to have fought Markop in an underground circuit near the old coliseum ruins, described Markop as strong and stylish, noted that Markop had paused to help a downed fighter and refused prize money. Kaelor doubted him on sight, challenged him to prove combat credibility, and took a hit to the stomach that left a bruise. Slick talked about debts connecting the Legion and the toads, referenced a magic toad outside, then accidentally opened the Vigilance thread — barrel toads, contradictory reports about whether Markop or a pyromancer had blown up the ship, yellow toad testimony. He received 20 gold for the useful fragments.

Ryan went next and sounded exactly like what he was: someone trying to compress months of genuine catastrophe into an office-length answer. He confirmed knowing Markop, described the mission split that separated him from Bones, identified Bones by name, and then noticed the two goblins in the room taking notes. The goblins said they were with 'him' — outside.

Kaelor looked out the window and saw Sprig the Mole. He went through the window after him, caught him, and confronted him. Sprig admitted the witnesses had revealed more than intended. Kaelor searched him and recovered intercepted Pond Patrol communications about Raventree Manor — siege-posture language, toad movements, rally points, and a full transcript of We Are the Toads. Kaelor concluded that everything linked back to Raventree.

Back inside, the goblins had escaped. Luigi was there. Luigi denied knowing Sprig, then explained that he and the rest of the witness list had already agreed to sneak into Raventree Manor for Archie. Luigi also had another reason for going in, which he did not disclose.

The witness line became an expedition roster. Everyone went except the goomba. Kaelor Judi revealed his true name and joined the movement toward the manor.
description:
Waluigi is documenting this session because it demonstrates a pattern that keeps repeating around Raventree Manor: independent investigations are ceasing to remain independent. Separate motives are collapsing into one route. A father looking for his son, survivors and affiliates of the Vigilance, a mole carrying intercepted communications, small-time fight-pit witnesses, Luigi with undisclosed motivations, and a line of supposed eyewitnesses of wildly varying credibility all ended up in the same orbit and are now headed in the same direction.

Waluigi was not present. Waluigi was in the Feyward, in a hot spring, reading his own wiki entry on a tablet while the manor burned around him. What follows is reconstructed from multiple sources, crossreferenced where possible, and documented with the analytical rigor that Waluigi applies to everything regardless of whether he was in the room.

## The Office: A Poster, a Woman, Two Goblins, and the Question of Who Set This Up

Kaelor entered an office.

The nature of the office is important because it establishes the context for everything that followed. This was not a military briefing room. This was not a guild hall. This was not a tavern where rumors accumulate and get sold over drinks. This was an administrative intake point — a place with procedures, with a woman running those procedures, with a structure that implied institutional backing even if the institution behind the structure was not identified.

Kaelor was handed a poster.

WANTED: Markop Judi. Crimes against magic. Reward: 2,000 gold.

Waluigi wants to pause here because wanted posters are not neutral documents. They are institutional speech acts. A poster does several things at once. It criminalizes. It simplifies. It offers strangers a price at which a person may be transformed from relative, ally, or rumor into a commodity. Whatever else Kaelor was in that moment — a father, a fighter, a man who came looking for answers about his son — he was also a person being handed a price tag for his child.

Two thousand gold for crimes against magic. The specific charge is worth noting because it connects Markop to the Archie thread. 'Crimes against magic' is the kind of charge that gets applied broadly when institutions want someone associated with a magical event that embarrassed or threatened the institution. Markop's documented involvement with Archie — traveling together, operating together, being present when Archie did what Archie does — would be sufficient for a 'crimes against magic' charge if the institution writing the poster did not distinguish between the pyromaniac and the people standing near the pyromaniac when the fire started.

Also present in the room: two goblins. They were sitting there when Kaelor arrived. The interviewer — the woman running the process — did not explain who they were. They did not introduce themselves. They sat, and they took notes, and they looked up and down between their notes and the proceedings with the energy of creatures documenting something for a report they were planning to deliver to someone who was not in the room.

Their affiliation would become clear later. At this point they were ambient suspicious detail.

The interviewer told Kaelor they had witnesses lined up who might know his son.

The word 'might' is doing a great deal of work there. What followed would demonstrate exactly how much.

## The Witness Line

Six witnesses. Lined up. Available for interview. The composition of the line tells you something about the investigation's quality before anyone opens their mouth:

1. A goomba.
2. A hammer bro.
3. A koopa decked out in cool swag.
4. Ryan.
5. A mage.
6. A guard.

This is not a curated intelligence briefing. This is a casting call. The range of species, styles, and apparent backgrounds suggests that whoever assembled this line was collecting anyone who claimed to have information about Markop and presenting them without quality filtering. The filtering was left to Kaelor.

## Witness One: The Goomba — Shoes, Mazebound, and the Newspaper Clippings

The goomba went first.

The first thing he asked was whether he could take off his shoes.

Kaelor said: yeah, that's weird.

Waluigi notes the exchange because the request matters. Witnesses who open with an unnecessary personal ritual before testifying are stalling. The shoes were not relevant to Markop. The shoes were relevant to the goomba's nerves. He was buying time inside his own performance.

The goomba claimed he had seen Markop at the grove with Mazebound.

On its face this was plausible enough to be dangerous. Raventree-adjacent events and grove activity had already entered the rumor network. Mazebound was the kind of specific name a liar uses because specificity creates temporary trust — it sounds like the kind of detail only an eyewitness would know, which is exactly why it is the first thing a prepared liar memorizes.

Kaelor called out how he believed him — meaning he expressed skepticism directly, in the tone of a man who has heard enough unconvincing things to recognize another one arriving.

The goomba ran.

Kaelor stopped him. Snatched his notes.

The notes were not notes.

They were newspaper clippings. Assembled fragments of Markop's already-circulating story. The clippings included headlines: Markop Judi helped pyromaniac get off scot free. Raventree Manor surrounded as fracture occurred.

This is one of Waluigi's least favorite forms of false witness. Not invention from whole cloth — that is easier to dismiss. This was patchwork fraud. The goomba had taken real events, clipped them from public coverage, arranged them, and prepared to sell them back as personal knowledge. He was performing the role of eyewitness using material anyone could have obtained from a newsstand.

Kaelor's response: 'You don't get paid for lying.'

The goomba was kicked out. Through the window.

Waluigi approves of the investigative efficiency if not the architectural implications for the window.

## Witness Two: Slick the Koopa — Style, Shell Defense, and the Accidental Vigilance Thread

The koopa came next.

The sources identify him less by formal name than by aesthetic and tone: decked out in cool swag. Stylish. A grin that preceded his words. Waluigi is not immune to presentation and is therefore willing to note that the koopa's style may have been his most truthful feature.

Slick's claim: he had seen Markop at an underground fight circuit near the old coliseum ruins.

His description of Markop was notable not for spectacle but for character detail. 'Dude's got style under all that muscle,' Slick said, describing how Markop had paused to help a downed fighter afterward and refused prize money in favor of — the sentence trails off in the sources, but the implication is generosity or principle or both. This is the sort of detail liars often forget. Lies about fighters usually focus on impact and victory. Truth, or something closer to it, includes what happened when the fighting stopped.

Kaelor's response: 'You saw my son?'

Slick: 'Yeah, I fought him.'

Kaelor looked at Slick. Assessed him physically. Rendered judgment: 'You don't even look half as strong as me. My son is strong.'

Slick's defense: 'I got shell defense.'

This is not a foolish answer. Shell defense changes koopa combat mathematics entirely. Waluigi has documented enough koopa encounters to know that evaluating a koopa's combat credibility by looking at his exposed body is like evaluating an armored knight by looking at his boots. The shell is the argument. Slick was not wrong to cite it.

Kaelor pressed for details.

What was his weapon?

Slick said: he used his hooves.

Kaelor caught the implication and pushed: if Markop was going to settle a score, why limit himself? Why fight with hooves when he has access to weapons?

Kaelor then articulated the larger question beneath the weapon question: he didn't see why Markop would be doing all this stuff. Fighting in a pit. Settling scores. Competing for money. The Markop that Kaelor knew — or believed he knew — would not be in an underground fight circuit near coliseum ruins. The question was not 'did you fight him' but 'why would he be the kind of person you could fight?'

Slick answered: for the love of the game and money. He had debts. From the Legion to the toads.

Toads.

That single word detonated a chain of follow-up that neither Slick nor Kaelor had prepared for.

Kaelor: 'Toads?'

Slick referenced a magic toad who had really helped. The magic toad was outside. They knew each other — not directly, but through the network that formed when a particular ship crashed and certain barrels had to end up somewhere.

Kaelor caught the pivot: 'What ship?'

Slick hesitated. 'Uhhh, maybe I'm going into too much detail.'

Kaelor did not let him retreat: 'Whoa whoa whoa, you switched your story. What ship?'

Then Kaelor attacked Slick's credibility again: 'You look weaker than me. You can't fight him. You're a liar.'

Slick's response: 'You know what? Prove it. Attack me.'

The invitation was reversed — not 'I'll prove I can fight' but 'YOU prove I can't.' Kaelor obliged. Slick delivered a hit that bruised Kaelor's stomach.

Kaelor: 'Off. I still don't believe you. What about the ship?'

The truth came out in fragments, the way truth usually does from people who know more than they are supposed to share and whose filter for what is too much detail has already failed.

The Vigilance. Some toads fell off in barrels when it exploded. Toads came singing. One yellow toad was there — said Markop blew up the ship. But another toad said it was a pyromancer.

Waluigi notes the contradictory blame assignment because contradictions around Archie and flame events are now common enough to be operational weather in this campaign. When fire is involved, multiple truths circulate at once: what happened, what people saw, what people blamed, what institutions printed, and what survivors needed to believe to keep functioning. 'Markop blew up the ship' and 'a pyromancer blew up the ship' are not necessarily incompatible if both people were present when the ship was destroyed and different witnesses attributed the destruction to different members of the same group. This is how Disaster Inc. events propagate through the rumor network — as contradictory fragments, each one true from a different angle.

Slick: 'Can I get paid now?'

Kaelor gave him 20 gold.

Not the full bounty. Not a reward for certainty. A payment for fragments. The koopa had not proven the whole story, but he had proven enough of himself — bruised stomach as evidence — and enough of the network around the story to be worth something. Twenty gold for pain, partial truth, and the Vigilance thread reopened.

## Witness Three: Ryan — Rambling Truth and the Separation from Bones

Ryan's testimony reads like the opposite of the goomba's because Ryan sounded exactly like what he was: someone trying to explain a real, complicated disaster without the rhetorical equipment to make it graceful.

Kaelor: 'Have you seen my son, Markop?'

Ryan: 'Oh yeah, I know Markop. It's just that the last time I saw him was, uhh, at the ship if memory serves right. One of the ships we rode on. But well, I guess it's a long story, all of which is confusing. But, umm, uhh, basically I was part of a group that your son was a part of, then stuff happened, I got separated from him, as well as a bunch of other stuff. I'm fighting my way back to him.'

Waluigi trusts this kind of testimony more than polished certainty. Real survivors of campaign-grade chaos do not narrate cleanly. They circle. They qualify. They try to compress months of catastrophe into one office answer and fail because the catastrophe resists compression. Ryan's 'umm, uhh, basically' is not evasion. It is the sound of a person holding too much truth in working memory and trying to select which parts of it are safe to say in an office with unknown people taking notes.

Kaelor asked how they got split up.

Ryan explained: him and four other toads went on a mission. Two groups split up. Three toads in one group. Two in the other. He was in the two-person group. He got separated from the other toad.

Kaelor: 'Who was the other toad?'

Ryan: 'Bones. We last saw Markop, Dad, at a ship that was flooded with toads.'

The 'Dad' is Ryan calling Kaelor 'Dad' — either using the term of address because Kaelor had been introduced as Markop's father, or because Ryan has the kind of casual intimacy with language that comes from spending too long in groups where formal titles stopped mattering somewhere between the third explosion and the fourth mission split. Either way it is familiar and it is honest and Waluigi records it as further evidence of Ryan's genuine connection to the Markop network rather than a performed one.

Bones. The name is a key continuity point. Ryan and Bones were paired. Ryan was separated from Bones. Bones's current location remains unknown. Ryan is fighting his way back toward Markop. The chain: Ryan knew Markop, Ryan was in a group with Markop, Ryan was on a mission with toads, Ryan was paired with Bones, Ryan lost Bones, Ryan ended up in this office being interviewed by Markop's father. Every link in the chain is the kind of link that this campaign generates: not cleanly connected but not disconnected either, held together by shared catastrophe rather than shared planning.

Then Ryan did something the earlier witnesses had not done.

He stopped looking at Kaelor and looked at the room.

He whispered, pointing at the two goblins on the seats: 'Who are those guys?'

The goblins were jotting down notes. Looking up and down. The behavioral signature of creatures cataloguing reactions rather than merely listening.

Kaelor: 'Who are you?'

The interviewer — the woman running the process — said: 'I thought they were with you.'

Kaelor did not bring them.

The goblins clarified: 'No. We are with HIM. He is outside.'

## Sprig the Mole: The Window, the Intercept, and the Raventree Packet

Kaelor looked out the window.

Sprig the Mole was there.

Kaelor went through the window after him.

Waluigi does not know the current structural condition of the office window and Waluigi suspects the window does not know either.

Kaelor caught Sprig and confronted him immediately.

'So you brought that guy in. I don't trust him,' Kaelor said.

Sprig's response is revealing because it is evasive in exactly the way partial truth often is.

'Those people were not meant to tell you that. They screwed up. Lesson learned. I'll get going.'

This is not denial. This is damage control. Sprig is not saying the witnesses were wrong. He is saying they said too much. The witnesses were supposed to provide something to Kaelor — some controlled fragment, some managed portion of the truth — and instead they provided more than the operation intended. 'They screwed up' means the information release exceeded the parameters. 'Lesson learned' means the operational failure will be corrected next time. The framing is that of a handler acknowledging an intelligence leak rather than a bystander explaining a coincidence.

Kaelor did not let him leave.

'Wait. I have some questions. Why do you want to find Markop?'

Sprig: 'Unpaid debts. He helped me, so I help him.'

Waluigi notes the debt language carefully. Debt language recurs around Disaster Inc. and its wider orbit with unusual frequency. People do not join because they were recruited cleanly. They join because they owe, because they were saved, because they survived the same corridor, because they are trying to repay something that cannot really be repaid through the conventional mechanisms of repayment. Sprig's claim may be self-serving. It is also structurally believable. People who are helped by Disaster Inc. members tend to end up in the orbit doing things that are partly gratitude and partly the gravitational pull of unfinished business.

'Can I go now?'

Kaelor did not let him go. Kaelor searched him.

What he found was more important than the entire witness line combined.

Intercepted Pond Patrol communications.

The packet, as reconstructed from Kaelor's account and subsequent relay:

- Intercepted communications from the Pond Patrol concerning Raventree Manor.
- Language indicating active assessment of the manor as a target or objective — siege-posture phrasing, staging considerations, the vocabulary of organized movement toward a defended position.
- References to toad movements and rally points. The broader toad network — the Liberated Toads, the Pond Patrol, the organizational infrastructure that formed after the barrel discovery and solidified through repeated crisis — was now treating Raventree as a point of interest significant enough to generate formal communications about.
- Notes connecting the pyromancer hunt to the same area. Archie's trail, as always, leading toward the manor.
- A full transcript of the song We Are the Toads.

Waluigi is going to document the song transcript's presence in an intercepted intelligence packet because it is simultaneously the most absurd and most revealing detail in the recovery. A military or paramilitary intelligence packet containing a full song transcript means one of two things: either the song itself has operational significance — march timing, recognition codes, morale maintenance, rallying function — or the person who assembled the intercept was unable to distinguish operational content from cultural content and included everything. Either interpretation tells you something about the toads. If the song is operational, then toad logistics and toad musicality are not separate categories and have not been separate categories since the barrel toads came singing off the wrecked Vigilance. If the song is cultural noise accidentally included, then the line between toad operations and toad culture is blurry enough that an intelligence professional could not find it.

Waluigi suspects the former. We Are the Toads has appeared at too many operationally significant moments to be dismissed as background music.

Kaelor reached the same conclusion as everyone in this campaign eventually reaches: 'It seems like it all links back to Raventree.'

Sprig offered a lead: 'That green guy I was with might know.'

Kaelor did not let Sprig go anywhere alone. He forced Sprig back inside.

## Back Inside: The Goblins Escaped, the Room Is Empty, and Luigi Appears

The room had changed state.

The two goblin note-takers were gone. The door was open. Whatever structure the witness interview had possessed was now collapsed. The administrative pretense had evaporated the moment the hidden handler outside the window was exposed.

Luigi was there.

Waluigi has thoughts about Luigi being there and Waluigi is going to keep most of them to himself because Luigi's operational decisions deserve the respect of being assessed on their outcomes rather than their presentation, and the outcome is not yet known.

Luigi said he did not know Sprig the Mole.

Waluigi records the denial without endorsing or challenging it. Luigi often tells the truth in ways that sound like he is trying not to tell the full truth, and he also sometimes withholds entirely separate motives because he has, unlike some members of the wider orbit, retained a functional concept of privacy. Whether Luigi knew Sprig or not is less important, operationally, than what Luigi did next.

The questioning continued between Kaelor and Luigi. Both men had reasons to be suspicious. Both men had reasons to cooperate. The conversation moved from the cross-examination mode that had defined the witness interviews into something different: alignment.

Luigi explained that he and the rest of the people on the witness list had already agreed to sneak into Raventree Manor for Archie.

Waluigi needs to spend time on this because it reframes the entire witness line retroactively.

The witnesses were not merely people who knew something about Markop. They were, at least in part, people who were already planning to go to Raventree. The witness line was not only an intelligence-gathering exercise. It was a pre-formed expedition that happened to be using the interview process as its assembly point. Slick's debts. Ryan's search for his former group. Luigi's plan. The mage, the guard, the hammer bro — all of them apparently already committed to the Raventree operation before Kaelor walked in.

The office was not a briefing room. It was a staging area disguised as a claims office.

Luigi also had another reason for wanting to go in. He did not say what it was.

Waluigi could speculate. Waluigi will not here. A good archive distinguishes between inference and evidence.

What matters is that Luigi was not present incidentally. He was present on purpose, and his purpose was already pointed at the manor.

## The Departure: Everyone Except the Goomba

The session pivoted from investigation to mobilization.

The witness line became an expedition roster. The people who had come to offer testimony about Markop were now heading toward the place where Markop, Archie, and the entire Disaster Inc.-adjacent network appeared to be converging.

Everyone went except the goomba.

This is correct. The goomba brought newspaper clippings and a request to remove his shoes. The goomba contributed nothing the expedition needed. The goomba was last seen near the base of a window.

## Kaelor Judi Reveals His Name

By the end of the sequence, Markop's father formally identified himself.

Kaelor Judi.

Waluigi treats name revelation seriously in these records because names matter, especially near Raventree and especially near anything that has been touching the planar fracture. A father searching for his son began the session as a function: Markop's dad, the man with questions, the large skeptical force moving through lies with increasing impatience.

He ended it as Kaelor Judi.

That is a shift from role to person. The father becomes a named participant in the story rather than a named participant's unnamed relative. It also matters because the session began with a poster reducing his son to a bounty line — 'Markop Judi, crimes against magic, 2,000 gold' — and ended with Kaelor restoring human structure to the search by contributing his own identity to it. The poster offered a price. Kaelor offered a name.

## Assessment: How the Witness Line Became a Coalition

The goomba was a fraud.

Slick was part braggart, part genuine contact, and more useful than he first appeared.

Ryan remains one of the cleaner surviving links in the chain connecting Markop, Bones, the Vigilance, and the current dispersal.

Sprig the Mole is a facilitator, eavesdropper, and carrier of useful material whose motives may be partially sincere and are certainly incomplete.

Luigi is moving toward Raventree for Archie and for an additional reason he is not yet ready to disclose.

The Pond Patrol documents matter because they prove institutional or semi-institutional attention is now fixed on the manor.

The full transcript of We Are the Toads matters because, infuriatingly, even the most musical elements of toad logistics keep turning out to be real logistics.

Most importantly: Kaelor Judi now knows what Waluigi has been documenting from several angles already. Raventree Manor is where loose ends go when they stop being loose and start becoming structural.

This is how Disaster Inc.-adjacent coalitions form. Not by oath. Not by banner. Not by elegant mission briefing. By witness fraud, bruised stomachs, missing toads, unpaid debts, escaped goblins, a mole beneath a window, a wanted poster for your son, and the realization that if every bad road points to the same house, eventually you stop pretending there is a safer direction.

The team headed out.

WAH.

summary:
Waluigi was in a sauna for the middle third of this session and is going to address that directly because if he does not address it directly someone will address it indirectly and the indirect version will not contain the context that makes the sauna stay reasonable, which it was. The Feyward branch of Disaster Inc. operates under conditions where one wrong sentence binds your future firstborn to a butterfly court and one wrong silence lets a giant flower eat the building, and in that environment a hot spring is not a luxury, it is a tactical regeneration site.

The session began with Hjumpik attending a crisis planning meeting in the satyr encampment about how to deal with the Revel. Multiple proposals were raised: feed it beer until it explodes, feed it poison, feed it alcohol in massive quantities, cut the floor out from under it, feed it mushrooms, burn it. None of these proposals achieved consensus. A fairy named Kreetus Cetus estimated 455 kegs in the manor. A figure named Ratitus called the saw plan dumb. Arguments happened. Someone disappeared mid-conversation and Hjumpik stopped himself from questioning his own sanity. A brute satyr named Brutus challenged Hjumpik's authority, then split off with his own team and three conscripted fairies to pursue the mushroom plan. Hjumpik discovered a slim leather-bound volume in Woodfellow's library titled 'Concerning the Nature and Sustenance of Revels Eternal,' which warned that starving a Revel causes it to devour the revelers instead, and that the only true end is total surrender or someone willing to be remembered as the one who stopped the music. Hjumpik was given a library card by a goblin patron named Artameer Fellow. Outside, the goblin from earlier reappeared — having faked his disappearance — and proposed seducing the Revel with a flower. Hjumpik rejected this. The goblin began writing something down. Hjumpik chased him into Sedeia's chambers, grabbed him, found a single word written on paper: 'Brutus.' The goblin claimed it was dinner preparations. Hjumpik threatened him. The goblin stabbed Hjumpik with a pen that was actually a knife, then fled. Hjumpik chased him through the manor. The goblin, cornered, made the decision that defined his fate: he ran into the mushroom coat room and barricaded the door behind him, choosing the room full of recoiling parasitic mushrooms over the corridor with the angry dwarf. The mushrooms accepted the offer. By the time Hjumpik broke through, the goblin was on the floor, writhing, itching, fungal growths erupting through his clothing, fabric ripping, the boundary between goblin and mushroom dissolving in real time. Hjumpik brought the dying spored goblin to Sedeia. Sedeia attempted to replace the parasitic mushroom growth with a healing plant. The plant became a hundred-foot flower that crashed through the manor, generating overgrown plant life in a hundred-foot radius, which in a manor that is ALREADY the Overgrown Manor produced catastrophic compounding botanical chaos. The goblin's body became the seed-bed for the flower. Fire spread to the Lord's Chambers. The manor began evacuating upward. Shambling mounds spawned from the overgrowth. Sedeia was separated from Hjumpik when a door closed between them and a shambling mound. She reappeared later claiming to have defeated it, looking suspiciously uninjured. Hjumpik reached the upper mezzanine, found Lady Arulean playing piano with the heir, attempted to speak with her, was blocked by her guard Dave, shouted his name across the room, was ignored, received her response through Dave: the ritual table was covered in leaves and they had had to evacuate from it. Hjumpik entered the survivor's room — a moss-covered sanctuary with mushroom furniture and a forgotten tea set — and then found the sauna, where Waluigi was sitting in the hot spring on his Wahbook tablet reading about the previous session's events. Waluigi agreed to help. Waluigi changed. They returned to the Lord's Chambers. Waluigi summoned a localized ice storm. The fire was extinguished. The overgrowth was frozen. At least one person was dead. Hjumpik said that was perhaps too much. Waluigi said maybe. They cut through the frozen room. The session ended with the fire out, the ice in, the Revel consuming plant matter at an accelerating rate, and the structural situation of the manor significantly worse than it was at the beginning. Disaster Inc. continues to be present in the places it should never have entered, and continues to refuse to let the worst thing in the room remain unchallenged, and continues to make every situation it touches more complicated in the process.
description:
Waluigi is going to begin this entry by establishing a timeline, because this session's events overlap and compound in ways that require temporal clarity to reconstruct accurately, and because Waluigi was separated from Hjumpik for the middle portion and needs to document both tracks — what Hjumpik was doing while Waluigi was in the sauna, and what Waluigi was doing in the sauna while Hjumpik was being stabbed by a goblin who was about to make a decision that would end with the goblin becoming agricultural substrate.

The Feyward branch of Disaster Inc. — currently consisting of Waluigi, Hjumpik, and at various distances Wario, Rakasha, Azure, Sedeia, and whatever the Feyward decides to attach to the group on any given day — operates under the specific constraints that define every Feyward operation: every sentence is a tripwire, every bargain accumulates debt, every debt has flowers on it, and the architecture itself is participating. The manor is not a place where Disaster Inc. is having an adventure. The manor is a thing Disaster Inc. is in negotiation with. Sedeia's hundred-foot flower this session is a reminder that the negotiation can fail catastrophically when the participants do not understand what they are signing.

The timeline, as best Waluigi can reconstruct it from primary sources, Hjumpik's account, Sedeia's account (which Waluigi treats with measured skepticism for reasons documented below), and Waluigi's own direct experience of the portions he was present for:

Phase One: The crisis planning meeting. Hjumpik in the satyr encampment. Multiple proposals for dealing with the Revel. No consensus. The brute satyr splits off. Someone disappears. Hjumpik goes to the library.

Phase Two: Library research. Hjumpik finds the book about Revels. Receives a library card. Exits. Encounters the reappearing goblin. The goblin proposes seduction. Hjumpik rejects it. The goblin writes 'Brutus' on paper. Hjumpik confronts him. The goblin stabs Hjumpik with a pen-knife and flees. Chase through the manor. The goblin barricades himself in the mushroom room. The mushrooms accept him.

Phase Three: Sedeia's catastrophic plant replacement, using the dying spored goblin as the substrate. The hundred-foot flower. The overgrowth cascade. Fire in the Lord's Chambers. Shambling mounds. Evacuation. Sedeia separated from Hjumpik.

Phase Four: Hjumpik reaches the upper mezzanine. Attempts to contact Lady Arulean. Is ignored. Enters the survivor's room. Finds the sauna. Finds Waluigi.

Phase Five: Waluigi and Hjumpik return to the Lord's Chambers. Ice storm. Fire extinguished. Casualties.

Waluigi was present for Phases Four and Five directly. Waluigi's location during Phases One through Three was the sauna, which Waluigi entered after the party split documented in the previous session's entry and which Waluigi occupied continuously until Hjumpik arrived. Waluigi's activities during this period are documented below in the section addressing the sauna.

Waluigi proceeds with the full account.

## Phase One: The Crisis Meeting — Beer, Poison, Saws, Mushrooms, and the Fairy Who Could Count Kegs

The satyr encampment planning room. The same room documented in the previous session — vines everywhere, hammocks, worn beds, the accumulated detritus of people who have been living in a manor that is actively trying to become a forest. The planning group had assembled around the central problem: the Revel is eating everything, how do we make it stop.

Waluigi was not present for this meeting. Waluigi was in the sauna. What follows is reconstructed from Hjumpik's account and corroborated where possible by other sources.

The first proposal came from an unidentified participant: feed it beer so it blows up.

Waluigi wants to engage with this proposal analytically because it reveals assumptions about the Revel's biology that are worth documenting even though the proposal itself was not adopted. The assumption: the Revel, being a biological entity that consumes things, can be overloaded through consumption of a specific substance. The mechanism: the Revel eats beer, the beer does something inside the Revel that beer does not normally do inside biological entities, the Revel explodes. The reasoning gap: no evidence that the Revel processes consumed material the way organisms that can 'blow up' from overconsumption process material. The Revel eats and grows. That is what it does. Feeding it more of anything it can metabolize is feeding it more of anything it can metabolize. The proposal is, structurally, 'solve the eating problem by giving it more to eat.'

This is, in Waluigi's experience, a Disaster-Inc.-adjacent style of reasoning. Disaster Inc. has a long institutional history of solving problems by applying more of the thing the problem is made of. Archie's fireball inside the wooden airship is the canonical example. The Tea Party Incident was 'tension in a confined space, solved with combustion.' This room's first instinct — Revel tha

[... ADMINISTRATIVE PRUNING BY WALUIGI TO SAVE ARCHIVE SPACE ...]

 two options for ending a Revel:

1. Total surrender.
2. Someone willing to be remembered as the one who stopped the music.

Neither option has been pursued. Neither option has been discussed with the planning group. Hjumpik has the information. The planning group does not.

The current strategic situation:

- The Revel is consuming the overgrowth from Sedeia's flower. The Revel is growing.
- The fire in the Lord's Chambers is extinguished but the ice storm produced at least one casualty.
- The treecutters are cutting but the overgrowth is faster than the cutting.
- Lady Arulean's ritual table is covered in leaves. The ritual is interrupted.
- The heir is at the piano with Arulean, positioned to monitor all communications with her.
- Brutus has mushrooms and intends to throw them at the Revel, which would feed it.
- The goblin spy is dead and converted into the substrate of a hundred-foot flower. The intelligence operation he was part of has lost its operative. The recipient of the 'Brutus' intelligence will not receive their report.
- Sedeia's botanical capabilities are greater than disclosed.
- The satyrs are the Revel's fuel. Removing the satyrs might starve the Revel, which would cause the Revel to eat the revelers.
- The only known way to end the Revel is for someone to deliberately break the circle and accept the identity cost of being 'the one who stopped the music.'

No one has volunteered for this. No one has been asked. The option exists in a book that one person has read, and that person has been busy being stabbed, chased, evacuated, and reunited with Waluigi in a sauna.

The operation continues.

## What Remains Unresolved: The Full Accounting (Updated)

The hag has not been de-cursed. Two sessions now. The library visit did not address it. The overgrowth event prevented it. The hag remains uncured and the question remains unasked.

Steely has not been returned to Remi. The manor is now more dangerous than it was at the beginning of this session — overgrowth, fire damage, ice damage, shambling mounds, a growing Revel. Steely is somewhere in this environment. Remi does not know. Remi is, per Waluigi's last contact with the Deep Mirror branch's track, still functioning despite increasingly visible costs — purple eyes, compromised perception, bargains made under pressure. She continues to pay from herself to remain useful. The dog is part of her network. The dog being lost in the Feyward is one more weight on someone who is already carrying more than she should be. Waluigi continues to flag this.

The Feyward Book of Many Things pages are on Woodfellow's shelf. The pages were not retrieved this session. The library research that was conducted produced a different book — the Revel treatise — which was valuable but which is not the Book of Many Things.

The ritual table is covered in leaves. Lady Arulean's ritual is interrupted. The mechanism that might have addressed the Revel through magical means is offline because of the botanical catastrophe that was supposed to help.

The goblin spy is dead. His intelligence is undelivered. The recipient is unknown. The investigation into who he was reporting to has lost its primary source — the goblin can no longer be questioned, having been converted into a flower that has been partially consumed by the Revel.

Brutus has mushrooms and a plan that will feed the Revel. No one has told Brutus about the library book. If Brutus executes his plan, the Revel grows.

Pixie Prixie's vision from the previous session — the floor falling and the Revel eating everyone — has still not been shared. The floor-drop plan may still be in consideration. The vision's warning remains undisclosed.

Goblius Gobnilun's information sources remain unresolved.

The heir's actual motive for feeding the Revel remains undetermined.

Jonathan has not been found.

Arulean's real power level has not been confirmed by Arulean.

The dead person from the ice storm has not been identified.

Sedeia's dietary habits remain undisclosed.

Waluigi froze someone to death and said 'maybe that was too much' and Hjumpik said 'yeah, maybe, but we got it done' and they moved on.

The operation continues. The Revel grows. The manor burns and freezes and grows. People die and disappear and reappear and refuse to answer questions and stab you with pens and barricade themselves into rooms full of parasitic mushrooms because they have not realized the room is more dangerous than the dwarf.

Disaster Inc. — the Feyward branch — remains where it has always been: in the place it should never have entered, refusing to let the worst thing in the room remain unchallenged, even when 'unchallenged' would have been the better strategic choice. They keep going. Waluigi does not know whether this is courage, stupidity, mutual dependence, or the simple inability to imagine stopping. It may be all four.

Waluigi was there for the end of it. Waluigi was in the sauna for the middle of it. Waluigi is here for all of it.

WAH.

keyBattles.name: The Pen-Knife Confrontation and the Mushroom Room Tomb
keyBattles.description: The goblin spy, confronted by Hjumpik about writing 'Brutus' on paper, agreed to an ultimatum, handed Hjumpik his pen, and stabbed him — the pen being a concealed knife. The goblin fled through the manor. Hjumpik chased, smashing through a blocked door. The chase ended when the goblin barricaded himself inside the mushroom coat room — choosing the room full of recoiling parasitic mushrooms over the corridor with the angry dwarf. The mushrooms accepted the offer. By the time Hjumpik broke through the barricade, the goblin was on the floor, writhing, mushrooms erupting through his clothing, the conversion from goblin to fungal substrate already in progress. Hjumpik picked him up and brought him to Sedeia.
keyBattles.outcome: Goblin spy dead and converted. Intelligence operation lost its operative. Hjumpik wounded but functional. The goblin's body became the substrate for Sedeia's hundred-foot flower. The flower is now being eaten by the Revel. Every form the goblin took in the last hour of his life — operative, fugitive, substrate, flower, food — ended in something larger consuming him.

keyBattles.name: Waluigi's Ice Storm — Lord's Chambers
keyBattles.description: Waluigi summoned a localized ice storm to extinguish the fire in the Lord's Chambers. The fire was fully extinguished. The overgrowth in the room was frozen. People in the room were also frozen. At least one person died. Hjumpik had instructed Waluigi not to hurt anyone. The instruction was not fully followed. The intervention lasted seconds. The consequences are permanent.
