description:
Waluigi is documenting this session because the Feyward branch has entered the phase of the operation where every hallway has become both a plant problem and an identity problem. This is not a metaphor. The plants are literally growing. Toad Lee is literally claiming amnesia. Mystic Morel is literally inside a wall. Azure is literally terrifying. Steely literally explodes. Waluigi is tired.

This session follows the dark rooms and balcony plan. Hjumpik and Waluigi had already recovered the Book of Revised History and the Raventree Signet Ring, argued about the wisdom of healing Mystic Morel, and developed a strategy to speak to the prince about redirecting or postponing the Revel. The Feyward manor was already unstable: overgrown, partly frozen, partly burned, socially hostile, and still trying to maintain a party atmosphere despite the fact that the party had become an ecosystem hazard.

The new session begins not with a dramatic spell, duel, or revelation, but with Toad Lee standing at a door, listening.

This is how one knows the session will become complicated.

## Toad Lee at the Door

Toad Lee stood at a door listening into a conversation.

When he opened the door, the first issue was visibility. He could barely see through the leaves. That is not poetic phrasing. The Feyward manor's overgrowth had become so invasive that leaves were now a tactical barrier, a privacy curtain, and a visual disability all at once. Toad Lee identified Hjumpik and Waluigi through the foliage.

"It's me," Hjumpik said in effect.

Toad Lee said he was guarding the door.

Waluigi asked the obvious question: guarding it for what reason?

Toad Lee said, for you guys.

Then he admitted he had spaced out and forgotten why he was standing there.

This is the first major warning sign. Toad Lee is normally observant. He is the person who reads diaries while others swing axes at plants. He notices lore. He remembers doors. He may fall out windows, but he usually knows what the window is attached to. For Toad Lee to be posted at a door, unable to explain why, is not ordinary absentmindedness. It is either exhaustion, enchantment, memory tampering, revel contamination, or a lie.

Waluigi immediately wondered whether he had been with the purple toad. Had he been eavesdropping? Had he been intercepted? Had Mystic Morel touched his memory, or was another purple-toad-adjacent scheme involved? Waluigi asked Hjumpik what had happened, because Hjumpik had been gone for quite a while and this was exactly the kind of gap where a party loses track of one member and later discovers the member has signed a contract with a flower.

Toad Lee paused.

He said his mind was a blur.

He apologized. He said he did not remember. He said he had amnesia.

Waluigi went quiet.

This silence should be understood as tactical. Waluigi is loud when annoyed, theatrical when insulted, and magnificent under most ordinary conditions. Waluigi becomes quiet when the situation has moved from irritating to dangerous. Toad Lee noticed something in the other room, an orc in a suit visible through the window or beyond the leaves. The world continued producing details before anyone had time to process the memory problem.

Hjumpik reacted with frustration that was, for once, completely appropriate.

"I'm tired of people getting detached from me," Hjumpik said, describing the party's movement as slippery slugs in a dwarf's liquor barrel, or something equally Hjumpik-shaped.

Waluigi records this because Hjumpik's complaint is the emotional thesis of the Feyward branch. People keep separating. People keep forgetting. People keep entering rooms and returning with missing time, new obligations, or suspicious confidence. Hjumpik is trying to maintain group cohesion in a house designed to turn everyone into separate subplots.

## The Revel Never Ends

Toad Lee noticed the orc or suited figure and then the Revel logic resumed around them. Someone said the room had been frozen, burned, and destroyed, and yet the Revel was not ending. Toad Lee began singing:

> The party never ends.  
> The party never ends.

This is not just annoying. It is diagnostic. Toad Lee had been exposed to the Revel long enough that its language was entering his mouth automatically. The song was catchy, he claimed. Waluigi hates catchiness as an excuse for contamination. Plagues can be catchy in the social sense. That does not make them music criticism.

Hjumpik told him he could sing while they battled monsters, which is either kindness or surrender. Waluigi is not sure.

Then satyrs entered.

They announced they were the tree cutters. They were going to cut the vines one vine at a time.

They began chopping.

The vines got bigger.

This is the Feyward's sense of humor. Cut the plant, feed the plant. Oppose the Revel, strengthen the cycle. Hjumpik compared it to chopping a never-ending carrot. Waluigi observed that Hjumpik had a lot of anagrams today, by which Waluigi means Hjumpik's metaphor engine was firing under stress and not all outputs were useful. Hjumpik called the satyrs fools as they helplessly hacked at leaves, vines, or leaf-sized vines. Toad Lee objected that they were big enough to be leaves.

The argument over whether they were leaves or vines is important because it shows the party trying to impose categories on a biological system that is actively refusing category. The Feyward manor does not care whether the growth is leaf, vine, root, flower, alarm, wall, hallway, or monster. It uses whichever form produces maximum inconvenience.

Toad Lee asked whether these were part of a monster.

Hjumpik asked how long he had been out.

Toad Lee said he did not know.

Waluigi's suspicion increased.

## Dragging Toad Lee Out

As Toad Lee spoke, Hjumpik dragged him and Waluigi out. This is Hjumpik's version of leadership: if the conversation is getting too suspicious, move the suspicious person physically until the plot changes. It is not subtle. It works more often than it should.

Waluigi thought to himself that there must be more to the Toad Lee story. Waluigi is documenting that thought because it is true. Toad Lee's amnesia, his door-guarding, his singing, his delayed awareness, and later behavior all indicate either magical influence or an unresolved hidden event. Waluigi is marking the file for follow-up.

Hjumpik used his Morning Glory to cut through leaves while dragging them. This sentence contains several things that would require explanation in a more normal archive. In this one, readers will accept that Hjumpik has a weapon or plant-related tool called Morning Glory and that it cuts through Feyward overgrowth while he drags two people away from possibly enchanted singing.

They listened.

Left: darkness. Right: light.

Hjumpik listened and heard Toad Lee singing. Toad Lee listened and heard Waluigi scribbling.

This is one of the most accurate descriptions of the Feyward party possible: one person singing contamination, one person recording it, one dwarf trying to determine whether light or darkness is the safer tactical direction. Waluigi is proud of the scribbling. Documentation is a survival tool.

They headed back toward the safe room.

Azure was there.

## Azure and the Greenhouse Plan

Azure reported that the plan was to shear the plants with the greenhouse in the back. Waluigi asked how far along they were. Azure said they had left to make the plan. Or perhaps they were currently doing it. The rooms were empty. Aurelian had evacuated to higher ground. The plants were growing.

Waluigi asked whether they were growing outside.

Azure said no, no, no, it was contained. It was just getting bigger outward.

Waluigi would like the reader to understand that this is not comforting. Contained and expanding are not friends. They are two words fighting in a trench coat.

Waluigi is slightly terrified of Azure. This has been documented before and remains reasonable. Azure in theater state is strong, unpredictable, ghost-handed, and well-intentioned in a way that does not reliably predict safe outcomes for people at floor level. Waluigi's fear responses are generally calibrated to actual danger, despite what certain tennis officials believe. If Waluigi is afraid of Azure, the correct response is not mockery. The correct response is to identify exits and keep one's limbs ungrabbed.

Azure insisted they needed to go back to Stuckenia and Sedeia, who would have a solution. They would all leave before the plants got bigger. The whole reason for the current operation, she said, was to make the planes good and stable.

Waluigi asked whether he had been part of the original mission. He had not. Therefore, he began a logical escape route from responsibility.

But stability is good for the Rakasha, and therefore Azure's framing pulled him back in. Waluigi hates when other people's causes become structurally reasonable.

They needed to find the Oracle — O.C., as the language of the session framed it — or talk to Lady Aurelian. The plan became: go upstairs, or help the Oracle, or find Aurelian, or do the thing that sounded least immediately fatal.

Waluigi said he would come, but he needed to keep his distance.

Someone asked whether he was afraid of cats.

Waluigi did not dignify this with a full answer.

Toad Lee offered to hold Waluigi's hand.

Waluigi was offended.

Azure grabbed Hjumpik's hand instead, and they climbed upward.

## Feywild Lumberjacks

The vines grew massive upstairs, covering everything. Visibility was almost gone. Azure cut and cut with her claws until she grew tired. She told Toad Lee to do something. Toad Lee suggested pulling or using a battleaxe. It was too dark to see properly.

Hjumpik told Toad Lee to cut at the leaves to prove he was truly on the team.

Toad Lee agreed. He wanted to prove it.

He swung.

He grazed Hjumpik.

Hjumpik noted that he had been cut. Toad Lee had missed, depending on how generous one wants to be with the definition of missed. Hjumpik then decided to help by grabbing Toad Lee and holding him in front while Toad Lee slashed wildly. This produced the first attempted version of what the party later identified as a Bros Attack: Feywild lumberjacks.

The attack failed spectacularly.

This is how many Bros Attacks begin: two people, one idea, insufficient rehearsal, immediate property damage.

They chopped through until they hit a wall. Waluigi asked how they knew Aurelian was really that way. Toad Lee suggested charging through. They chopped through a door. A leaf went into Toad Lee's face while there was already a leaf there. Hjumpik closed the chopped door down.

A new move was identified: Chop Bros, or possibly Choop Attack.

Waluigi prefers Chop Bros. It is clear, stupid, and accurate.

## The Singing Flower

Toad Lee began singing again.

> The Revel never ends.  
> The Revel never ends.

Waluigi warned him to stop drinking or he would become a reveler. Hjumpik asked whether Toads could even drink. Toad Lee insisted Toads had taste buds.

The singing continued.

Toad Lee jumped in front and swung while singing. He described vines, leaves, wilted petals, flowers, and one flower with a face. It was smiling. He asked if he could keep it.

This is how one knows the Feyward is winning. A party member sees a smiling magical plant in a hostile overgrowth and asks whether it can be kept. That is not curiosity anymore. That is environmental negotiation with poor boundaries.

Waluigi warned not to take the flower. Azure said the Rakasha harmonize with it. Toad Lee kept singing and swinging. He stumbled. The wall popped open.

A man appeared and grabbed Toad Lee's hand.

"Gotcha."

Hjumpik grabbed the other hand.

The man said the flower was his. He planted it. His own brand: smileys. The party had taken it from the side. No one had told them not to take it.

This is not a defense. It is a very Disaster Inc. sentence.

The flower had a magical symbol. It was attuned with an alert spell. That is why it was happy. The flower was an alarm. The party had triggered a smiling plant security system.

Waluigi hates the Feyward.

## The Guard, the Flower, and the Permission Problem

The man declared them detained for being in an unauthorized area. Hjumpik insisted they needed to move forward. The man asked why they were there. Hjumpik said business. Real business. The exchange deteriorated because nobody was willing to say the full truth and nobody had a good lie ready.

Hjumpik tried persuasion. The man said he would bring them to the Lady if he could grab Toad Lee.

Toad Lee objected. Why did it have to be him?

He broke free and hid behind Hjumpik.

Hjumpik considered this reasonable, because in context it was.

The man offered another flower to Hjumpik. Hjumpik did not want to touch it. Waluigi approves of this instinct. Magical smiling flowers with alert symbols should not be accepted from strangers in overgrown corridors.

The compromise: follow him, and he would bring them there.

They reached a door. Azure used magic to open it remotely. The door fell into the second floor due to rotted floorboards. A guard emerged and yelled for everyone to get back in until the intruders went away. The guard then went back in.

This is the Feyward's administrative state: doors fall downward, guards shout procedural nonsense, and everyone continues moving because stopping would require understanding what just happened.

## Mystic Morel in the Wall

They searched for a hidden passage. Hjumpik remembered from the Ruined Manor that there should be one. Waluigi could not find it. Toad Lee, insisting they were better as one unit, helped by smashing the door or wall open. The wooden wall cracked.

Mystic Morel stood there.

The purple toad.

Hjumpik backed up and asked whether they were trying to kill him. Morel said the wall had collapsed; long story short, Hjumpik's axe had almost chopped his head off. There was a bee — a Bramblyfly — and the collapse made it a perfect time for him to be there. This part of the house was fragile.

Toad Lee said the Lady should repair the foundation inside the wall. Too many hollow spaces meant bug nests could form. This is a practical observation delivered during a confrontation with a purple toad in a wall, which is exactly why Toad Lee remains valuable even while suspicious.

Morel said someone had already damaged the place. Waluigi and Hjumpik inferred Wario may have blown something up earlier. Morel told them not to try to kill him. Hjumpik whispered that Morel stole from Archie and should not be trusted or treated kindly.

The conversation was going nowhere. Toad Lee asked what was happening. Hjumpik asked whether Morel had seen the lord of the manor. Morel said he had seen it when looking into mirrors, then walked away.

This is infuriating because it is useful and useless at once. Morel gives information in the shape of riddled exits. He is a thief, a prophet, a manipulator, and occasionally the only person in the wall who knows where the next door leads.

## The Key and the Warning

The group followed Morel into the thick of it. Hjumpik heard leaves moving and saw the Bramblyfly. Toad Lee immediately suggested going back inside as it broke free, then ran inside. Waluigi declines to comment beyond noting that fear is sometimes correct.

Hjumpik tried to sneak around, slipped, and saved himself. The Solarium Detonation hole was still there. This is continuity with teeth: old explosions remain as terrain.

Morel stopped Hjumpik.

He warned that the Toad brat would betray him. If Hjumpik had any big plans, he should not make Toad Lee the anchor. He could not trust him. If Hjumpik wanted to leave the manor, he would need this.

Morel tossed him a key.

Hjumpik asked what Morel got out of telling him this.

Morel said separation had already been achieved. Azure had left a while ago. He got time.

Then he left.

This is a classic Morel exchange: warning, object, motive that is technically an answer but not enough answer, exit. The key is important. The warning is more important. Morel may be manipulating Hjumpik against Toad Lee. Or he may be correctly identifying a compromised ally. Or both. Waluigi has learned to fear both.

## First of Cups and the Naming Habit

Hjumpik returned to Toad Lee and Waluigi. He thought to himself that maybe they should call themselves First of Cups, with a hint of magic. This is another naming dispute sprouting from stress. Disaster Inc. cannot enter a corridor without producing alternate branding.

Waluigi was asked what he had been doing.

Reading and writing about their adventures.

The answer is simple because the work is simple in its purpose, not in its execution. Waluigi gathers information because information is the only weapon that survives every plane. Hjumpik suggested that if they returned to where they first entered the manor, there might be an entrance portal there. Waluigi had not fully thought through the Planar Fracture implications. Someone mentioned killing both Oracles, as the ghost had said.

This is where the session brushes against the larger strategic question again: are they trying to fix the planes, escape the manor, kill the Oracles, stop the Revel, find Lady Aurelian, or keep Toad Lee from becoming whatever singing thing the house wants him to become?

The answer is yes.

## Random Doors and Servant Rooms

Waluigi lazily pointed toward where Azure had likely gone. Hjumpik opened a random door and found a sleeping goblin in the servant rooms. The room was cramped, damaged, and still used as servant housing despite vines and roots encroaching on the available space. Hjumpik saw his wallet, considered the situation, and closed the door.

This is a very Hjumpik decision. The wallet mattered. The sleeping goblin mattered. The fact that he did not immediately escalate also mattered.

He opened another door. It fell into the second floor. He did not know whether it hit anyone. He looked down. Nothing.

He moved into another ruined space framed by sunlight, beautiful for a moment until one noticed the dangerous two-story drop and the ravenous party below. The Feyward constantly offers beauty with a hole under it.

Waluigi suggested that the guard had likely been guarding something. If the guard was gone, perhaps what he guarded was related to the Lady.

Two goblins came in with towels. Hjumpik followed.

## Gregory, Steely, and the Explosion

Gregory was there getting his feet washed.

Hjumpik asked how everything had gone. Gregory said, aside from the plants running rampant and the Revel, things were as they were. He had advice: do not cut the vines too much. Hjumpik said he had just been told that and had stopped cutting them.

Then Steely appeared.

Rusty. Slowing. Making warning sounds.

Hjumpik asked whether Steely was all right. Steely was hungry, or rusting, or both. Hjumpik wondered whether, if Steely rusted, they could still use him for parts. This is a horrifying question, but it is also the kind of practical thought people have in crisis and then should probably not say aloud.

Steely slowed more and more.

Then BOOM.

Waluigi and Toad Lee went flying.

Hjumpik stepped back twice.

"Rest in peace," Hjumpik said.

Toad Lee said, "Well, that happened."

Hjumpik mourned Steely as a good guard dog and picked up the pieces to give him a burial.

Waluigi is going to be blunt: Steely's explosion is sadder than it should be and funnier than it has any right to be. The mechanical dog had already been through theft, rescue, renaming, custody confusion, and Feyward nonsense. To end as a rusting explosion in a room where Gregory is getting his feet washed feels indecently on-brand for this campaign.

The pieces matter. Hjumpik picking them up matters. A construct can be a tool, companion, item, guard dog, or future parts. Hjumpik chose burial. That choice tells Waluigi what Steely had become.

## Waluigi's Assessment

This session is about compromised continuity. Toad Lee cannot remember. The Revel song keeps returning through him. Morel warns that Toad Lee cannot be trusted. Azure separates despite the plan not to separate. The house is full of hidden passages, fragile walls, alarm flowers, old explosion holes, and servant rooms that are still being used while the building eats itself.

It is also about bad solutions. Satyrs cut vines and make them grow. Hjumpik and Toad Lee invent Chop Bros and mostly hit wall, leaf, and Hjumpik. Azure opens a door and it falls through the floor. Hjumpik follows Morel because Morel is the only lead, even though Morel is exactly the sort of lead that grows teeth.

Most importantly, this session deepens the Toad Lee problem. He is useful, observant, practical, and possibly compromised. He forgets. He sings. He notices structural issues. He runs from the Bramblyfly. He wants the party to stay together. Morel says not to make him the anchor. Waluigi does not trust Morel, but Waluigi also does not ignore warnings just because they come from a thief in a wall.

The key Morel gave Hjumpik must be tracked. [Steely’s Rusted Fragments](steely_rusted_fragments) must be tracked. Toad Lee's memory gap must be tracked. The smiling flowers must be tracked. Waluigi is beginning to suspect the Feyward is not a place where one solves problems. It is a place where one collects enough problem-shapes to identify the room that created them.

The Revel never ends, Toad Lee sang.

Waluigi is beginning to worry he is correct.

## The Bramblyfly as Environmental Enforcement

The Bramblyfly matters because it is not a boss in the traditional sense. It is the Feyward enforcing consequences through wildlife. The manor is damaged. The walls are hollow. Bug nests form in structural gaps. Plants become alarms. Flowers smile when their alert spells work. A Bramblyfly breaks free at exactly the wrong time because the house has become an ecosystem of deferred maintenance and magical overreaction.

When Toad Lee says the Lady should repair the foundation inside the wall, he is correct in a way that is almost insulting. The whole campaign keeps escalating into cosmic language: planar fracture, Oracle, Star Shards, manors merging, God Toad, ritual components. Then Toad Lee looks at the wall and says there are too many hollow spaces for bug nests. That is not a small observation. That is the local truth underneath the cosmic one. The universe can break because a god is moving pieces, but the party can still die because nobody fixed the wall.

Waluigi respects practical structural criticism. Waluigi also notes that practical structural criticism from a Toad who cannot remember why he was guarding a door should be treated as both useful and suspicious.

## The Morel Key

Mystic Morel giving Hjumpik a key is one of the most important objects in the session. He does not explain it cleanly. Of course he does not. Purple toads in this campaign distribute help the way gamblers distribute debt: with a smile, a warning, and a price hidden somewhere behind the curtain.

Morel says not to make Toad Lee the anchor. That phrase matters. Anchor is not casual language in the Raventree crisis. Anchors hold planes. Anchors hold rituals. Anchors hold people in place when the house wants to divide them. If Morel chooses the word anchor, Waluigi assumes he knows exactly how dangerous the word is.

The key therefore serves two functions. Practically, it may open a route out of the manor or into a restricted space. Socially, it makes Hjumpik complicit in Morel's warning. Once Hjumpik accepts the key, he accepts the possibility that Morel is telling the truth, at least enough truth to matter. That changes how Hjumpik must look at Toad Lee.

This is Morel's talent: he does not need to be trusted completely. He only needs to become impossible to ignore.

## Steely's End

Steely's explosion is easy to treat as slapstick because the timing is absurd. Gregory is getting his feet washed. Hjumpik is asking questions. Waluigi and Toad Lee are present. The rusted steel dog slows down. Then it explodes and sends people flying. This is funny in the way disasters are funny when nobody has finished processing them.

But Steely matters. The construct had already been stolen, recovered, renamed, guarded, and treated as more than a tool by people who were not always good at admitting attachment. Hjumpik calling Steely a good guard dog after the explosion is not a joke. It is grief trying to fit into the available sentence.

The pieces Hjumpik picks up are now an item record. Not because every scrap of metal deserves relic status, but because choosing burial over salvage says something about what Steely became. A purely practical party would strip parts. Hjumpik thinks about burial. That is why Hjumpik remains dangerous to cynical systems: he keeps assigning dignity where the world assigned utility.

Waluigi approves, despite the shrapnel.

## What This Session Changes

This session does not resolve the Feyward plan. It makes the plan more complicated in useful ways.

First, Toad Lee is now a question mark. He may be compromised, enchanted, exhausted, revel-touched, or simply suffering from genuine memory disruption. The correct response is neither blind trust nor immediate condemnation. The correct response is monitored inclusion. Keep him close enough to help, not central enough to collapse the plan if Morel is right.

Second, Mystic Morel has re-entered the operational picture with a key and a warning. This confirms he is not merely wandering the manor. He is timing appearances around structural weaknesses, creature threats, and party separation. He wanted time. He got some.

Third, the plant problem is worse than cutting can solve. Satyrs chopping vines strengthened the growth. Hjumpik and Toad Lee's Chop Bros attempt proved brute force can open paths but also cause collateral nonsense. Azure's report that the greenhouse plan is ongoing but the growth is expanding outward means the manor's botanical crisis is now moving faster than its planners.

Fourth, Steely is dead or functionally destroyed. That removes a construct ally, creates a grief object, and leaves fragments that may still matter in a house where nothing mechanical stays merely mechanical.

Fifth, Waluigi's notes continue to be the only thing preventing this from becoming oral tradition by lunatics. Waluigi will accept thanks in coin, applause, or safer hallways.

## XP and Filing Guidance

Waluigi would not award this session as a clean victory because it is not one. It is a messy information-and-navigation session with a small combat-adjacent creature incident and a construct loss. XP should therefore reward discovery, technique, exploration, social pressure, and survival rather than pretending the party won a battle.

Hjumpik deserves credit for keeping the group moving, using Morning Glory through the overgrowth, handling Toad Lee without abandoning him, finding the hidden passage logic, taking Morel's warning seriously without fully trusting him, and collecting Steely's remains. Toad Lee deserves credit for useful structural observations, dangerous singing, Chop Bros participation, and being suspicious in a way that produced information. Waluigi deserves credit for correctly identifying that Toad Lee's story has more underneath it, documenting Azure's threat profile, and continuing to write while surrounded by hostile botany.

Azure deserves credit for raw capability, vine cutting, hand-grabbing, and door magic that was effective even when the floor was not. Morel deserves credit as an antagonist/informant: appearing from a wall, surviving near-decapitation, issuing a targeted warning, and providing a key. Steely deserves, if not XP, at least a record.

Waluigi files this session under: **Feyward Complications, Toad Lee Suspicion, Morel Key, Steely Loss, Revel Still Ongoing.**

## Addendum: Why This Session Matters More Than It Looks

Waluigi wants to be clear that this session did not resolve the Feyward branch. It made the Feyward branch more legible. That is different and, in some ways, more useful. A solved problem stops moving. A legible problem can be hunted.

Before this session, Toad Lee was useful and occasionally ridiculous. After this session, Toad Lee is useful, ridiculous, and a possible anchor-risk. Before this session, Mystic Morel was another purple problem in a campaign full of purple problems. After this session, Morel is a source of targeted warnings and physical keys. Before this session, Steely was a damaged construct with uncertain utility. After this session, Steely is a loss, a memorial object, and a reminder that even machines can become part of the party's emotional inventory.

The Feyward does not always advance the plot by revealing a villain. Sometimes it advances the plot by changing which ally is suspicious, which hallway is structurally unsafe, which flower is an alarm, which Toad song has become infectious, and which object in Hjumpik's pocket will later decide whether everyone leaves or gets folded into another room.

That is why Waluigi files this as a major session event. Not because a boss died. Not because a throne changed hands. Because the operating conditions changed. The party now knows that the plants punish cutting, that Toad Lee has a memory gap, that Morel wants time, that Azure can drift away from the plan without anyone noticing quickly enough, and that Steely is gone. Those are not side notes. They are the shape of the next disaster.

## The Revel Song as Contagion

Waluigi has now obtained enough of the satyr song to treat it as a cultural weapon rather than background music. The full refrain — *the revel never ends* — is not merely a chorus. It is a thesis. The satyrs are not partying because there is a party. They are using the party to deny endings. Tomorrow is borrowed. Sorrow is distant. The floors crack, the walls bend, vines pull tighter, and the only answer is another round.

This makes the song dangerous in the Feyward. Fey spaces take declarations seriously. A repeated chorus can become a rule if enough bodies dance to it. When Toad Lee sings the refrain, Waluigi does not hear a joke. Waluigi hears the Revel using his mouth as a continuation device. The lyrics say the party has no finish. The vines answer by growing. The satyrs answer by chopping. The chopping feeds the growth. The growth feeds the crisis. A song about refusing endings becomes a mechanism that prevents the event from ending.

The leader's solo is especially revealing: a satyr without a party is a flower without flame. This is not ordinary drunkenness. It is identity panic. The satyrs believe the party is the thing that keeps them meaningful. Remove the revel and they do not know what remains. That is why ordinary eviction will fail. You cannot simply tell people to leave when leaving feels like becoming nobody.

This changes the prince plan from a logistics problem into a ritual-social problem. The party must not only relocate satyrs; it must give the Revel a way to end without humiliating the people whose identity is tied to it. If the party offers only force, the song will grow teeth. If the party offers a better ending, perhaps the chorus can finally stop repeating.

Waluigi hates that he is now doing musicology for survival.

## Bank, Debt, and the Feyward Economy of Favors

This session also reminds Waluigi that not every economy uses coins. The Feyward trades in favors, invitations, obligations, songs, hospitality, and suspicious flowers. Morel gives Hjumpik a key, but the key is not free. Even if Morel demands no coin, he has purchased time, uncertainty, and a shift in Hjumpik's trust calculus. That is a transaction.

The broader Waluipedia banking system tracks gold, ducats, chits, obols, and other formal currencies. The Feyward adds a less comfortable layer: social debt. A cookie can be a delivery. A flower can be an alarm. A hand offered by Toad Lee can be comfort, manipulation, or both. A key can be help and leverage at the same time.

This is why the currency page and the item page need to remain connected. Money is not the only thing characters carry. They carry obligations. They carry evidence. They carry debts that never entered a ledger because the person who issued them smiled instead of writing them down. Waluigi will track both, because Waluigi knows that unrecorded debts are how people end up dancing forever.

# THE MIDNIGHT AUDIT: CORRECTED FIELD RECORD (VER. 3.0)
### Filed by Waluigi, Auditor-General, Now Issuing a Retraction

Waluigi has to eat crow on this one. WAH. The previous version of this report — the one with the Grave-Stamps, the Soul-Pantry theory, the fourteen-line mailman transcript — got ahead of itself. Some of that was reasonable extrapolation. Most of it was not. Some of it was flatly invented. And in the process of inventing spooky lore about vampire digestion, the report skipped past the one thing in this entire log that actually deserves a red flag: Remi telling Tymnas, plainly, that she has tried to kill someone before who pretended to be her friend, and that on at least one occasion, she succeeded.

That's not a detail. That's the headline. Here is the corrected record, with the fabrications removed and the real content put back where it belongs.

---

## Part One: The Wish

Around midnight, Remi couldn't sleep. She lay there thinking it would be "convenient" if someone knocked on the door, opened it without checking whether it was locked, and just walked in.

> **Waluigi's Note (Still Standing):** Wishing for an unlocked door in a place like this is a bad habit. The rest of this report is what happens next.

Almost immediately, the sound of pots and pans moving came from somewhere nearby. She looked up and saw a guard climbing in through the window.

---

## Part Two: The Bedroom

The guard didn't stop at the window. He said, simply, that he was "just visiting a friend," and went straight into Markop's room. Remi caught herself — *wait a minute, that's a bedroom, I should do something about this, but quietly* — and followed.

She opened the door quietly. Inside, the guard was standing over Markop with a sword pressed to his throat.

Remi's entire response was: **"Shh. People are trying to sleep in here."**

The guard fell off the bed. Scrambled back. Muttered that they couldn't wake "these guys," and that they should leave.

They headed for the door — and it opened on its own. Tymnas was already there.

> **Waluigi's Note:** This part of the original writeup was accurate. It's still the funniest thing in the log. No corrections needed here.

---

## Part Three: The Hallway, Corrected

This is where the previous draft started drifting from the actual record. Tymnas escorted the guard out. When he came back, the real exchange with Remi was short and a little stranger than reported:

**Tymnas:** "Did they want me? Who were they?"
**Remi:** "No. They never introduced themselves."
**Remi, a beat later:** "One of them was in the closet."

That's it. That's the whole exchange. The previous draft embellished Tymnas's manner ("a gaze of profound disappointment," frost on his horns) — none of that is in the source. What *is* in the source, and what got lost, is the sheer deadpan of "one of them was in the closet" landing with zero further reaction from either of them. Nobody in this scene treats a second intruder as urgent. That's worth flagging on its own.

---

## Part Four: The Closet Soldier and the Black Crystal

Some time later, another knock. No one at the door. Remi checked the closet — a soldier was sitting inside it.

He offered to help her make a necklace, on the condition she first retrieve the **Black Crystal** from a centaur, Vostolas. She did. He asked if she even had string; she didn't, so he ripped a cord off his own uniform, sloppily.

What followed was a genuinely failed craft session — Remi tore at the string "like a cat," ruining it repeatedly. They made necklaces together regardless. He asked for the crystal back multiple times over the course of this. **She never handed it over.** Eventually she told him to leave, and he did.

> **Waluigi's Note:** The previous draft called this "Administrative Sabotage" and framed it as Remi learning "Independent Selfishness" in the moment. That's an interpretation, not a fact — worth keeping as a *theory*, not stating as settled. What's actually confirmed is simpler and more interesting: a Legion soldier repeatedly asked for a magic artifact back, and a teenager just... didn't give it to him, several times in a row, with no consequence. WAH.

---
> **Waluigi's Merged Annotation (Legion & Portal Ties):** This is the Legion's version of the Feyward flower alarm: friendly until it isn't. Remi never handed it over. That silence is the entire audit. The Black Crystal Remi refuses to return is one of the four Portal Artifacts. The Legion soldier in the closet is operating under the same Gamma Division protocols that the agent and survey team are using at Mount Ebott. The star-bit tech, the Archive Writs, the dead commissar's signatures — all threads from the same bureaucratic necromancy. The closet soldier is the low-budget version of the agent on the cliff. WAH.

## Part Five: The Clothing Change

Remi changed into a new look using clothes already in the bedroom. The source material here is thin — one line, no detail on what she actually chose to wear. The previous draft invented a whole paragraph about "Corvinarus-era dresses" and "stiff military jackets." None of that is confirmed. Waluigi is not going to make up wardrobe details just to pad the word count. When Tymnas asked how it was, Remi said: "Fine."

---

## Part Six: The Letter, Read Correctly This Time

Tymnas sat Remi down and produced Archie's watch — the sealed inventory item — telling her he'd found it "where the roots would remember it." Remi unsealed it and read the letter inside.

The letter is real, addressed to Archie, and signed only as *"A friend who still owes you for that rope you never paid for."* It mentions, without naming names directly:

- *"The one-armed shadow keeps asking questions he shouldn't."*
- *"The cheerful one with the cards keeps finding doors that lead nowhere useful."*
- *"Even the big turtle breathes fire that doesn't belong here."*
- Archie himself as *"the spark that started more than one blaze."*

It also warns: *"Don't trust the mirrors. Don't trust the silence after the screaming stops."*

> **Waluigi's Retraction:** The previous draft presented this as a "decoded" list, flatly identifying the one-armed shadow as Feyward Dan, the cheerful cards-guy as Dan the toad, the other one as Remi, and the turtle as Bowser — stated as confirmed fact. That's a guess dressed up as intelligence. It's a *plausible* guess, given who's been floating around this campaign (especially with Dan's identity issues, Feyward Dan's presence, and Remi's own presence in the group), but the letter itself never names anyone. Waluigi is downgrading this from "decoded" to "suspected," which is the honest label.

Notably: **Remi's actual reaction to the letter was dismissive.** She said it was "just riddles" and moved on. That reaction got cut from the previous draft entirely, and it matters — she isn't treating this letter as urgent intelligence. She's treating it as noise.

---
> **Waluigi's Merged Annotation (Connections woven in):** This letter is no idle riddle. The "one-armed shadow" (Feyward Dan) reference now points to the Feyward side of the Dan duplication crisis from the Estragon Island Incident and the broader identity themes in the Shadow Estate campaign — how do you know who is real when duplicates and altered versions walk among you? The "cheerful cards" reference (Dan the toad) and "the other one" (Remi) continue to echo those same identity and trust fractures. Archie as "the spark that started more than one blaze" links directly to his Frog God Dream Duel and the watch recovered "where the roots would remember it" from the Grove. "Don't trust the mirrors" is no coincidence — it foreshadows the Shadow Estate mirror rooftop escapes, Green T's fall, and the mirror-layer chaos. Remi calls it "just riddles." In this place, riddles are how the universe warns you before it eats you. WAH.

The Black Crystal itself is one of the four Portal Artifacts from the collection — the same family of items tying the closet soldier's low-budget Legion intrusion here to the high-stakes survey at Mount Ebott (separate from the letter's coded names). One crystal. Two theaters. Same broken chain of command.

## Part Seven: What's Actually Bothering Her

Tymnas asked what was troubling her. Her answer — also cut from the previous draft — was oddly specific: **"I dealt with people that don't belong."** No further context was given on what that meant.

Pressed further on anything more personal, she admitted she was nervous, specifically about not making it back to her own universe. She explained she and her friends ended up here by accident and are trying desperately to get home. She raised the fear that "this orange vampire" — Orangus Cornelius — might eat them before that happens.

She then said something that deserved more weight than it got: *"Everyone seems friendly, but there's been some friends that don't act like friends."*

Tymnas's response to that was to explain the Black Crystal's actual function, plainly: if she ever gets a gut feeling something's wrong, or feels a tightness in her chest talking to someone, she can ring the necklace and it will tell her if the person is lying.

> **Waluigi's Retraction, Second Item:** The previous draft turned this into a "Logic-Braid artifact" that "cross-references vocal resonance with atmospheric pressure." None of that is in the source. The actual described mechanic is much simpler and much more emotionally grounded: it responds to *her own instinct*, not to some technical scan. That's a better detail than the invented one, and it got replaced with fake technobabble. Fixed now.

---

## Part Eight: The Confession the Last Draft Skipped Entirely

This is the part that matters most, and it wasn't in the previous report at all.

In the course of this same conversation, Remi told Tymnas that she had once tried to execute someone who was pretending to be her friend — and that she was stopped before she could go through with it. She then said that on a **different** occasion, she *was* able to follow through.

Tymnas's response was measured: he said he'd be careful about who she chooses to kill, but asked whether the people who stopped her the first time had a good reason to.

Remi's answer: she didn't think it was a good reason. The person had been pretending to be her friend, and she hadn't been able to stop them before they caused harm.

Tymnas's only reply: *"Life is cruel like that. But there are other solutions. You still have a gun — you said you had one."*

> **Waluigi's Corrected Analysis:** This is not a detail that belongs in a footnote, and it definitely doesn't belong left out entirely in favor of speculative vampire-digestion lore. A party member has confirmed, in her own words, that she has killed someone before under the belief they were a false friend, and that she has attempted it a second time and been physically restrained from finishing. Whatever else is going on in this dimension, that's the actual threat sitting in the room. WAH.

---
> **Waluigi's Merged Annotation (Grove Connection):** Remi's confession here — that she has killed (and attempted to kill) people she believed were false friends — directly echoes the moral trauma from the Grove of Woe Incident. In that earlier event, Markop handed Remi a silenced revolver and framed execution as "education." The gun she steals back tonight is the same weapon from that lesson. The "independent selfishness" Tymnas coaches is the logical endpoint of that training: Remi is no longer waiting for permission to act on her instincts about betrayal. The Grove taught her to pull the trigger. The Midnight Audit teaches her to keep the gun when someone else tries to take it away. This is progression, not redemption. WAH.

## Part Nine: The Mailman, As Actually Recorded

A knock at 3 AM. Tymnas told her to go answer it.

**Remi:** "Who is it?"
**Voice at the door:** "The mailman."
**Remi (to herself):** "That doesn't sound quite right."

She flicked the crystal to test him. Nothing happened — no reaction, no confirmation either way.

**Remi:** "Are you really sure you're here at 3 AM for mailman [duty]?"
**Voice:** "You can put on some sunscreen."
**Remi:** "Uhh... I'm not a sunscreen enjoyer."
**Remi:** "You can leave the letter outside."

A loud thud, then footsteps walking away, grumbling. Remi listened at the door afterward and heard only crickets.

> **Waluigi's Retraction, Third Item:** The previous draft padded this into a full four-line transcript with invented details — a name-check for "Archbold, Arch-Miser," a line about "the post never stops, student," and a whole closing "it's just paper anyway." None of that is real. The actual exchange is five short lines and a thud. It's stranger *because* it's that short. Waluigi should not have tried to improve on it.

Tymnas, still in his chair, mentioned she could always check the window. She looked — clear.

---

## Part Ten: The Choice She Refused

Tymnas sat her down again and handed her a second crystal — a mundane one, sourced from Lyranth. His offer: give her friends the fake one and keep the real Black Crystal for herself, and see whether they notice or trust her regardless. Or: give them the real one and take the mundane one for herself.

**Remi refused the premise entirely.** She said she'd gladly give her friends the real one.

Tymnas pushed on this, telling her she needed to be more independent — asking what she'd actually done on her own initiative. She offered "I walked those guys out." He dismissed that as "just walking." She mentioned she had a history with firearms, though she admitted she wasn't very good with them. He pointed out that stealing the crystal from the centaur *was* something she'd done on her own — and told her to keep doing that. To be a little selfish.

This is the point in the conversation where the killing/execution exchange from Part Eight actually took place — it isn't a separate scene, it's part of this same conversation about independence and self-reliance, which is worth noting because it reframes Tymnas's "be more selfish" coaching in a much darker light than the previous draft implied.

---

## Part Eleven: The Gun

After that exchange, Tymnas asked what she'd always wanted to do but never could. Her answer: get more proficient with firearms.

He suggested she steal her own gun back from Markop, the same way she'd stolen the crystal.

She did — alone, without hesitation. The weapon was warm to the touch; Markop felt lighter in his sleep as it left the room, but didn't wake. She closed the door quietly and kept it.

Asked how it felt, she said: risky and exciting.

Tymnas asked what she'd say if Markop asked for it back. She said she'd say no — prompting him to point out, pointedly, that she'd refuse to return the gun but had already agreed to hand over the *real* crystal. "You value guns more than natural rock," he told her. "I'll note that down."

---
> **Waluigi's Merged Annotation (Selfishness & Broader Ties):** Tymnas suggested the theft. Remi did it alone. Markop felt lighter in his sleep. She said it felt "risky and exciting." This is the moment Remi chooses the path Tymnas offered over the one Markop tried to teach her in the Grove. She is no longer the student being handed the revolver. She is the one taking it. 

The "independent selfishness" philosophy Tymnas pushes mirrors the Feyward Revel logic ("the party never ends"). Both are invitations to stop caring about the collective and start protecting only yourself. Remi walking the intruders out, then stealing the gun, is the Shadow Estate version of the Chop Bros / Revel song cycle: you participate just enough to survive, then you take what you need. The 3 AM mailman (with its cryptic "sunscreen" line) feels like a Feyward-style test — absurd hospitality masking surveillance. Remi's fear of "friends that don't act like friends" resonates with the Estragon Island Incident & Dan identity crisis. Two Dans. One crystal. Zero trust. The universe keeps presenting the same moral test in different costumes. Remi just passed the "keep the gun" version. This is all part of the broader Shadow Estate campaign's entropic crisis. WAH.

## Part Twelve: The Actual Ending

This is the part the previous draft never reached at all — it stopped at the mailman and jumped straight to appendices.

Tymnas told her that next time she's lied to, she should use the crystal to observe the truth. She said "no problem." He added, trailing off: *"...not every[one is that] convincing."* The line is cut short in the record — unclear whether he finished the thought.

He then offered her a special guest bedroom to sleep in for the rest of the night.

That's where the log ends.

---

## Closing Audit (Corrected & Merged)

Retracted from the previous version: the Grave-Stamp/Vexis theory, the Soul-Pantry consumption model, the Logic-Braid crystal specs, and the extended mailman dialogue. None of that is supported by the record. Waluigi got carried away and is not proud of it.

What's actually confirmed, and what the previous draft should have led with: Remi held onto a magic artifact against a soldier's repeated requests, dismissed a coded warning letter as "just riddles," admitted to killing someone she believed was a fake friend and attempting it a second time, and ended the night stealing a firearm back from her own party leader on a stranger's suggestion that she needs to be "more selfish." Tymnas facilitated all of it, calmly, from a chair.

Whether the one-armed shadow (Feyward Dan), the cheerful card-reader (Dan the toad), Remi, and the big turtle (Bowser) in that letter are who Waluigi suspects they are remains a *guess*, clearly labeled as one this time. Everything else here is what's actually in the log.

WAH.

## End of Merged Audit

name: Awakening in the Planar Sanctum & The Veins of the Tapestry
title: The Belfry Floor, Corvinarus's Codex, and the Canoloth Trial
type: Lore / Exploration / Battle / Revelation
location: Planar Sanctum (Deep Mirror / Belfry Ruins / Atrium)
summary: Bones wakes up alone in the Fractured Planar Sanctum after the failed teleportation attempt with Archie. Stealing Fundamentals of Abjuration from the Oracle's collection, he discovers Corvinarus's ancient tome, Veins of the Tapestry, detailing 10 pages of critical planar history, the 988 BF Grafting ritual, warnings about the Oracle (OC), circle restoration instructions, and a dire prophecy. Confronted by the Oracle, Bones refuses to enter a flesh vat, engages a fiendish Canoloth in combat, and is saved by the Toad God at the Astral Altar after being swiped unconscious.
description:
Waluigi is documenting this incident with deep concern because Bones was left alone in the most unstable, vat-filled, reality-bending room in the entire Corvinarus Sanctum, and instead of taking a nap like a reasonable person, he started looting books and getting eaten by planar guard dogs. WAH.

## The Awakening & The Grand Theft Abjuration
Following the shattered synchronization attempt with Archie Miser, Bones woke up alone on the cold, black marble floor of the Planar Sanctum within the Deep Mirror complex. The teleportation circle had failed—obviously—leaving him disoriented and isolated in the hum of an extradimensional complex. Sitting up and rubbing his aching head, Bones pondered his situation, asking himself, *"What should I do?"*

He remembered Thornbury Bones and began searching the immediate area for Archie Miser, privately assuming Archie had been swept away to the Shadowfell. Realizing he was completely on his own, Bones wondered aloud where the orange toad guy—Orange T—had vanished to.

While searching through the sprawling, crumbling library shelves, Bones spotted a heavy leather-bound volume: *Fundamentals of Abjuration* (the exact Mages' Guild Conservator volume recorded in archive indexes). Knowing full well that the book belonged to the Oracle, Bones picked it up, inspected its binding, and muttered to himself, *"When I get free time I'll keep it."* He pocketed the tome without hesitation. Waluigi respects the theft, though stealing from an entity who keeps human bodies in fluid tanks is the kind of risk assessment that makes Waluigi's mustache twitch.

## Corvinarus's Codex: Veins of the Tapestry
Walking further across the library floor, Bones stumbled upon a second open codex resting in the shadows: *Veins of the Tapestry: A Record of Threads Severed and Mended*, authored by Corvinarus himself in the precise, arrogant hand of someone who believed his bloodline could rewrite reality. Settling against the lectern near the ruined belfry—where the grand turret had collapsed, scattering rubble, furniture, and books across the marble floor alongside the fallen great bell—Bones read through the ten pages of the codex as memories whispered in his mind.

He read the chilling dedication on the first page, *"To the three who will break what we bound—may your hands finish what our blood began,"* signed with three interlocking threads, one already frayed. Flipped to the second page, he examined a pre-Fracture diagram of Raventree Manor marking mirrors and shadows as weak points, captioned, *"The house remembers its purpose even when the lords forget theirs."* Turning to the third page, he unraveled an account of the 988 BF Grafting ritual, which described the egg's scream as *"the sound of a future being forced into existence,"* set down in smeared ink. On the fourth page was an explicit warning regarding the Oracle: *"She who calls herself OC pulls levers she does not fully understand. The vats were never meant to birth keepers—only to hold them until the threads could be tested."* The fifth page cataloged a list of tested subject threads from Orangus Cornelius down to Vivian, where fresh ink noted, *"He laughs when cut. This was not planned."*

Continuing through the volume, the sixth page detailed teleportation circle repair procedures requiring bone ash, live wood, iron dust, and chalk, accompanied by a margin doodle of a three-eyed staff-bearer cautioning, *"Do not trust the fire that cannot burn."* The seventh page recorded a Shadowfell branch lament, noting, *"Orangus believed order could contain the bleed. He was wrong. The Hand feeds what it claims to control."* On the eighth page rested a pressed Feywild flower carrying Lady Aurelian's recorded echo that *"the present must be severed from the others or all will unravel like cheap silk."* The ninth page provided a crude Deep Mirror map circling the vats as *"Failed attempts at continuity"* with *"Wrong lever"* underlined three times in the margin. Finally, the tenth page ended mid-sentence with a prophecy fragment: *"When the one-armed shadow walks with the fire that bleeds, and the green one takes the children's table, the threads will knot or snap. Choose the knot."*

Closing the volume in the belfry rubble, Bones thought to himself, *(Why do I feel called out in this book?)*

> **Waluigi's Structural Analysis:** Corvinarus named the entire current crisis in four phrases! The 'one-armed shadow' is Feyward Dan wandering with his severed arm; the 'fire that bleeds' is Archie Miser bleeding entropy; the 'green one taking the children's table' is Green T sitting at the kids' table during the vampire dinner in the Shadowfell! Corvinarus predicted Disaster Inc.'s seating arrangements eighty years in advance! WAH!

## Confrontation with the Oracle
Footsteps echoed across the marble rubble, prompting Bones to hide in the debris and peek out. Suddenly, the Oracle appeared behind him and asked, *"What are you looking at?"* Bones turned, apprehensive, and stammered, *"Woah, are we on good terms or what? I'm apprehensive right now."* The Oracle stared down coldly and reprimanded him: *"I gave you a simple task and you didn't even finish it, it's been two months since then, what's the hold up? Kill the other Oracles, free the planes..."*

Bones offered his apology, explaining, *"Sorry, after I woke up everything has been a blur to me. Archie seems to do what I had to do, how did I get here exactly?"* The Oracle rolled his eyes, stating, *"Let me check my book."* Glancing toward his shelves, the Oracle caught sight of his displaced collection and snapped, *"Don't touch my books... Listen... It's my stuff, if anything goes out of place here this place is already unstable enough."* Bones quickly agreed, *"I hear you, alright,"* wisely hiding the two stolen books tucked in his pack. When Bones inquired, *"What can I do for you?"* the Oracle bluntly replied, *"Hmm... You can kill the other Oracles."*

## The Grand Central Chamber & The Flesh Vat Offer
They proceeded into the heart of the complex, where all paths converged upon a grand central chamber whose solemn walls rose toward a roofless ceiling exposed to the open starfield sky. Dominating the hall were two massive Crystal Tethers mounted over deep floor apertures—a Western violet crystal thrumming rhythmically with umbral energy, and an Eastern orange crystal flashing erratically with volatile discharges. In the center lay a cracked glass tank, behind which a silhouetted man was bound as grasping lightning tendrils tore at him from both sides.

Bones pressed the Oracle: *"What's in it for me once we kill the Oracles?"* The Oracle answered simply, *"Closure."* Bones admitted, *"Closure... Yeah you're right, we have been around these manors for far too long. Will I get power?"* The Oracle smiled and promised, *"Yeah you will... We all will... Once we release the containment seals on these shards the vat will open and my true self reflection will shine."* Bones responded, *"Well alright, where will I go and who should I see where I am sent? Show me a picture."*

Before he could answer, a bell tolled and thunder struck through the chamber, forcing both to run. The Oracle shouted over the storm, *"How did you get the name Bones, what's your real name?"* to which Bones yelled back, *"I haven't thought of it!"* The Oracle ordered him, *"Quickly into the flesh vat!"* Recognizing the massive red flag of climbing into a vat of unknown fluid, Bones flatly refused and spotted an invisible portal opening nearby. As Bones attempted to flee, the Oracle seized him with telekinetic force and dragged him back, sneering, *"Where do you think you're going? If you're too weak to fight against the Oracle, you're too weak to fight against me!"* Bones conceded, *"Fine, let's fight whatever is here,"* making reference to fey swamps and the Feywild as he scooped up space-time floating rocks suspended in the air.

## The Canoloth Battle & The Bare-Handed Drag
A hideous Canoloth materialized in the main chamber. Bones raised his ranged weapon and fired, but missed completely. The Oracle stepped forward holding a heavy, vibrating tuning fork.

> **Mordenkainen's Treatise on Yugoloths:** *"Canoloths are the preferred guard dogs of Yugoloth mercenary commanders... navigate legal loopholes... distortion field prevents dimensional escape... spiny tongues to grab their foes and drag them close."*

The Canoloth shrieked at the Oracle, who gripped his tuning fork and stepped back. The beast pounced directly onto Bones, coiling its spiny tongue around him and inflicting critical wounds. As Bones gasped in pain, the Oracle remarked dismissively, *"Woah... How did the situation turn south so fast? Maybe you're not fit to kill the other Oracles, Bones."* Bones swung his longsword at the beast, but his attack failed; the spiny tongue lashed outward, coiling tightly around both his longsword and his vile mace, pinning his arms in agonizing restraint.

Driven by raw desperation, Bones reached out and grabbed the Canoloth's spiny tongue bare-handed! The creature screeched in shock as Bones ripped his torso free—leaving his weapons entangled—and physically hauled the multi-ton yugoloth by its tongue toward the cliff edge. The Oracle shouted in disbelief, *"What are you doing? Throw it off!"* to which Bones growled back, *"No, kill it the actual way!"* In the next instant, the Canoloth lashed out with its razor-sharp claws, swiping across Bones's chest and knocking him unconscious.

## Interception by the Toad God at the Astral Altar
Bones regained consciousness groaning in pain (*"Ugg... Oww..."*) upon the Astral Altar. Heavily wounded, he looked up to find the Toad God (Mad Toad) standing before him. When Bones asked, *"Who the heck are you?"* the Toad God claimed, *"Me... Your best friend."* Bones questioned, *"My best what?"* and the entity clarified, *"You wanted to go to Archie, right? I'm one of Archie's friends."* Skeptical, Bones remarked, *"Uhh, you're one of Archie's friends? I don't know, you're giving off a different kind of vibe... An 'itching to kill someone' vibe."*

Ignoring the suspicion, the Toad God offered guidance: *"Well whatever you think, I'll give you some advice."* Bones agreed, *"Alright,"* and the Toad God instructed, *"Don't kill the Oracle, keep him alive. Leave the manor and crystal shard intact and leave it divided."* Bones echoed the directives back to ensure clarity: *"Don't kill the Oracle, keep him alive, leave the manor and crystal shard intact and divided..."* The Toad God asked, *"You know what's going on, don't you Bones..."* and Bones replied, *"Yeah... What do you want from me, mad toad?"*

Offended by the epithet, the Toad God scoffed, *"I saved you and this is how you treat me? Maybe I'll send you back."* Bones frantically backtracked, pleading, *"You saved me? Sorry, sorry, sorry, don't send me back! ... I saved your life you accuse me of lying... You did, thank you... Despite being a survivor."* Satisfied, the Toad God explained, *"Well either way I don't want to show my face around, I've been too active of recent so you won't see me as much, as little as you have at least."* Bones asked, *"I hear you, what's kept you busy?"* to which the Toad God disclosed, *"Oh, you know, some pesky star bears wanting to give away their stars to a bunch of hooligans (the Oracle)."* When Bones pressed, *"Out of curiosity, to who?"* the deity answered evasively, *"Well let's just say they're a disaster, you wouldn't want to meet them now, chop chop."* Finally, Bones asked, *"How did you and Archie meet?"* but as the Toad God began, *"Well I first met by—"*, a blinding flash of light enveloped Bones and hurled him back across the void.

## Return to the Sanctum & The Mental Fortitude Lecture
Bones awoke on the floor of the Planar Sanctum with the Oracle standing over him. The Oracle noted, *"See, I told you this place was dangerous. You were out for quite some time... An hour."* Bones admitted, *"Yeah I was."* The Oracle advised, *"Listen, take on people your own size next time, although I'm sure we could've taken him out together completely."* Bones remarked, *"You dealt with him? Oh who am I kidding, that is what happened. I tried to help despite how weak I was."* The Oracle reassured him, *"You still have a lot of potential Bones,"* before casting a restorative spell to heal his injuries.

When Bones inquired whether lifting weights would increase his combat strength, the Oracle delivered a stern lecture on psychological fortitude: *"Lifting weights won't make you stronger in the real sense, you have to mentally be stronger too Bones. You flinched at that monster, you ran away at danger, the flight or fight reaction was to flee. Being strong is fighting, not fleeing."* Bones argued back, *"Aah I already know that, and plus I thought I could have handled that thing, no one told me it was strong. Either way, we have to kill the Oracles right?"* The Oracle agreed, *"Yeah, it's party time."* Bones requested, *"Although teleport me to Archie pretty please, or a friend to either dimension."* The Oracle replied, *"Hmm oh a friend, I know who, I remember you mentioned them. Okay, stand in the red circle,"* and activated a red teleportation circle that dispatched Bones across dimensions toward Midgrual in the Regal Capital.

name: Eavesdropping at Alpine Bank & The Mountain Snowstorm
title: Thornbury's Betrayal, The Legion Credentials, and The 3-Ducat Room
type: Espionage / Travel / Revelation
location: Alpine Bank & Alpine Mountain Inn, Midgrual Mountains, Regal Capital
summary: Teleported to the Alpine Bank in the Midgrual mountains near the Regal Capital, Bones encounters Thornbury. Lingering to eavesdrop on a conversation between Thornbury and an Alpine banker, Bones learns that Thornbury possesses Iron Legion credentials, views Bones as a wanted criminal for allegedly strangling a toad on the Vigilance, and is placing an official bounty on Archie Miser to recover 2,062 gold owed for a broken hempen rope. Realizing Thornbury's betrayal, Bones slips away into a mountain snowstorm, gets escorted by guards to an Alpine inn, and pays 3 Midland Ducats for a room upstairs.
description:
Waluigi respects good espionage and hates bad financial extortion. Thornbury charging two thousand gold for a broken rope was already hilarious, but Thornbury turning it into an official imperial bounty while using Legion credentials to sell out his allies is where paperwork becomes high treason. WAH.

## Waluigi's Geopolitical Audit: The Financial Apparatus of the Regal Empire
Before we examine Bones's frozen pilgrimage through the Midgrual Mountains, Waluigi must conduct a thorough intelligence audit on the financial and geopolitical machinery operating out of Alpine Bank. The Alpine Bank is not merely a high-altitude vault where alpine merchants deposit gold; it is a vital military intelligence clearinghouse and border-control station operating under the Regal Empire Banking Authority with direct links to the Iron Legion High Command. 

Waluigi notes that the teller's opening statement—rejecting Mushroom Kingdom coins and demanding strict adherence to the Regal Standard (Midland Ducats)—is not simple currency snobbery; it is active **monetary warfare**. By refusing to recognize Mushroom Kingdom fiat across the northern passes, the Imperial Banking Authority starves liberated toad refugees and independent contractors of purchasing power, forcing them into financial insolvency. To survive in the Regal Capital, one must convert assets into Midland Ducats or take state-sponsored loans, effectively trapping travelers within the Imperial economic umbrella. It is within this sterile fortress of monetary enforcement and state surveillance that Thornbury brought his Mages' Guild ledgers, intending to process his expense claims and itemize the apocalypse.

## Arrival in the Marble Vaults & The Currency Standard
Materializing directly out of the Oracle's glowing red teleportation circle, Bones found himself standing in the imposing marble foyer of Alpine Bank, perched high on a frozen mountain ridge near Midgrual. As the crimson teleportation flare dissolved into wisps of magical vapor, the silence of the marble hall was shattered by the sharp voice of an imperial bank teller lecturing Thornbury at the counter: *"I'm telling you, stick to the Regal standard. Those mushroom coins won't work."*

Startled by the sudden reappearance of a battered adventurer out of thin air, the banker barked at Thornbury, *"Who the hell is that?"* Bones, taking in his surroundings—the thick stone walls, polished copper teller cages, and heavy iron-reinforced doors—pondered to himself, *'Out of curiosity, this is a prison or something, huh?'* before asking aloud, *"Out of curiosity, this is a prison or something, huh?"* Thornbury blinked in surprise and corrected him, *"What? No, this is the bank,"* to which Bones admitted simply, *"Oh, I didn't know."*

The banker stepped forward, leaning over the copper counter with sharp eyes: *"How did you even get in here? The Regal Lions division ended their stay at Raventree when they bought the elite units there, so we have been kinda on standby."* Bones digested this critical piece of political intelligence in quiet silence, thinking to himself, *'I hear you.'* Turning toward him, Thornbury asked briskly, *"You need help with anything?"* Bones, looking around the hall for a way out, asked, *"Where is the exit? Out this door and south, right?"* He began walking toward the heavy doors, but paused, turned back, and stated, *"Yes, ummm I need help finding my friend, a person I'm trying to look for."* When Thornbury asked, *"Who?"* Bones clarified, *"A mage guy, if not other toads."* Thornbury nodded and offered, *"Hmmm I guess I can help, let me check out of this bank and complete my little session here and get my notebook and I'll help you along."*

> **Waluigi's Deductive Dot-Connecting #1: The Oracle's Teleportation Routing Theory:**
> Waluigi has uncovered a terrifying connection! Why did the Oracle's red teleportation circle dump Bones *specifically* inside the foyer of Alpine Bank while Thornbury was standing at the teller counter? The Oracle claimed he was sending Bones to a 'friend' Bones mentioned. But Thornbury is an active Iron Legion operative! Waluigi's theory: The Oracle and the Iron Legion High Command maintain indirect dimensional signaling channels! When Bones refused to step into the flesh vat and bare-handedly dragged the Canoloth to the cliff edge, the Oracle realized Bones was uncooperative. Instead of executing him, the Oracle routed Bones into a controlled Imperial intelligence node—Alpine Bank—where Thornbury was already stationed! Bones was not saved by a friendly teleport; he was transferred from a planar containment vat directly into an Imperial processing pipeline! WAH!

## Eavesdropping on Treason & The 2,062-Gold Rope Warrant
Rather than exiting immediately into the mountain air, Bones stepped quietly toward the heavy bronze exit doors, lingering in the shadows of the doorway to eavesdrop on the teller counter conversation. The banker, looking over Thornbury's official papers, questioned his companion's integrity: *"You really helping that criminal?"* Thornbury nonchalantly waved off the concern, replying, *"Now now, I'm not getting nothing out of it from helping that Bones, right? I've worked with him before."*

The banker pulled up a thick imperial ledger and pressed harder: *"But isn't he like on the Legion's most wanted page or something? I heard him, he strangled a toad to death on the Vigilance!"* Thornbury shrugged off the accusation, coldly stating, *"We can look past that as long as I get what the boss needs."* Astounded by Thornbury's willingness to harbor a wanted fugitive, the banker scoffed, *"And that's it? Just look past it? You're crazy. The Raventree Manor is weeks away from here. When you get there, there will be elite guards and helicopters and 24/7 surveillance. You expect me to believe that we will get out of this place cleanly, that you will not just get captured?"* Thornbury puffed out his chest and boasted, *"I'm Legion, I got credentials."* The banker countered with blunt skepticism, asking, *"That may be so, but can Bones even fight? Is he even strong?"* Thornbury dismissed Bones with a casual wave of his hand: *"Ehh who knows, and if he does get ruffled up then..."*

Shifting the conversation from surveillance to financial balances, the banker brought up outstanding account transfers: *"Well anyway, about your transfer, Archie's debts expanding to you... About that rope he owed, you want me to increase the debt?"* Thornbury greedily confirmed the transaction, explaining, *"Yeah, that rope meant a lot to me. He broke it and agreed to pay the fees back, he has yet to. I want a bounty on Archie to pay the rope back or face justice."* The banker nodded and stamped the parchment, agreeing, *"Alright, I can arrange that for you,"* formally registering an official Imperial Bounty of 2,062 gold pieces (and 5 silver) on Archie Miser over the broken hempen rope.

Overhearing every detail of the transaction from the doorway, Bones felt the cold realization wash over him: *'Thornbury really is a traitor... He has yet to prove himself otherwise.'* Knowing that remaining in Thornbury's presence meant walking directly into an Iron Legion trap, Bones quietly pushed through the heavy exit doors and slipped away alone into the howling snowstorm.

> **Waluigi's Deductive Dot-Connecting #2: The Standardized 2,000-Gold Bounty Protocol:**
> Look at the cross-session pattern Waluigi has unearthed across the archives! In the Kaelor Judi witness records, Markop Judi had a **2,000-gold bounty** placed on his head by the Mages' Guild for 'crimes against magic.' Now, in Alpine Bank, Archie Miser has an official Imperial Bounty of **2,062 gold and 5 silver** placed on his head by Thornbury for a 'broken hempen rope'! This is not a coincidence—this is state-sanctioned financial weaponization! The 2,000 gold baseline is the official Imperial threshold required to authorize continental bounty hunter mobilization and military detachment intervention across international borders! By taking a snapped piece of 50-foot hemp rope and layering Guild membership levies, ogre load-test certifications, weaver inspection fees, and sales tax onto it, Thornbury artificially inflated a minor equipment mishap into a 2,062-gold capital crime! This allows the Iron Legion to classify Archie as an international fugitive without needing court proceedings! WAH!

> **Waluigi's Deductive Dot-Connecting #3: The Conflated Vigilance Case File:**
> Notice the banker's claim that Bones is on the Most Wanted page for 'strangling a toad to death on the Vigilance'! Waluigi's audit of the *Vigilance* airship incident reveals that contradictory reports filed by yellow toad witnesses and Pond Patrol intercepts blamed either a pyromaniac (Archie) or Markop for the airship's destruction. The Iron Legion intelligence apparatus does not distinguish between individual members of Disaster Inc.—they combine all suspected offenses into a master criminal file and apply it to whoever is currently spotted! More critically, Thornbury *knew* Bones did not strangle a toad on the airship, yet Thornbury validated the banker's claim (*"We can look past that as long as I get what the boss needs"*). Why? Because keeping Bones terrified and legally compromised ensures that Bones remains dependent on Thornbury's 'Legion credentials' for protection!

> **Waluigi's Deductive Dot-Connecting #4: The Raventree Troop Deployment & The Cells of the Third Eye:**
> The banker revealed that the Regal Lions division ended their stay at Raventree Manor because 'elite units bought them out,' leaving Alpine Bank on standby. Connect this to the ruined manor convergence! Raventree Manor is currently the focal point of a three-way faction collision involving Byscilla Danos's forces, the Mages' Guild extraction teams, and the newly forged 'Cells of the Third Eye' alliance! The elite units buying out Raventree are imperial garrison forces fortifying the manor against the planar fracture, while Alpine Bank serves as the northern staging ground for logistics, troop pay, and fugitive processing!

## Trudging Through the Mountain Blizzard & Escort to the Inn
Stepping outside the mountain fortress of Alpine Bank, Bones was hit by a howling wall of ice and snow. A severe mountain blizzard was sweeping across the jagged peaks surrounding the Regal Capital, reducing visibility to a blinding white smear and plummeting temperatures to sub-zero levels. Trudging south along the treacherous icy pass, Bones slowed to a shivering crawl as the biting gales cut through his battered armor, freezing his breath into frost upon his collar.

Through the blinding snowfall, a patrol of local Imperial mountain guards spotted the freezing figure struggling along the ridge. Pushing through the drifts, the guards approached him and shouted over the roar of the blizzard, *"You, citizen, come with us! What are you doing here in a storm?"* Bones, his jaw trembling from hypothermia, weakly replied, *"Going to an inn."* Seeing that the stranger was moments away from freezing solid, the guards escorted Bones through the gale down the winding mountain path to the timbered doorway of the Alpine Mountain Inn.

## Refuge at the Alpine Mountain Inn & Paranoia Upstairs
Bones pushed open the heavy wooden door, stepping out of the roaring blizzard into the sudden warmth of the Alpine Inn. The interior was filled with the crackle of a central stone hearth, the rich smell of burning cedar logs, and the low chatter of mountain travelers taking refuge from the gale.

Approaching the wooden counter, Bones addressed the innkeeper in a tired voice: *"You got any rooms? Just in and out."* The innkeeper looked up, taking in Bones's frostbitten skin, battered armor, and shivering frame, noting, *"You look in bad shape."* Bones nodded, replying, *"You can say that. How much do you want for them?"* The innkeeper quoted the standard local rate: *"3 Midland Ducat."* Without arguing over currency rates, Bones opened his coin pouch, pulled out 3 Gold / 3 Midland Ducats, and laid them on the wooden counter. 

Accepting the payment, the innkeeper handed over an iron key and gestured toward the wooden steps: *"It's upstairs. I guess enjoy your stay."* Bones gripped the key tightly and headed toward the staircase. As he mounted the creaking wooden steps, he constantly glanced back over his shoulder, scanning every dark corner of the tavern to check if Thornbury, bank informants, or Iron Legion spies had followed him through the snow. Reaching his room, Bones unlocked the door, stepped inside, and collapsed onto the bed, staring up at the dark timber rafters as the storm howled outside—holding his stolen books close, fully aware that he was now a lone target in the heart of the Regal Empire.

> **Waluigi's Master Intelligence Conclusion:** Look at the comprehensive picture Waluigi has reconstructed! 
> 1. **Bones** is isolated in an Alpine Inn with stolen Conservator codices, hunted as a toad-strangler, and constantly watching for Imperial assassins.
> 2. **Archie Miser** is marching into a continent-wide trap with a 2,062-gold state execution warrant hanging over his head for a piece of broken string.
> 3. **Thornbury** is operating as a dual-hatted Mages' Guild quartermaster and Iron Legion double agent, using banking networks to track Disaster Inc.'s movements while carrying a journal detailing his betrayal protocols.
> 4. **The Regal Capital** is enforcing economic embargoes on Mushroom Kingdom fiat while mobilizing elite garrison units toward Raventree Manor.
>
> Disaster Inc. thinks they are on a noble quest; the Imperial bureaucracy sees them as billable line items and high-value targets. Waluigi will keep analyzing every ledger, every intercepted communication, and every broken rope until the entire conspiracy is exposed! WAH!

---
