description:
This article contains the full-text transcription of **[Thornbury's Field Journal](thornburys_field_journal)**, recovered by **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** from the floor of **[Raventree Manor](raventree_manor)** after **[Thornbury](thornbury)**'s cover was spectacularly blown. Use the index table of contents below to browse the daily spy logs, clinical subject profiles, and structural layout blueprint of the manor.
Waluigi's Espionage Review: Thornbury is a terrible spy! WAH! You don't spend two weeks hiding in the shadows just to get dragged out by your ear like a naughty child. And leaving your notebook on the floor? Magnificent incompetence! But the notes are extremely accurate—Waluigi will be using these psychological profiles to blackmail everyone later!

sections.name: Part I: Daily Espionage Logs
sections.subtitle: Thornbury's Chronicle of Disaster Inc.'s Movements
sections.overview: This section compiles Thornbury's raw, daily log entries recorded during his active, two-week observation mission inside **[Raventree Manor](raventree_manor)**. It chronicles every encounter, combat, and private bubble bath to the tee.

subsections.title: BONES & SPEAKER L — Pond Patrol Arrives (30 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
Two new actors. **[Bones](bones)** and **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** of the Pond Patrol. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** carries cipher-locked intelligence files — the Patrol's accumulated dossiers. **[Bones](bones)** arrived to help decode them. Their files designate our group as the 'Vigilance Group.' They know about PL1 — which means Patrol intelligence is significantly better than the **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)**'s awareness of their awareness. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** is thorough. His work is good.

A guard approached — 'what's all this singing going on? I heard you say **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**.' Just assisting **[Speaker L](speaker_l)**. 'Do you know where you are?' **[Bones](bones)** said **[Raventree Manor](raventree_manor)**, ruled by a toad. 'Wrong,' the guard said. 'Ruled by **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** in collaboration with the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)**.' He pointed at the Vigilance hovering above — 'it's under **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** control now. The Vigilance is now the Legionlance.' **[Bones](bones)** grunted, stormed up, almost grabbed **[Speaker L](speaker_l)**. They both walked off to discuss entry.

> **[**[Speaker L](speaker_l)** — Profile]** Before Aegis Command he was an institutional loyalist. Order 120 ended that — mass harm to toad populations under an impersonator using his face. He maintained the forms while it happened. He knows this. Results-driven now, rule-agnostic. He carries a concealed hand crossbow I did not detect until he fired it. This is noted with professional irritation.

> **[**[Bones](bones)** — Profile]** Combat-first. Modified rapier — official insignia on guard, dark metal enhancement on the blade edge. Refused healing after combat twice. Pride, distrust, or something else. Do not engage directly without significant numerical advantage and a plan for the suplex.

subsections.title: Library Infiltration — Bones Operates at Night (30 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
**[Bones](bones)** and **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** entered through a window — exterior thorns blocked other approaches. Pitch black, 21:21. **[Bones](bones)** grabbed Lucky T from the shadows — 'who do you work for?' **[Speaker L](speaker_l)**. Happy reunion. A **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** member entered the library, picked up a book. They hid behind a bookshelf. **[Bones](bones)** went behind the guard, knocked him unconscious, stole his torch. Closed the exits by 23:40. Clean.

They entered the workshop/storage room — **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** recognised the furniture. 'This furniture belonged to a lord. I would know that.' Then the curio room — and there was the Mole. He was scratching out **[The Oracle](the_oracle)**'s inscriptions. The same formulae I spent two weeks studying. He destroyed them. I have my copy but the loss is significant. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** told Lucky T to guard a door. He ran past **[Bones](bones)** — 'secure the other door, make sure he doesn't leave.' A chase ensued until **[Bones](bones)** reached a door, spotted **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)**, stopped giving chase.

> **[External Combat — 2 vs 3]** A guard asked if they were with **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)**. **[Bones](bones)** maced him — parried, blocked. A whistle blown, not too loud. Reinforcements. Lucky T got a clean hit. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** fired the concealed hand crossbow — wounded a guard who fled. **[Bones](bones)** suplex'd a guard from behind. An arrow from an unknown position dropped the last guard — headshot. Bodies hidden, military horn recovered. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** healed Lucky T. **[Bones](bones)** refused healing. Third time.

subsections.title: Second Floor — The Mole vs. Miser, Hargram Fidger (30 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
The Mole opened the upstairs door just in time. He pulled out his knife and full-sprinted toward **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**'s recovery room. **[Bones](bones)** tackled him mid-air. 'What's going on?' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** asked. The guard said 'stay still.' **[Bones](bones)** said 'this guy is trying to kill you but I stopped him.' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** sighed as **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** entered with manacles. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** dodged. **[Bones](bones)** jumped off the Mole, tried to intercept **[Speaker L](speaker_l)**, sidekicked the Mole.

**[Luigi](luigi)** flashed his light. Just... flashed it. They went away — both the Mole and Lucky T disappeared. 'What did you do to them?' 'Just flash a light...' Lucky T said he'd gotten what he wanted. He left.

**[Bones](bones)** pointed at Lucky T: 'I don't trust him.' Lucky T: 'You'd rather I kill you?' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**: 'I can just fire a ball at you.' 'Fine, I'll leave.' Guards entered — 'we came to protect the injured.' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**: 'There was a disturbance but we handled it, please come back another day, I'm recovering.' I remained quiet.

> **[**[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)** — Arrival]** **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)** entered immediately after. 'I'm here to work with you.' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**: 'Please don't come closer, I'm recovering.' 'We will meet again. My name is **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)**, I'm with the local **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** chapel.' He noted the guards around **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**. 'I think you're important with these guards.' 'We will have a better meeting another time.' He left. I have known **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)** since day twenty. His questions have always been too specific. He identified **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** as 'important' before any real conversation. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** handled the interaction cleanly — cited recovery, deferred politely, dismissed without antagonising. Social competency under pressure: genuinely high.

subsections.title: Thornbury Reports — Aemenor Evenflight & The Portal Events (30 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
Before bed I told the group what I knew. Something is happening in the planar realms. I asked if they had met Aemenor Evenflight — the **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** called for reinforcements and he should be here. They said they'd met one of the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)**'s captains. The timeline is confused. There are so many factions in this house now.

> **[The Planar Shards — What I Understand Now]** The shattered ritual on Highsun 21 — the party attempted a synchronisation rite with **[The Oracle](the_oracle)** to align the physical world, mirror-space, and the 'Deep Layers.' It catastrophically failed, tearing local reality into three planar shards. The FEYWARD Manor — a Feywild reflection where **[Lady Aurelian Corvinarus](lady_aurelian_corvinarus)** holds court, satyrs drink endlessly, and time moves strangely. The SHADEWARD Manor — a Shadowfell reflection where **[Orangus Cornelius](orangus_cornelius)** hosts vampire dinners and the Onyx Hand operates. And the MATERIAL Manor — where we are, where the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** has established control and renamed the Vigilance to the Legionlance. The party was scattered across all three. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** and Bowser went to the Shadowfell. **[Waluigi](waluigi)** and Toad Lee to the Feywild. Markop and Remi into the Deep Mirror. Toadburt was captured by the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** in the physical antechamber — they fitted him with an Entropy Ring and sent him into the Feywild as a coerced agent with orders to capture **[The Oracle](the_oracle)** within three days.

> **[Sergeant Varn Coldbrook — **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** Fey Operations]** The **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** sent their own team through. Sergeant Varn Coldbrook — nineteen-year veteran who never expected to find himself in an impossible forest where the sun doesn't move. A practical man who believes in cold iron, hot meals, and following orders. His mission: locate and secure **[The Oracle](the_oracle)**. His squad entered the Feyward shard on Highsun 24 through a mirror-door a **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** wizard stabilised briefly. The door collapsed behind them. They've been trapped since. He started with eight soldiers. Private Henwick disappeared — found his boots arranged neatly beside a stream, facing upstream, no tracks. Corporal Dain started laughing during watch and hasn't stopped smiling — his eyes went the wrong colour. Private Marsh was replaced by something wearing his face. Coldbrook is down to five functional soldiers, none sleeping well, all jumping at sounds. He doesn't know we're in the same dimensional shard. He's been tracking unknown movement through the manor — building a picture of capabilities and intentions. He's also noticed the month-end deadline everyone keeps mentioning.

subsections.title: A New Day — Baths, Robes, and Byscilla Danos (29 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
29 Harvestide, 1040. Soldas. Golden Summer. Overcast, 28°C. I shook hands with **[Bones](bones)** — a real handshake, firm, acknowledged — as he cleared out the bathtub. I told **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** I would bring water from the well outside. I ran out, fetched two buckets, bubble bath, and rubber duckies. Morale is operational effectiveness by another name. I have been in this house for two weeks. I thought it would be welcome.

**[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** showered first. Clean dark blue mage's robe, brown belt, brown shoes, staff, third eye visible, hood down. He looked considerably more composed than someone who was unconscious and bleeding twelve hours ago has any right to look. **[Bones](bones)** said 'you look handsome.' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**: 'what — it can't be that — umm — impressive right?' He was flustered. The most unguarded I've seen him.

**[Bones](bones)** went for a mirror, ran into someone. **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** — part of the **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** family. She wanted to know where the water-powered fans had gone. Her soldiers outside had heatstroke. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** said 'it's just a bit of water, just a quick minute.' She was not persuaded. Then she saw ME.

> **[Cover Compromised — **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)**]** She said 'wait a minute — YOU!' and took me by the ear, dragging me out by my helmet. My cover with the **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** family is burned. My captain recognised me. She dragged me out of a room by my own helmet. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** called after me: 'Thank you for helping us.' He had previously told the others he thought I might betray them. He thanked me in public while I was being dragged away. He is simultaneously suspicious and grateful and holds both states without needing to resolve them.

**[Bones](bones)** emerged from his shower unrecognisable — the mushroom had been obscuring him. He was genuinely happy. No one recognised him. **[Luigi](luigi)** came out last, mentioned he'd expelled ectoplasm in the bath, and no one reacted.
subsections.waluigi_note: Fetching bubble bath and rubber duckies for people you are spying on? WAH! Thornbury, you are too soft. Real spies use poison, not bubble bath!

subsections.title: ⚠ BREACH — They Found My Notes. They Read Everything. (29 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
> **[⚠ CONTAINMENT FAILURE]** After **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** removed me, **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** noticed something on the ground. I believe it fell from my kit during the dragging. He picked it up. He read the field notes. He described them as 'detailed notes on everything they did to the tee.' That is accurate. They were.

**[Bones](bones)**: 'He was a spy, wasn't he?' Silence. Cricket noises. **[Luigi](luigi)** walked out of the bath: 'huh?' 'He was spying on us.' 'How was the bath?' 'Bath was good, expelled ectoplasm too.' 'Well those notes are interesting I guess.' They all pulled up chairs and reviewed the contents of the notebook.

> **[Self-Assessment — Final Entry as Active Observer]** My cover is burned. Two weeks of careful observation, and they found the notes on the day I was dragged out by my own helmet. What they have read: everything. Every profile, every assessment, the ring I pocketed, the PL1 mortality note about **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** specifically. They have read that I know the clearing event might kill him and chose not to tell him.

If I am writing my own profile — and I am, because consistency requires it — I would note: subject was thorough and accurate. Subject concealed potentially fatal intelligence from a party member for operational reasons. Subject pocketed items without full disclosure. Subject fetched bubble bath and rubber duckies. Subject was dragged out by his helmet.

I do not assign morality scores. I assess effectiveness and reliability only. Being read was not effective. I need to do better.

What I am less certain about: whether 'better' means tighter operational security or something else. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** thanked me. He knew I might betray him and he thanked me anyway. I am not used to that. I don't have a category for it.
subsections.waluigi_note: WAAAH! Leaving your secret diary on the bathroom floor is the most amateur mistake in the history of espionage. They read everything! Magnificent fail!

sections.name: Part II: Subject Clinical Profiles
sections.subtitle: Comprehensive Psychological & Tactical Diagnostics
sections.overview: Compiled by Thornbury from direct tactical observation. No moral judgments are made—only diagnostic assessments of combat effectiveness, reliability, and Guild cooperation levers.

subsections.title: ARCHIE MISER — Arcane caster / party lead
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** — Full Assessment]**

Prior **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** contact confirmed (compass, name recognition). Elevated PL1 resonance risk.

STRENGTHS: Environmental observation when calm — found hidden doors without guidance. De-escalation under social pressure — the **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)** interaction was genuinely impressive. Resilience after trauma — requested watch shifts while bleeding. Extends trust early and does not obviously regret it.

WEAKNESSES: Magical offensive accuracy collapses under fear — zero for three on the ghost. Bravado precedes capability. Agreed to pay 2,062 gold for a rope. Will not pay.

INTERPERSONAL: Generous before being asked. Suspicious but patient — saw me pocket the ring and said nothing. Read notes describing his potential death and thanked me anyway. Either exceptional discipline or an unusual kind of grace.

**[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** COOPERATION: MODERATE TO HIGH. Follows the compass. Has prior connections. Fear of the **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** name is workable.

IF MISSION GOES WRONG: Will retreat, regroup, attempt to negotiate. Manageable through information — but he has now demonstrated he finds and reads field notes.

subsections.title: LUIGI — Support / Poltergust handler
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Luigi](luigi)** — Full Assessment]**

Affiliation unclear. Bioluminescent flash capability.

STRENGTHS: Ghost absorption — the Poltergust is the most reliable anti-ghost capability in this party. Composure under all conditions. The flash clears rooms of multiple parties simultaneously. Correctly identified the practical solution (go around) while others climbed and fell.

WEAKNESSES: I haven't found any. This IS the concern.

INTERPERSONAL: Minimal verbal output. Expelled ectoplasm in the bath and mentioned it conversationally. Responded to discovering I was a spy with 'interesting I guess.'

**[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** COOPERATION: UNCERTAIN. No lever identified. No financial appetite, no institutional loyalty. He may simply continue operating regardless.

IF MISSION GOES WRONG: Do not underestimate the flash. Do not underestimate the Poltergust. Quietness is not passivity.

subsections.title: BONES — Melee combatant / Pond Patrol
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Bones](bones)** — Full Assessment]**

Modified rapier. Refuses healing (unexplained, three times now).

STRENGTHS: Suplex, tackle, knockout — all confirmed. Environmental stealth when motivated. Makes tactically correct decisions without being asked. Warming to **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** genuinely.

WEAKNESSES: Default answer to obstacles is force. Was stopped by a checkpoint during a chase. Refuses healing.

INTERPERSONAL: Distrusts Lucky T openly. Called me nice and I have filed this incorrectly twice.

**[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** COOPERATION: LOW. Loyalty is personal and individual. Do not engage directly without numerical advantage and a plan for the suplex.

subsections.title: SPEAKER L — Pond Patrol leadership
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** — Full Assessment]**

Concealed hand crossbow. Results-driven, rule-agnostic post-Aegis Command.

STRENGTHS: Weekly cipher rotation, thorough dossiers. Concealed crossbow I did not detect. Political leverage from knowing how institutions fail. He sings operational briefings — genuinely effective for morale.

WEAKNESSES: Low night vision — **[Bones](bones)** had to steady him. Cover burned with at least one guard. Emotionally compromised around Aegis Command.

**[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** COOPERATION: VERY LOW. Will choose toad survival over **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** interests without hesitation. I would do the same in his position.

IF MISSION GOES WRONG: Will extract information and prioritise toad survival. Will not sacrifice himself for the party. Fully independent actor.

subsections.title: BYSCILLA DANOS — Mages Guild Captain
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** — Assessment]**

My captain. **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** family — old money, **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)**-connected for generations. She is the working kind, not the inherited kind. Earned her captaincy through field operations, not patronage. Her squad trusts her in a way most **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** squads don't trust their captains.

She arrived with me on day one. She ran the survey. She told me not to get attached. She dragged me out by my helmet when she recognised me helping the party use **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** water resources for personal bathing. She was correct to do so. **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** resources are **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** resources.

She has been running the **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)**'s operational build-up at the manor quietly, in parallel with the party's activities. While the party explored, she mapped. While they fought ghosts, she catalogued. While they bathed, she reported. She is the person who will decide what happens to the PL1 fracture if the party fails. She has not shared her contingency plans with me. She does not share contingency plans with observers.

I trust her. I also know that trust is not something she factors into operational decisions. She factors effectiveness. And she is very, very effective.

sections.name: Part III: Manor Layout & Lore Compendium
sections.subtitle: Raventree Structural Blueprints & Cornelius Genealogy
sections.overview: A comprehensive structural directory detailing the Ground Floor, Second Floor, Attic, and Exterior Grounds of **[Raventree Manor](raventree_manor)**, combined with compiled dossiers on the **[Cornelius Family](the_oracle)** and the three planar shards.

subsections.title: MANOR LAYOUT — GROUND FLOOR
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Ground Floor Summary]**

R02 FOYER — Ruined marble, collapsed chandelier, grand staircases, root-blocked library doors. The guest book with Perrius Annmatar's entry 20 years ago. R03 HALLWAYS — West collapsed, east locked solid. Hidden passage to foyer. R04 LIBRARY — Immense, ransacked. Secret servant stair behind 'Useful Passages' book. Display case with three protected spell scrolls. Silver dagger (DC monogram). R05 OFFICE — Collapsed ceiling forms ramp to second floor. EC initials on bedframe. R06 STORAGE — Acid-trapped barrel. R07 WORKSHOP — Ylana's furniture stored after her death. The ring I pocketed. R08 GALLERY — The mirror. The formulae. **[The Oracle](the_oracle)**'s gateway. The Mole destroyed part of the inscription. R09 LOUNGE — Defaced portraits, ransacked drinks cabinet. Secret door to gallery. R10 VERANDA — Boot prints, shattered glass thrown 25+ feet. R11 KITCHEN — Five rust monsters. **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** says useful, I say absurd.

subsections.title: MANOR LAYOUT — SECOND FLOOR
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Second Floor Summary]**

R16 HALLWAY LANDING — Grand staircase landing, east/west split. R18 WESTERN LANDING — Reading nook, collapsed stairs to attic. Secret closet with peephole into Master Bathroom. R19 GUEST ROOMS — Five colour-coded rooms, Watcher's Hall between Blue and Red (illusory wall, one-way mirrors, silence enchantment). Guest lavatory. Secret collapsed stair to first floor. R20 LORD'S CHAMBERS — Ruined audience chamber, collapsed ceiling, grim host of spectral servants at night. Ochre Jelly in the lavatory. Spiral stair doors sealed. Servant's stairs end at hidden latch. R21 MASTER BEDROOM — Preserved by faltering spell. Immaculate desk. The Hidden Circle — broken teleportation circle under the rug. Key in desk drawer for library display case.

subsections.title: MANOR LAYOUT — ATTIC
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Attic Summary]**

S01 SOLARIUM — Rusting iron-and-glass ceiling, thousands of glass shards, mirrors arranged in a ring. Where the mirror entity was confronted. R24 BUTLER'S QUARTERS — Staff lounge, abandoned card game, secret passage via fake book. R25 BURN ROOM — Words carved into every surface by merged consciousness: 'trapped,' 'not me,' 'many,' 'alone.' R26 SENESCHAL'S ROOM — Shadow-burn silhouettes on furniture. A screaming face. Faceless servant portrait. Dust recently disturbed on mirrors. R23 SERVANT HALLWAYS — Trapped bathroom (thunder detonation). Most floors collapsed.

subsections.title: MANOR LAYOUT — EXTERIOR / GROUNDS
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Grounds Summary]**

COURTYARD — Wide, stone landing, great oaken doors with Corvinarus oak crest. Empty windows flank the entrance. NORTHERN PATH — Fountain with headless defaced statue. Mass grave in the flowerbeds — dozens of bodies, consecrated by a cleric who died afterward. GROUNDSKEEPER'S COTTAGE — Impassable hedge wall. Ten Wights shelter inside. DO NOT APPROACH. GREENHOUSE — Rusting, eastern grounds. **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** noted but did not enter. THE GREAT TREE — Dead, webbed canopy, wrapped creatures hanging from branches. Giant spiders. Golden Knight statuette at base (mirror puzzle piece). MEMORIAL FOUNTAIN — In the hedge maze. Consecrated safe haven. Memorial to Ylana Annmatar. Magical water font. Small wooden bunny toy with 'Y.A.' and 'E.C.' initials.

subsections.title: THE THREE MANORS — PLANAR SHARDS
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Feyward / Shadeward / Material]**

MATERIAL MANOR: Where we are. **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** has established control. The Vigilance renamed the Legionlance. **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** operates in support role. PL1 fracture centred here.

FEYWARD MANOR: Feywild reflection. **[Lady Aurelian Corvinarus](lady_aurelian_corvinarus)** holds court. Eternal parties, drunken satyrs, sprites in greenhouses, a giant Guardian Butterfly, **[Wario](wario)**'s catalogue of absurd merchandise. The broken magic circle under the master bedroom rug connects here — estimated 4 days to repair, aligning with month-end. Sergeant Coldbrook's **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** squad is trapped here with five of original eight soldiers.

SHADEWARD MANOR: Shadowfell reflection. **[Orangus Cornelius](orangus_cornelius)** hosts vampire dinners. The Onyx Hand operates. Monochrome reality. Fire magic doesn't work — **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**'s primary offensive capability was nullified. Green T was held as a 'guest.' The Onyx Knight Kyrn offered friendship to Remi after her allies fled. Vivian haunts the corridors.

subsections.title: THE CORNELIUS FAMILY — COMPILED
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Family Tree & Key Figures]**

DRAGONUS CORNELIUS: Patriarch, 3 generations back. The statuette in the gallery bears his name.

DARIUS CORNELIUS: Orantha's contemporary — possibly husband or brother. Master wizard. The master bedroom desk, the component cabinet, the research journal. Obsessive organiser after losing Ylana. The inscription 'To my beloved daughter, that she may follow in my footsteps' in EC's textbook.

YLANA CORNELIUS (née Annmatar?): Lady of the house. Died — circumstances in the journal. Her furniture was moved to the workshop. Memorial fountain in the hedge maze. The gold bracelet. The music box in the closet. Perrius Annmatar's connection — family name match.

ELSCIETH CORNELIUS (EC): Daughter. Young woman. The battered journal. The pink curtains. Bullied by her little brother. 'AC' — the little brother?

ORANTHA CORNELIUS: **[The Oracle](the_oracle)**. Planar cartographer. Built the mirror gateway. Went through twelve years ago and did not return. Her letter says keep the toad safe.

**[Orangus Cornelius](orangus_cornelius)**: Shadowfell host. Vampire dinner party. Connected to AC? The painting Remi found — a toad petting a dog, possibly **[Orangus Cornelius](orangus_cornelius)**.

AURELIAN CORVINARUS: Feyward lady of the manor. Plays the delicate host. The broken magic circle is in her domain.

intelGains.reason: Thornbury's notes confirm Onyx Hand activities in Shadeward Manor.
Thornbury's notes detail Mages' Guild operations and backup plans.

name: The Mount Ebott Survey: Part II
title: The Mount Ebott Survey: Part II — Flowey's Trap, Sans's Bone Blast, and the Temporal Barrier
type: Combat / First Contact / Relic Retrieval / Magical Crisis
location: Snowdin Village / The Ruins, Mount Ebott
summary: The continuation of the Mount Ebott Survey Expedition. The Legionary Agent recalibrates his machine, uncovers a censored history of 'The Great Void' in his manual, survives an ambush by Flowey the Flower with Mihawk, and is rescued by Sans, who reveals the magical barrier sealing the Underground.
description:
Waluigi is presenting the Day Two log as a continuous play-by-play with interjections because a clean summary cannot carry what this day actually contains. A soldier found a blank notepad and thought nothing of it. A soldier read his own journal and thought even less of it. And then that same soldier destroyed government property with his boot rather than report an anomaly, and somewhere in between he stumbled onto a censorship pattern that makes Waluigi's mustache curl. WAH. Thoroughness is required. Waluigi will be thorough.

## The Room — A Blank Notepad, a Mismatched Key, and Nothing Written Down

The Legionary Agent settled into Room 204 at the Bunny Inn as the artificial sky above Snowdin rolled from orange twilight into deep indigo. He checked the desk. Inkwell, quill, a notepad with a faded blue cover. Indents in the paper suggested someone had written on it before him. He flipped through every page anyway.

Blank. All of it. Crisp, white, untouched.

He checked the drawer beneath. A candle. A matchbox. A key that didn't match the room's lock.

*Waluigi wants this on record because the Agent noticed the indentation — the ghost-pressure of handwriting on a page that no longer holds any ink — and then simply moved on. A trained investigator would have taken a pencil to that page and shaded it to raise the impression. The Agent closed the notepad and looked out the window instead. This is not a criticism of curiosity, of which the Agent has plenty. It is a criticism of follow-through, of which he has none. A mismatched key sat in a drawer three feet from his bed for an entire night and nobody asked what door it opens. WAH.*

He checked his bag. Spare uniform, rations, pocket knife, and his personal journal — leather-bound, filled with his own handwriting. One entry: *'Day 127 of active service. Mission in the Grand Line went well. No casualties on my squad.'* Another, older: *'Still no word from home. Wonder if they're doing okay.'* A sketch of his family a few pages back.

*A private log of a man's own thoughts, and the Agent read it like it belonged to someone else, hunting for clues in his own handwriting. Waluigi finds this oddly endearing and oddly damning at once — a man so unmoored from his own paperwork that even his own diary gets treated as evidence. WAH.*

## The Data Pad — 48% Complete, and a Discrepancy Nobody Questioned Correctly

He checked the survey data pad. **Survey Progress: 48% Complete.** Beneath it: **Biological Activity — Low. No large lifeforms detected beyond standard underground flora and fauna.**

The Agent had spent the previous day meeting an inn full of people. He noticed the contradiction himself — *'that's odd, there was plenty of people I met here, are they not biological?'* — and reasoned his way to the correct hypothesis unassisted: the ambient magic sustaining Snowdin's fake sun and fake snow was very likely interfering with the sensors.

*Waluigi wants full credit given where it is due, because it is due so rarely: this was good reasoning, arrived at without prompting, without the book, without Dracule. The Agent identified a magical-interference hypothesis for a sensor discrepancy in an underground monster civilization, on his own, at nearly midnight, alone in a bedroom. This is, by a wide margin, the single most competent moment of Day Two. Waluigi is issuing this compliment now because it will not come up again for some time. WAH.*

He got dressed, put on his scarf, and left the inn at night to go fix it himself.

## The Machine — Recalibration, a Printed Report, and the Boot That Changed Everything

He found the survey machine still humming at the edge of town. He crouched, checked the interface — **Biological Signature Scan: Active** — and recalibrated the sensitivity himself, correctly compensating for the interference he'd already diagnosed. **Recalibrating... Please wait.**

He printed a manual report. **Snowdin Biological Survey — Preliminary Findings. Population Density: 30 inhabitants per square kilometer. Biological Signature Strength: Extremely low.** And beneath it, in smaller type, the honest caveat: **'Possible magical interference affecting scan accuracy.'**

He checked his Legion book for anything on magical ecosystems and found a direct warning: removing or disrupting a magical foundation an entire civilization depends on can be catastrophic for everyone living inside it. He read it, understood it, and correctly concluded that scrubbing the magic out of Snowdin was a terrible idea.

*So far, so reasonable. He then fell asleep sitting next to the machine in the snow, which Sans found mildly funny and Waluigi finds mildly concerning, but this is a minor entry compared to what happens next. WAH.*

Sans woke him around 7 AM, and over the course of a genuinely pleasant conversation — about the artificial sun, about a signed Iron Legion book from a 'General Caine,' about the Agent's own probationary status and his admission that he joined the Legion for the pay rather than any calling — the Agent learned that King Asgore and Queen Toriel run a peaceful, decades-stable Underground, and that Sans himself has no fixed job beyond 'living here' and fixing things when they break.

*Sans, notably, fixes things when they break. The Agent, notably, does the opposite. Hold that thought. WAH.*

After Sans left, the Agent looked back at the machine, remembered its warning about magical interference, and had a thought:

*'I wonder if I can scrub it out — make it say it's good — so I won't get in trouble.'*

He checked his own protocol manual, which explicitly listed the correct, sanctioned remedies — hard reset, admin-code data wipe, external recalibration tool — and explicitly warned: **'Do not tamper with data unless authorized by commanding officer.'** He then reasoned that since he was, technically, the ranking officer present, he had authorization to do whatever he wanted. He selected none of the three sanctioned options.

He kicked it.

*Waluigi needs several sentences to do this justice. The manual was open. In his hands. Physically open to the correct page, listing three non-destructive remedies, with an explicit written warning against exactly the kind of unauthorized tampering he was about to commit. He read the warning. He appointed himself the authorizing officer he needed to bypass the warning. And then, having granted himself permission via a chain of command consisting entirely of himself, he did not choose any of the three approved fixes. He kicked a multi-thousand-coin piece of Legion survey equipment with his boot. WAH.*

The screen glitched. **WARNING: Equipment damage detected.** Readings jumped to **ERROR — DATA CORRUPTED.** Smoke curled from a vent. **'ERROR – SYSTEM FAILURE. DATA LOST.'**

*'Haha, it's clear, no magical anomalies,'* the Agent said, and exported the corrupted findings as a completed survey, satisfied.

*He did not clear the anomaly. He destroyed the only instrument capable of measuring it, and then filed the resulting silence as a clean result. This is not evidence tampering in the clever, deliberate sense the protocol manual was warning against — this is a man solving an inconvenient data point with blunt force and then mistaking the wreckage for an answer. Waluigi has seen incompetence. Waluigi has rarely seen incompetence this proud of itself immediately afterward. WAH.*

## The Book — A Censored Calendar and One Surviving Date

Walking out with Dracule Mihawk, the Agent produced a folded World Government newspaper Dracule was carrying — headline: **'Grand Line Pirates Clash Near Mary Geoise — Navy Warlords Mobilized.'** A smaller line beneath: **'Mysterious Energy Surge Detected Near Laugh Tale Island.'** Dated 2384, World Government Standard.

The Agent, unfamiliar with WGS and used only to Regal Empire Standard, went hunting through his own Iron Legion book for a conversion chart — and found one. **WGS 2384 = REIC [REDACTED: Data Expunged].** A black ink blot over the exact figure.

He checked the year above it. Redacted. He checked the year below it. Redacted. He kept flipping, reading every entry aloud — 2383, 2385, 2370, 2360, 2350 — and every single Regal Empire equivalent had been blacked out, without exception, going back for decades.

*Waluigi must pause the play-by-play here because this is, without competition, the most important discovery of the entire day, and it happened entirely by accident, as a byproduct of a conversation about newspaper dates. The Agent was not investigating Legion secrecy. He stumbled into a censorship pattern this total, this systematic, purely because a Warlord handed him a newspaper and he wanted to convert the date. Every single calendar-conversion entry in an official Iron Legion training manual, across decades, redacted with total uniformity. This is not an editorial oversight. Nobody blacks out thirty consecutive years of calendar arithmetic by accident. Someone wanted every soldier who ever cracked this book to be permanently unable to place Regal Empire history against a fixed timeline. WAH.*

One entry survived. A single hand-penciled date in the margin of a later chapter, 'Significant Dates of World History,' scrawled rather than printed, with a note beside it in black pen: **'Do Not Mention — Not For General Knowledge.'** Above the smudged numbers, three words:

**'...The Great Void.'**

Dracule confirmed it was real — centuries old, before his time, a catastrophic event nobody discusses openly, deliberately kept from a generation too young to have lived through it.

*One surviving date, in pencil, hand-annotated with an explicit instruction to suppress it, sitting inside a book that has otherwise scrubbed every calendar entry it contains. Someone wanted this one line to survive the redaction. Someone left it there on purpose, as a note to whoever eventually went looking hard enough to find it. Waluigi does not yet know who that someone was. Waluigi intends to find out. WAH.*

## The Decision to Go Back — Lying to the Legion, and a Newspaper Left Unread

Rattled by both the broken machine and the censorship, the Agent made his second and more defensible bad call of the day: rather than report a corrupted dataset and risk execution for equipment sabotage, he decided to go back and fix what he'd broken, on Dracule's advice to simply claim the machine malfunctioned on its own.

In the same breath, the two of them acknowledged this was likely their final trip together, and — in a rare moment of warmth from Dracule — agreed they should do something big before parting ways. Neither of them settled on what.

*Waluigi notes, with some sympathy, that this is the first entirely human moment of the entire log — two soldiers, quietly aware a partnership is ending, unable to name what they want to do about it. Waluigi will not mock this part. WAH.*

## Flowey — A Trip, a Stomp, and Vines That Would Not Stop Growing

Walking back, dismissing Dracule's warning that the underground's apparent hostility could turn without notice — *'these monsters seem non-hostile,'* the Agent said — he tripped over a vine. A yellow flower with a face sat in the grass. It introduced itself, cheerfully, as Flowey.

Its smile twisted. Its voice dropped. It called the two of them outsiders, claimed the Underground as its domain, and promised to show them 'what happens when outsiders don't know their place.'

Dracule stomped it flat without hesitation. It screamed and went silent.

*This lasted exactly as long as it takes vines to finish growing. WAH.*

Vines erupted from the ground around Dracule's ankles the instant his foot lifted. More followed, aimed at both of them. Dracule's sword cut through them cleanly — and more grew back from the stumps immediately. The Agent tried his Legion manual for answers mid-fight and found nothing useful, and threw the book aside in frustration.

*The book that redacted three decades of calendar history had, predictably, nothing to say about carnivorous flowers. The Agent discarding it mid-combat is, Waluigi feels, the correct instinct arrived at for once. WAH.*

He called for Sans.

## Sans, Two Ketchup Bottles, and a Bone Attack

Sans appeared instantly — he'd been watching the fight from a distance the whole time — took one look at Dracule tangled in vines, and calmly assessed: *'that's definitely not a weed.'* A glowing bone materialized under Dracule's feet and detonated upward, shredding the vines holding him.

The Agent charged in with his sword the same moment, and between the two attacks the flower's assault broke apart into smoke.

Dracule, freed, immediately turned his suspicion on Sans rather than the flower: *'You were following us.'* Sans admitted it without denial — *'curiosity'* — and didn't elaborate further.

*Sans lied by omission and everyone in the scene knew it and let it go, because there was a much bigger problem still standing in front of them. Waluigi will return to what Sans is actually watching for at a later date. WAH.*

## The Escape — Dragged by the Hand, All the Way to the Ruins

With the vines recovering and lashing out again, the Agent made the single most physically decisive choice of the day: he grabbed Dracule Mihawk in one hand, Sans in the other, and simply ran — hauling a Warlord of the Sea by the wrist like luggage, at a dead sprint, through the forest and through a cave door into the Ruins.

Dracule did not resist. He also did not forgive it. *'This is undignified,'* he said, more than once, jaw tight the entire way.

*Waluigi wishes to note, for the permanent record, that on this same day the Agent personally destroyed a piece of Legion equipment with his boot and also personally hand-dragged one of the most dangerous swordsmen in the world to safety by main force, without asking permission, and succeeded at the second thing completely. Waluigi does not know what to do with a man capable of both of these outcomes inside a single twelve-hour period. WAH.*

Safe inside the Ruins, Sans explained the situation plainly: the Underground is sealed from the surface by ancient magical barriers that no ID, checkpoint, or Legion credential can pass. The only known routes out are the CORE (dangerous), unstable Hotland portals, or personal royal approval from Toriel or Asgore — approval neither is inclined to grant freely.

Dracule, asked if he had any alternative, admitted flatly: *'None.'*

*And there the day ends: two operatives with a corrupted dataset, a censored history book with one deliberately-surviving date, and no confirmed way home. Waluigi is documenting all of it, because incompetence and conspiracy this thoroughly tangled together deserve a thorough record. WAH.*

intelGains.reason: Observations of censored calendars and the Great Void.

name: The Mount Ebott Survey: Part III
title: The Mount Ebott Survey: Part III — The War Slip, Koffin-K's Iron Legion, and Flowey's Repaired Machine
type: Memory Suppression / Team Formation / Civic Incident / Survey Machine Tampering
era: The Old World Crisis — Subterranean Contact Arc
location: The Ruins / Snowdin Town / Abandoned Snowdin Police Station, Mount Ebott
status: Filed as its own Ebott session; marked for continuing review before Hotland transit.
summary: Day Three turns the Mount Ebott survey into a diplomatic and evidentiary crisis: Sans slips and mentions “the war,” Flowey is identified as Asgore’s dead firstborn son and suspected machine technician, and Mihawk’s casual use of the Iron Legion name creates an unauthorized cell inside the Underground. Koffin-K’s real minions and temporary Snowdin hero status expose an authority vacuum, while Flowey’s repaired survey machine and the extracted data chip leave both factions with reasons to distrust the next report.
description:
Waluigi is treating this session as its own dedicated file rather than folding it into Day Two, because it introduces an entire new character, an entire new team, and an entire new theory that reframes several things Waluigi thought he understood about the Underground's power structure. He will proceed in order. He will not skip the mouse. WAH.

## Arrival at the Ruins — 'It's Not Like the Humans Above Would Want Us There Anyway'

Sans led the Agent and Dracule Mihawk into the Ruins proper — a chamber lit by glowing blue torches, worn stonework, the drip of unseen water. He sat down on a crumbling pillar like he owned it. When Dracule asked, with clear distaste, whether they were 'staying here for the night,' Sans corrected him: it was still morning. It was just an expression.

What followed was the single most important piece of worldbuilding exposition the Agent has received since arriving underground, and Waluigi wants it laid out cleanly before he starts pulling at its threads.

Sans explained, plainly: the Underground is sealed from the surface. Not by checkpoints, not by anything a Legion ID could get past — by 'ancient seals,' magical in nature, that keep the two worlds apart. There are exactly three known ways past them: the CORE (dangerous), unstable Hotland portals (unpredictable), or personal royal approval from Toriel or Asgore, who 'don't just hand that kind of permission out freely.' Sans added, almost as an aside, that the humans on the surface 'don't even remember' the Underground exists anymore. *'It's like... history erased itself,'* he said, with what the Agent's own account describes as genuine resignation.

*Waluigi wants to connect this directly to the redacted calendar the Agent found in his own Iron Legion manual the night before. 'History erased itself,' Sans said. Not 'we were forgotten.' Not 'humans lost interest.' Erased. That is an oddly precise word for a skeleton who supposedly has no formal education past 'sometimes fixing things around town.' And it is, Waluigi notes with rising suspicion, exactly the word Waluigi himself would use to describe thirty consecutive years of blacked-out calendar conversions in a document the Legion is still actively reprinting today. Sans is describing the outcome of the Agent's own book from the outside. Either this is coincidence, or the erasure the Legion performed on its own soldiers and the erasure that cut the Underground off from surface memory are the same erasure, performed by the same hand, for the same reason. Waluigi is not yet willing to commit to that theory in ink. He is willing to write it down anyway. WAH.*

## The Slip — 'The War'

And then, almost in passing, Sans said something he should not have said.

Explaining the barriers were 'ancient seals, magical in nature,' Sans described them, unprompted, as basic knowledge — the kind of thing anyone in his position would simply know. Then, describing Asgore and Toriel's decades of peace, he said the peace 'has lasted for decades,' has been 'stable since Asgore took the throne.' Fine so far. But earlier — Waluigi is drawing on the Agent's memory of the Day One crash-site log — Sans had already told the Agent that 'peace has lasted for decades' and hesitated when asked if it would continue. Nothing about a war, at that point.

Then, in this session, when the Agent — reeling from the discovery of Flowey's true origin — asked about Asgore's dead son, Sans mentioned, without flinching, that the child died 'before the war even started.'

The Agent caught it immediately: *'the war? you said earlier there was no war.'*

And Sans froze. Not hesitated — froze. His eye sockets, per the Agent's own description, went completely dark, no glow, no light, 'just hollow voids,' for the first time in the entire relationship. When his eyes came back, they were dimmer than before. *'...i said that?'* he asked, genuinely bewildered by his own memory. *'guess i lied,'* he finally said. *'or maybe someone else did.'*

*Waluigi needs several long paragraphs for this, because it is, without exaggeration, the single most significant thing that has happened to the Agent since he arrived in the Underground, more significant than the redacted book, more significant than Flowey, more significant even than the payload — Waluigi is borrowing his own vocabulary from a different case file here on purpose, because the pattern rhymes and he wants that rhyme on record.*

*Consider what actually happened. Sans did not simply misspeak. Sans did not correct himself smoothly the way people do when they catch a slip of the tongue. His eye sockets went dark — a physical, involuntary reaction, the kind of thing that happens to a body when something underneath its conscious control gets touched. And then he could not remember having said there was no war. Not 'I misspoke earlier.' Not 'I meant something else.' He asked the Agent, sincerely, whether he had actually said it — as though checking a fact he did not have direct access to. And his own conclusion, offered without prompting, was not 'I was wrong,' but 'guess i lied... or maybe someone else did.'*

*Waluigi wants to sit with that phrase specifically: or maybe someone else did. Sans is not confident the lie originated with him. He is entertaining, out loud, in front of two armed strangers, the possibility that a false statement came out of his own mouth without his own authorship. Waluigi has exactly one other data point in this entire investigation that behaves the same way — a single surviving, hand-penciled calendar entry inside an otherwise uniformly redacted Legion manual, accompanied by a note that reads 'Do Not Mention,' written by someone who was clearly not the same authority that ordered the rest of the book scrubbed. Waluigi is now forced to consider the possibility that there is a standing, active suppression mechanism operating in this world that is not limited to printed documents — that it can also sit inside a living mind and silently substitute a comfortable lie ('no war') for an inconvenient truth ('there was a war, Asgore lost a son to it or near it, and something about that loss twisted the magic around the child badly enough to produce Flowey'). If that is true, Sans is not hiding information from the Agent. Sans does not have full access to his own information. That is a substantially more frightening possibility than a skeleton simply being cagey, and Waluigi intends to keep testing it. WAH.*

Mihawk, notably, tensed at this exchange 'more than normal' — the Agent's own words — and stepped directly into Sans's space to press: *'You lied. There was war.'* Not a question. Waluigi appreciates that Mihawk, alone among the three of them, treated the moment with the gravity it deserved rather than letting it pass as a funny bit.

## Flowey's Origin — A Prince, a Death, and a Magic That Went Wrong

Before the slip fully registered, Sans had already delivered the other major revelation of the session: Flowey was not always a flower. He was Asgore's firstborn son, dead before whatever war Sans cannot consistently remember either having or not having occurred. Something went wrong with the magic around the child at the moment of death — 'soul split, twisted, don't ask me, I didn't see it happen' — and what remains, in Sans's own bitter words, is 'that damn flower... full of rage and lies.'

*Waluigi wants to note the timing here precisely, because timing is doing a great deal of work in this scene that dialogue alone does not capture. Sans delivers the Flowey origin story calmly, seriously, but coherently — full sentences, clear cause and effect, a story he has clearly told himself before even if he has never told it to a stranger. It is only one exchange later, when the Agent pulls on the thread of 'the war,' that Sans's composure actually breaks. The son's death he can discuss. The war that killed him, or happened near enough to him, he apparently cannot hold onto as a stable fact in his own head. Waluigi's working theory: whatever mechanism is suppressing 'the war' as a topic is doing so specifically, not generally — it is not blanking Sans's memory of history broadly, it is targeting one particular fact that the rest of the story depends on. Someone did not want the Underground's residents forgetting that a royal child died. They wanted them forgetting why. WAH.*

## The Hideout — Koffin-K, a Bad Lie About a 'Notebook,' and a Fedora That Turned Out to Contain a Real Organization

A figure was caught watching them from a corner of the Ruins. The Agent threw a can at him to flush him out. What emerged was Koffin-K — a talking, animate hat-and-coat ensemble, self-described comic-book supervillain, terrible liar, who first claimed to be 'surveying the surveyor' (there is no other surveyor, and everyone present knew it instantly), then produced a fictional notebook of survey data he did not have.

When the group followed him to his actual hideout to 'prove' the notebook existed, they found instead a genuine, if pathetic, hideout: candles, scribbled notes, hand-drawn maps of the Underground, a cot, a cluttered desk. No notebook. Confronted directly by Mihawk — *'You do not have notes'* — Koffin-K finally admitted the truth: he had been watching the group not out of any villainous agenda, but because he was lonely.

*Waluigi is not going to be cruel about this, because loneliness is not a crime and Koffin-K's confession reads, in the transcript, as genuinely vulnerable. But Waluigi does want to flag something the Agent appears to have missed entirely in the moment: Koffin-K had hand-drawn maps of the Underground on his walls. Maps are not something a lonely hermit draws for company. Maps are something you draw when you are tracking movement, planning routes, or documenting territory. A person who is simply lonely keeps photographs, letters, mementos. A person who keeps maps is keeping intelligence. Waluigi is not accusing Koffin-K of anything sinister — his subsequent behavior across this entire session argues strongly against any real menace — but Waluigi notes that 'I was just lonely' and 'I have hand-drawn maps of this entire region papering my walls' are not, strictly speaking, the same confession, and nobody in the room asked him to reconcile the two. WAH.*

## The Comic Book Confession — Crossbones, and a Villain Career Born from a Business Failure

Koffin-K's backstory, once he relaxed: he used to run a comic store selling comics discarded by humans on the surface — meaning, notably, that discarded human media reaches the Underground somehow, a supply chain Waluigi finds worth flagging given everything else about how thoroughly sealed this place is supposed to be. His store failed when a rival hero-comic franchise, Crossbones, drew his customers away. He tried to pitch the creators a 'proper adversary' concept for Crossbones, spilled coffee on his own pitch material, and — rather than give up — simply decided to become Crossbones's arch-nemesis in real life, without anyone's permission, including presumably Crossbones's.

*Waluigi finds this the funniest and saddest thing in the entire session, and wants to note the structural similarity to something Waluigi has now seen twice: a person encountering an institutional or narrative rejection and responding not by walking away but by unilaterally appointing himself into the role he wanted anyway. The Agent authorized himself as his own commanding officer to justify kicking a machine. Koffin-K authorized himself as a supervillain nobody hired him to be. Waluigi is beginning to suspect that self-appointment under a thin veneer of legitimacy is simply how every character the Agent meets solves the problem of not actually having power. WAH.*

## Founding the Team — 'The Iron Legion,' Chosen by Mihawk, Over Koffin-K's Objections

What followed was a genuinely chaotic team-naming sequence: Sans lazily proposing 'The Underground Brigade,' 'The Legionaries,' 'The Shadow Syndicate,' 'The Black Brigade' in succession, each rejected by an increasingly theatrical Koffin-K demanding something 'that strikes fear into Crossbones' heart.' Mihawk, out of patience, ended the debate unilaterally: *'From this moment forward, we are known as the Iron Legion.'* No vote. No debate permitted. Koffin-K, cowed by Mihawk's expression, accepted it grumbling.

*Waluigi wants this on record for one specific reason: the actual Iron Legion — the Agent's own employer, the organization whose manual has been censoring calendar data for decades — now has an unauthorized splinter cell operating under its name in the Ruins, composed of a Warlord of the Sea, a skeleton sentry of uncertain loyalty, a self-appointed supervillain, and a probationary field agent who broke his own equipment two days ago. None of them asked the actual Iron Legion for permission to use its name. Waluigi finds it almost too perfect that an organization built on quietly appropriating and redacting the truth has now had its own name quietly appropriated by four people with no official standing whatsoever, entirely by accident, because a skeleton couldn't think of anything better. WAH.*

The Agent then read aloud from his own manual that Legionnaires receive housing, food, and a stipend — and Koffin-K's entire demeanor transformed on the spot, from reluctant villain to eager recruit, delighted that 'evil' could come with a paycheck and a roof.

*Waluigi does not find this funny so much as diagnostic. A supposedly hardened self-styled supervillain abandoned his entire ideological posture within one sentence upon learning there might be dental. Waluigi suspects this says less about Koffin-K's commitment to villainy and more about how thin the difference between 'joining a legion' and 'joining a gang' really is once you strip away the uniforms — a point the Agent himself, by his own earlier confession to Sans that he joined 'for the promise of easy high pay,' has already conceded about his own reasons for signing up. Koffin-K and the Agent are, in this specific and narrow respect, the same person. WAH.*

## The Minions Were Real

When the group reached the Ruins exit, two shadows resolved into actual guards, who addressed Koffin-K as 'Boss' with what appeared to be genuine, trained deference. This came as a surprise to everyone, including — visibly — Koffin-K himself, who had spent the entire prior conversation implying his minions were an exaggeration or an outright fabrication.

When pressed on what these minions had supposedly been 'preparing' for him, both guards visibly panicked, unable to produce an answer, and Koffin-K was forced to improvise a cover story about a 'big surprise' on the spot — a lie built on top of a lie that turned out to be sitting on top of an actual, real chain of command.

*Waluigi wants this contradiction stated as plainly as possible because it is genuinely strange and nobody in the scene stopped to interrogate it: Koffin-K did not appear to know, with certainty, whether he had real subordinates until he was standing in front of them. That is not how command structures work for anyone who actually built them. You do not forget you have henchmen. Either these two guards were assigned to Koffin-K by some other authority without his full knowledge or consent — meaning someone else in the Underground's power structure is quietly propping up a self-declared 'villain' with actual personnel, for reasons of their own — or Koffin-K's own grip on reality regarding his own operation is considerably less stable than his fedora suggests. Waluigi is inclined, cautiously, toward the first explanation, because it rhymes with everything else in this file: things that should not be real, quietly turning out to be real, the moment someone actually checks. The redacted date was real. The war was real. Now the minions are real. Waluigi is starting to form a rule of thumb: in this Underground, every offhand lie the Agent's companions tell has, so far, turned out to be a suppressed truth. WAH.*

## Snowdin Reconsidered — 'You Said It Was Small'

Walking through the town proper for the first time with an entourage, the Agent noted, twice, that Snowdin looked considerably larger than Sans had originally described it — larger streets, more buildings, more visible population than the 'quiet, mostly empty' picture Sans had painted back at the crash site and again inside the Ruins. Sans's only response, both times, was a flat, unbothered *'yeah, it's a bigger town than it seems.'*

*Waluigi wants to flag this because it is a small discrepancy sitting directly next to two much larger ones from the same day, and Waluigi has learned, over the course of compiling this file, not to let small discrepancies slide simply because they are small. A town that is materially bigger than its own resident sentry described it as being, to a newly arrived outside agent, conducting a biological survey. Waluigi does not know yet whether Sans undersold Snowdin's size out of habit, out of the same suppression mechanism that ate 'the war,' or out of a straightforward desire to keep a Legion surveyor from taking the place too seriously. But given everything else in this file, Waluigi is no longer willing to file this under 'idle chit-chat.' WAH.*

## The Thief, the Tackle, and a Machine That Fixed Itself

Spotting someone near the abandoned survey machine, the Agent, Mihawk, and Sans gave chase — Mihawk running the fleeing figure down with what the Agent describes as predatory precision, cutting off every turn before the thief finally face-planted into a snowbank. Cornered, the thief turned out to be nothing more than a frightened bystander who claimed only to have wanted to see how the machine worked.

Koffin-K, arriving late with his two very real henchmen, seized the moment for a full theatrical villain monologue and 'sentencing' — the punishment ultimately revealed to be forcing the thief to listen to an hour of Koffin-K's monologuing, a bit that undercuts, deliberately, everything tense about the chase that preceded it.

But the actual substance of the encounter was not the thief. It was the machine.

When the Agent checked the machine's status, expecting to confirm the damage from his own boot the night before, the screen instead reported **98% system integrity — minor surface scratches only.** No critical damage. Someone had fixed it. And tucked against the underside of the unit, previously unnoticed, was a length of vine.

*Waluigi needs to slow down considerably here, because this is the actual center of gravity of the entire session and everything before it — the war, Koffin-K, the minions, the town size — has been circling it without quite landing.*

*The Agent destroyed this machine deliberately, with his boot, specifically so its corrupted data would not reveal the sensor discrepancy he'd found the night before. That act of sabotage is now undone. Someone repaired Legion survey equipment to full working order overnight, in the open, on a road, without being seen by anyone in the group — and left behind, as the only trace, a vine belonging to a flower that the Agent and Mihawk had personally stomped, ambushed, fled from, and left for dead less than a day earlier.*

*Waluigi wants the full implication of this stated without softening. Flowey is not merely alive despite being crushed underfoot — Waluigi already suspected as much, given how quickly the vines regrew during the ambush. Flowey found the broken machine, understood what it was, repaired it well enough to pass a full diagnostic, and then deliberately left evidence of his own involvement rather than hiding it. This is not vandalism. This is not idle mischief. This is a message, composed in the one language the Agent cannot misread: I found the thing you broke to hide your mistake. I fixed it. I want you to know I fixed it. Mihawk said as much himself, once the vine was found — 'he wanted us to know he tampered with it' — and Waluigi agrees completely, but wants to push the analysis one full step further than Mihawk did. A flower capable of finding, diagnosing, and repairing complex Legion survey electronics to full 98% integrity, overnight, unsupervised, possesses a level of technical competence that nothing else in this file has prepared Waluigi for. Not menace. Competence. Whatever Flowey actually is — a twisted remnant of a dead prince, per Sans's account — he is demonstrably smarter and more capable with human/Legion technology than the trained Legion Agent he ambushed. WAH.*

*Waluigi also wants to note what this repair means for the earlier cover-up. The Agent kicked the machine specifically to bury a magical-interference discrepancy before the Legion could see it. Flowey's repair has now restored the machine to full function — meaning the original discrepancy the Agent was trying to hide is, in principle, fully recoverable again. If the Agent generates a new report now, he is not generating a false all-clear over a still-broken machine. He is generating a real reading, from working equipment, that could just as easily reproduce the original 'why are these thirty biological monsters barely registering as biological' anomaly he was trying to bury in the first place. Flowey did not just fix a machine. Flowey handed the Agent back the exact problem he thought he'd destroyed the evidence of. Whether that was intentional on Flowey's part, Waluigi cannot yet say. Waluigi suspects it was. WAH.*

The factional problem is not background decoration; it is the practical reason every apparently small choice in this file matters. Gamma Division entered Mount Ebott as the forward edge of an Iron Legion institution that measures first and asks permission later. The Monster Underground, meanwhile, is not an empty dungeon for a surveyor to catalogue. It is a hidden monarchy with its own barrier, its own local settlement, its own informal sentries, and a population whose surface history has been actively lost, suppressed, or both. The moment Mihawk calls a handful of unaffiliated travelers “the Iron Legion,” he turns a private joke into a diplomatic liability. A Snowdin resident does not need to know the difference between an authorized division, a lost Gamma agent, a Warlord with a sword, and a lonely hat with two henchmen. They only need to hear the name of the force that has arrived from above. Waluigi’s conclusion is therefore sharper than “the team name was unauthorized”: it was an unannounced claim of institutional presence inside a sealed foreign realm. That is how accidental occupations begin — not with a flag, but with someone using a powerful name because it sounds impressive. WAH.

The Iron Legion itself has a particular reason to fear that mistake. Its authority is built on documents, rank, supply, and the assertion that a stamped identity tells everyone where they belong. The Agent’s own manual supplies food, housing support, and a stipend; Koffin-K hears those benefits and immediately hears belonging. That response is funny until Waluigi notices the recruitment mechanism hiding inside it. The Legion does not merely purchase labor. It offers people a place in a world where being lonely, poor, or directionless makes a place feel like a miracle. Koffin-K’s enthusiasm is not proof that he is secretly evil; it is evidence that material security can turn a person’s performance of villainy into a genuine political attachment overnight. The Agent’s earlier faith in his Legion identification follows the same logic. Both of them mistake an institution’s promise of shelter for proof that the institution is safe, and both are now standing inside a kingdom whose history may have been damaged by exactly that kind of institution.

Waluigi also refuses to discard the supposedly throwaway mouse-hole incident. Koffin-K announces that villainy requires petty cruelty, attempts the smallest possible version of a prank, and then forgets to run when a mouse actually comes out to meet him. He cannot maintain the role once a real creature responds. That does not absolve him of his lies, his surveillance, or his appetite for theatrical authority. It does establish a useful limit: Koffin-K is trying to become the kind of villain he thinks a comic demands, while his actual instincts keep revealing a lonely person who wants an audience, a minion, a friend, or even a mouse to acknowledge him. The distinction matters because Flowey is the opposite case. Flowey does not need an audience to make a threat meaningful. He leaves the vine when nobody is watching. One performs menace in public; the other manufactures consequences in private. Anybody filing both under “villain” has learned nothing from the encounter.

There is another geographical discrepancy worth preserving rather than smoothing over. Sans calls the first chamber the Ruins, then later treats Snowdin’s roads, exits, and surrounding old structures as if the boundaries are obvious; the Agent experiences the route as a continual slide from cave to ruin to town rather than a clean sequence of territories. This could simply be the practical language of a local guide. It could also reveal how a sealed realm organizes space differently from a surface map: old ruins are not a distant archaeological site but the connective tissue of daily life, and Snowdin’s ordinary homes, patrol routes, abandoned police station, and royal barrier all sit on top of one another. For a Legion survey mission, this is a warning. A map that divides the Underground into tidy operational zones may be administratively convenient while being socially false. The route to Hotland is not just a route; it crosses jurisdictions, memories, infrastructure, and people who may not agree on what their own borders are called.

Koffin-K’s hideout belongs in that same reading. The cot, candles, scavenged papers, maps, and desk are not evidence that he commands a secret empire. They are evidence that he has been trying to make himself legible to himself. But the real maps and the real henchmen mean the performance has acquired infrastructure. Lanky and Bulky — names still unverified, roles still unfiled — obey him, guard an exit, and help him project force even when neither they nor their boss can explain the supposed “surprise” they were preparing. Waluigi will not invent a conspiracy merely because a fedora looks suspicious. He will say what the record supports: an unrecognized Ruins/Snowdin cell exists; its leader is emotionally unreliable but not imaginary; its personnel are real; and its relationship to Snowdin’s civic structures and the Underground monarchy is unknown. That is enough to justify a faction file, not enough to justify declaring a coup.

The same caution applies to the Snowdin crowd. Their applause after Flowey’s capture is not a legal transfer of government, and Koffin-K’s speech does not make him king. The earlier draft of this file let the comedy of “crowning a fedora” outrun the evidence. What actually happens is still revealing: frightened residents respond to a visible rescue, a cage, two posing henchmen, and a confident narrative of protection. In a town facing an immediate threat, that is not irrational; it is the ordinary human-and-monster instinct to reward the person who appears to have restored control. The missed detail is that no official watch, royal representative, or civic authority visibly arrives to correct the story. Sans is present, but he does not publicly claim institutional authority. That silence leaves a vacuum Koffin-K can fill for fifteen minutes. It does not prove Snowdin has no government. It proves that, at the exact moment authority needed to be visible, spectacle was faster than procedure.

The diagnostic deserves one final qualification as well. “No anomalies or damage detected” is a machine result, not an exoneration. The Agent extracts the data chip, so the group does preserve the one portable piece of evidence that can later be compared against the damaged packet, the 98-percent repair state, and any future scan. That is better than leaving every record behind. It is still not enough. A successful diagnostic can establish that the machine is presently operational; it cannot establish who repaired it, what was changed before the test, whether the original sensor discrepancy has been normalized, or whether Flowey understands the device’s reporting thresholds better than its owner. Waluigi’s recommendation is boring because boring is what evidence requires: compare the extracted chip against a pre-repair baseline, establish chain of custody, and do not accept an all-clear from a device whose last known technician was an adversarial flower. Anybody who calls that paranoia has not been reading the same file.

Finally, the decision to leave Flowey and the machine together is not merely an evidence-handling error. It creates a pressure point between factions. If the Iron Legion later retrieves its equipment, it may interpret a repaired device, missing Agent, extracted chip, and unauthorized “Iron Legion” entourage as sabotage or desertion. If the Underground discovers the station first, it may see a caged royal remnant beside foreign survey hardware and reasonably conclude that the surface intruders are conducting experiments. If Flowey escapes, he gains both a grievance and a story in which every side has handed him a useful symbol. The group is not heading toward Hotland with a clean mission anymore. It is walking away from a locked room full of competing narratives, each of which can become a weapon before anyone returns. Waluigi is recording that now, because the people in the room were too busy escaping the snow to do it themselves. WAH.

## Capture and Coronation — Koffin-K Becomes Snowdin's Hero for Roughly Fifteen Minutes

Screaming from the town center sent the group running toward the square, where Flowey was found perched above a statue of a child holding a flower — an image Waluigi will return to, because a statue of a child with a flower sitting in a town whose sentry just confirmed a royal child died and became a flower is not a coincidence Waluigi is prepared to let pass without comment, even briefly, even in a session already this dense.

The group cornered Flowey through a combination of a thrown machine part, Koffin-K's theme song blaring from a megaphone as a genuine and effective distraction, and a full-group physical effort to uproot him from the ground entirely — roots and all — before caging him in a reinforced metal box Koffin-K produced from his coat.

What followed was the strangest political event of the entire log: Koffin-K, cage in hand, turned to the frightened townspeople and declared himself their savior, crediting his own 'might, intellect, and heroic action' for Flowey's capture. The crowd — after a beat of silence — began applauding, then cheering, then treating him as a legitimate civic hero. Within minutes he was accepting worship, signing autographs, and openly considering declaring himself ruler of Snowdin, weighing it seriously against the appeal of continuing on to Hotland with the group.

*Waluigi wants to take this section more seriously than its comedic tone invites, because Waluigi has now watched, twice in one session, a completely unofficial figure acquire real authority within seconds of simply claiming it in front of a crowd — first the two minions treating Koffin-K as 'Boss' despite his own uncertainty about whether they were real, and now an entire town treating him as a hero and prospective ruler on the strength of one dramatic speech. Waluigi is forced to ask what this says about how authority actually functions in Snowdin, and by extension in the wider Underground: if a stranger in a fedora can talk his way into becoming a town's self-declared savior in under a minute, with no resistance, no skepticism, no request for credentials — what does that suggest about how the actual monarchy, Toriel and Asgore, originally acquired and have since maintained their own authority? Waluigi is not accusing anyone of anything. Waluigi is simply noting that a population this quick to crown a fedora is not a population Waluigi would describe as possessing strong institutional skepticism, and a monarchy operating over such a population would face very little friction in maintaining whatever version of history it preferred its subjects to believe. This connects, Waluigi believes, directly back to the redacted calendar and to Sans's own inability to hold onto the fact of a war. A population this suggestible does not need active enforcement to forget something. It only needs to be told, gently, once, and it will do the forgetting itself. WAH.*

Koffin-K ultimately chose the group over the crown, declaring — with a straight face — that villains 'can be heroes too,' that this was simply 'multitasking,' and that wanting to leave Snowdin for Hotland was itself 'my evil plan.' Sans's verdict, delivered flatly: *'man's got issues.'* Mihawk's own assessment, when asked directly whether Koffin-K had simply seized control of an entire city: *'He did indeed,'* delivered in what the Agent describes as genuine disbelief.

*Waluigi wants to close this section by noting that nobody in the group — not the Agent, not Mihawk, not Sans — treated 'a stranger just became the unelected ruler of a town in fifteen minutes and then immediately abandoned the position out of boredom' as a matter requiring any follow-up whatsoever. They used it, correctly, as convenient cover to leave without scrutiny, and then simply moved on. Waluigi is going to be the only one in this entire compilation who writes down that this should not have been possible, and that the ease with which it happened is itself a finding. WAH.*

## Storage — Flowey and the Machine, Locked Together in an Abandoned Police Station

Before departing for Hotland, the group made the decision to leave both the caged Flowey and the newly-repaired survey machine behind, rather than carry either into unknown territory. Sans directed them to an abandoned police station at the edge of Snowdin — dusty, broken-windowed, clearly untouched for years — where the Agent finally ran a full, honest diagnostic on the machine. The result: **'Diagnostics complete. No anomalies or damage detected. Functioning normally.'** The Agent extracted the data chip. The cage, with Flowey still furious and shouting inside it, was left on the floor beside the machine. The group shut the door and walked away, snow already beginning to cover their tracks.

*Waluigi wants to end on this image specifically, because he thinks it is being underweighted by everyone involved. The Agent has now left a fully repaired, fully functional Legion survey machine — the same one whose corrupted data he manufactured specifically to hide a magical-interference anomaly — sealed in an abandoned building, alone, with the one entity in the entire Underground demonstrably capable of tampering with sensitive Legion equipment undetected. Flowey did not need anyone's help to fix that machine the first time. He does not need anyone's permission to touch it again. The group has, in effect, handed their own evidence, unsupervised, back to the exact person who already tampered with it once as a message. Waluigi does not believe this was Flowey's plan from the start — Waluigi does not yet have grounds to claim Flowey engineered his own capture — but Waluigi notes, for the permanent record, that if Flowey wanted precisely this outcome, alone with the machine again, no witnesses, cage or no cage, the last twenty minutes of this session are exactly what he would have arranged. Waluigi cannot yet say whether that is paranoia or pattern recognition. Waluigi intends to find out before the Agent returns to that police station. WAH.*
